questions.stem: The king of Lagos that ceded territory to the British in 1861 was
questions.explanation: Oba Dosunmu (or Docemo) was the King of Lagos who, under pressure from the British, signed the Treaty of Cession in 1861, which led to Lagos becoming a British colony.

questions.stem: Beyond funding the building of a mosque in the 1890s, what else did Muhammed Shitta Bey, a Muslim Creole, encourage?

options.A: The spread of traditional African religions.
options.D: The migration of Nigerian Muslims to other countries.

questions.explanation: Shitta Bey also encouraged Muslims to acquire Western education, stressing the numerous benefits it offers.

questions.stem: All except of one of the following were widespread in pre-jihad Hausaland

options.A: The practice of pouring libations on rocks
options.C: The practice of venerating trees and rocks

questions.explanation: Before the Fulani Jihad of the early 19th century, traditional Hausa religion, characterized by polytheism and the veneration of natural objects (including pouring libations and venerating trees and rocks), was widespread. Christian missionary activities became significant in Nigeria much later, primarily during the colonial period of the late 19th and 20th centuries, and had minimal presence in pre-jihad Hausaland.

questions.stem: In which Pentecostal organization do women enjoy full ordination and play important administrative roles?
questions.explanation: The text states that 'within some Pentecostal organizations, women enjoy full ordination and play important administrative roles as is the case in the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG).'

questions.stem: What hindered gender solidarity amongst women following independence?
questions.explanation: Study Session 14 states that party, religious, and ethnic allegiances split women into opposing camps, taking precedence over gender solidarity.

questions.stem: The National Youth Service Corp (NYSC) was established in _____.
questions.explanation: The National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) scheme was established in Nigeria on May 22, 1973, during the military regime of General Yakubu Gowon, with the aim of fostering national unity and development.

questions.stem: What is the term used to describe the combination of a society's economic organisation and its corresponding political structure?
questions.explanation: The text mentions: 'The system of economic organisation in any society and the corresponding political structure resting on it constitute a socio-economic formation.'

questions.stem: The initial leader of the Boko Haram was __________
questions.explanation: Muhammed Yusuf was the founder and initial leader of Boko Haram in 2002.

questions.stem: In traditional Igbo society, what was the fate of individuals who died of smallpox, were lunatics, or died in accidents or childbirth?

options.A: They were given elaborate second burials after three months.
options.B: They were thrown into the evil forest or hurriedly buried.
options.C: Their bodies were preserved and displayed to warn others.
options.D: They were buried in their father's compound with special rites.

questions.explanation: The text explicitly mentions: 'You will note that lepers and those who died of small pox were thrown into the evil forest. Those who died of accidents, lunatics or women who died at child birth were hurriedly buried.'

questions.stem: One of the significant limitations of traditional or indigenous education in pre-colonial Nigeria was:

options.A: Its exclusive focus on vocational training, neglecting character development.
options.B: Its inability to equip individuals to fit usefully into their society.
options.C: The absence of writing, leading to reliance on memory and potential loss of knowledge if custodians died.
options.D: The widespread cases of unemployment among trained individuals.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'However, it had its limitations. For example, in the absence of writing, people depended on the power of their memory to retain and transmit all learned ideas to future generations. However, memory could fail, and when a custodian of some useful information or skill died, all was lost.' It also explicitly states: 'There were, however, no cases of unemployment.'

questions.stem: The Nupe women traders during the pre-colonial period were noted for their ________ ?

options.B: Involvement in both local and long distance trade

questions.explanation: Nupe women traders were noted for their involvement in both local and long distance trade.

questions.stem: Which aspects of Nigerian life were greatly shaped by colonialism according to the text?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'Nigeria's political and economic cultures were greatly shaped by colonialism.' However, it also notes that 'every aspect of life' was affected.

questions.stem: Who said, We are quelling a rebellion, not fighting an external enemy ________?
questions.explanation: General Yakubu Gowon made this statement during the Nigerian Civil War, referring to Biafra as a rebellion.

questions.stem: What was the role of Ilorin in the spread of Islam in Yorubaland during the second half of the 19th century?

options.A: It was a center for anti-Islamic movements
options.B: It served as a frontier emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate and a vanguard for Islamic spread
options.D: It was a main trading hub for Christian merchants

questions.explanation: The text states, 'Secondly, you will note that the wars that ravaged Yoruba land during the 19th century and the emergence of Ilorin as a frontier emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate contributed to the rapid spread and growth of Islam. For much of the second half of the century, Ilorin was in the vanguard of the spread of Islam to different parts of Yoruba land.'

questions.stem: ________ wrote The history of the Yoruba from the earliest times
questions.explanation: Rev. Samuel Johnson wrote 'The History of the Yorubas from the Earliest Times to the Beginning of the British Protectorate'.

questions.stem: In Urhobo marriage, when does the bride undergo circumcision, distinguishing it from the Benin system?

options.C: In the seventh month of her first pregnancy.
options.D: Immediately after giving birth to her first child.

questions.explanation: The text explicitly states: 'Unlike the Benin system, the bride in the Urhobo system undergoes circumcision in the seventh month of her first pregnancy.'

questions.stem: According to the text, what characterises relationships in a communal society?
questions.explanation: The text states communal societies encourage 'long lasting social relationships which are mostly personal and intimate,' in contrast to the formal relationships of associational societies.

questions.stem: The judiciary can support the anti-corruption war in Nigeria through all except if _________

options.A: The judiciary is strengthened and reinvigorated

questions.explanation: Study Session 15 states that the judiciary needs to be strengthened and reinvigorated, and judges must be fearless, persistent, and not corrupt to effectively fight corruption. If judges are compromised, the anti-corruption war will fail.

questions.stem: What is the primary way 'new' diaspora Nigerians financially contribute to their homeland's economic development, as mentioned in the text?

options.A: Direct foreign aid to the government
options.C: Remitting money home to family members for construction or business
options.D: Investing in the Nigerian stock market

questions.explanation: Section 10.3 highlights: 'Apart from sharing ideas, almost, if not all Nigerians abroad remit money home to family members for construction or business. Monies sent by Nigerians in diaspora sum up to billions of Naira every year and economic analysts state that such financial stimulus has contributed to Nigeria's economic development, especially in the past three decades.'

questions.stem: What function do the forces and dynamics of civil society, particularly the political class and ruling ideology, serve for the economy?

options.B: They provide the economy with a guiding compass.
options.C: They are irrelevant to economic development.
options.D: They directly control all means of production.

questions.explanation: The document states: 'the forces and dynamics of the civil society, particularly the political class and the ruling ideology, provide the economy with a guiding compass.'

questions.stem: Islam did not contribute to the development of Nigeria through _________
questions.explanation: Islam contributed to Nigerian culture through Arabic language, architecture (like mosques), and the adoption of Islamic modes of dressing. Nepotism is a form of corruption and is not a developmental contribution of Islam.

questions.stem: The Nigerian Export Timber Trade at Koko was established in _______
questions.explanation: The Nigerian export timber trade at Koko was established in 1917 by Miller Brothers.

questions.stem: Which manufacturing industry was considered the most widespread and engaged a large number of people in pre-colonial Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'The cloth industry according to record appeared to be the most widespread and the one which engaged a large number of people in the production of cotton, yarns, threads and dye.'

questions.stem: What are the three fundamental components of every culture according to the text?
questions.explanation: The text explicitly lists 'the technological, the sociological and the ideological' as the three fundamental parts or components of every culture.

questions.stem: Nigeria has reached a situation of ________.

options.A: The budding of the culture of corruption
options.D: The prevalence of the culture of corruption

questions.explanation: The statement implies that corruption in Nigeria is widespread and deeply entrenched, suggesting a systemic issue rather than isolated incidents or just emerging problems.

questions.stem: A dependent economy is a:
questions.explanation: The text clearly states, 'A dependent economy is a disarticulated one. It lacks internal inter-sectoral interdependence and symbiosis.'

questions.stem: Which of these roles was most influential for women in the Benin Kingdom?
questions.explanation: The Queen Mother (like Idia) held significant influence and power in the Benin Kingdom, often playing crucial roles in politics and military affairs.

questions.stem: Why is it fashionable today to describe the world as a 'global village'?

options.A: Because all nations now have the same political system
options.B: Because of the level of interactions that technological breakthroughs have engendered
options.C: Because English has become the universal language
options.D: Because the world population has decreased significantly

questions.explanation: The text states the world is described as a global village 'because of the level of interactions that technological breakthroughs have engendered among different societies in the world.'

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a communal society?

options.A: Large, with complex division of labour and formal relationships
options.B: Typically small, with simple division of labour and limited differentiation of roles
options.C: Characterised by weak group identity and many subgroups
options.D: Modern, urban, and focused on segmental roles

questions.explanation: A communal society is 'typically small, with a simple division of labour and consequently has a limited differentiation of role' and 'long lasting social relationships which are mostly personal and intimate.'

questions.stem: A historical explanation of a city comprises its _______.

options.D: Origins, growth and the interactions of the various groups in time perspectives

questions.explanation: A comprehensive historical explanation of a city involves understanding its origins, how it grew over time, and the dynamic interactions among different groups of people within it through various historical periods. The other options represent components but not the complete historical explanation.

questions.stem: The first shipment of Nigerian crude oil was exported through _______
questions.explanation: The first shipment of crude oil was exported through Port Harcourt in 1958.

questions.stem: How were skills for occupational development primarily acquired in the pre-colonial period?

options.A: Through formal education in established institutions like universities.
options.B: By consulting spirits and goddesses of knowledge.
options.C: Through professionals within the family and community, often by apprenticeship.
options.D: By trial and error, with individuals discovering skills independently.

questions.explanation: The document states, 'In the pre-colonial period, skills for occupational development were acquired through professionals within the family and community. In most cases, boys were brought up to take to their father's occupation. In some other cases, they were sent to live with other men as apprentices to learn various vocations and life etiquette.'

questions.stem: The establishment of Port Harcourt was to facilitate the:
questions.explanation: Port Harcourt was established in 1912 by the British colonial administration primarily to export coal, which was discovered in Enugu. Its development was crucial for transporting the coal from the hinterland to the coast for shipment.

questions.stem: According to the text, what could be a consequence for a married woman in Edo land who commits adultery without confessing?

options.A: She would be exiled from the community.
options.B: It could lead to the death of her children or some serious sickness.
options.C: She would be forced to pay a heavy fine to her husband.
options.D: Her husband would be obligated to divorce her immediately.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'Among the Edo, adultery could lead to the death of children born by the woman or some serious sickness if she does not confess.'

questions.stem: What did the 'intellectual training' for boys in pre-colonial societies primarily involve?

options.A: Learning to read and write complex scripts.
options.B: Sitting with fathers at meetings, learning arbitration, oratory, and proverbs.
options.C: Formal lessons in mathematics and science.
options.D: Competitive examinations for entry into leadership roles.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'Intellectual training for them consisted of their sitting quietly beside their fathers at meetings and listening attentively to learn the intricacies of such tasks and skills as arbitration of cases, oratory (public speaking), wise sayings and use of proverbs.'

questions.stem: The profound socio-cultural western influences on Nigeria include
questions.explanation: Western influences, particularly through missionary activities, profoundly shaped Nigeria by introducing Christianity and Western-style education, which had lasting impacts on the socio-cultural fabric of the nation.

questions.stem: Who was the first female Vice Chancellor of any Nigerian university?
questions.explanation: Professor Grace Alele Williams was the first female Vice Chancellor of any Nigerian university.

questions.stem: Colonial cities had _________
questions.explanation: Colonial cities introduced modern functional facilities like standard roads, electricity, and piped water.

questions.stem: The Nigerian civil war covered ________
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Civil War (also known as the Nigeria-Biafra War) lasted from 1967 to 1970. Study Session 7 mentions the war as lasting from 1967-1970.

questions.stem: According to the text, what gives meaning to the life of an individual in a society?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'Culture is what gives meaning to the life of an individual in a society,' providing the framework for understanding existence.

questions.stem: Who captured the Biafra Radio and announced a takeover by the Nigerian forces?
questions.explanation: Colonel Hassan Katsina captured the Biafra Radio and announced the takeover by Nigerian forces.

questions.stem: Which of these is contained in the marriage culture of the Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Alligator pepper (also called ose in Yoruba) is used in Yoruba marriage rites.

questions.stem: In Fulani marriage traditions, how was the bride's chastity before marriage typically verified on the first night?

options.A: A communal interrogation by the village elders.
options.B: The spreading of a white sheet on the bed to check for bloodstains.
options.C: A ritualistic confession before the groom's parents.
options.D: A test of endurance and strength by the bride.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'You will note that the final test of the Fulani marriage is chastity before marriage. On the first night of the marriage, a white sheet would be spread on the bed. If it is stained with blood, the bride and her family would be highly respected, for that implies that the lady was not defiled before marriage.'

questions.stem: Among some groups in Nigeria, a woman who committed adultery without confessing would not
questions.explanation: In some traditional belief systems, unconfessed adultery by a woman was believed to lead to serious spiritual or physical consequences, including the inability to Be able to bear children, or complications in childbirth.

questions.stem: During colonialism, Enugu was not a/an _________
questions.explanation: Enugu was founded as a commercial and industrial centre due to coal mining, and later served as an administrative seat. It was not a spiritual headquarters.

questions.stem: Who, said, we are quelling a rebellion, not fighting an external enemy _________?
questions.explanation: This statement is attributed to General Yakubu Gowon, who was the Head of State during the Nigerian Civil War (1967-1970). It reflected the Federal Government's perspective that the conflict was an internal affair aimed at suppressing a secessionist rebellion, not a war against an independent foreign entity.

questions.stem: Which area of cultural change is NOT mentioned as a consequence of war in pre-colonial Nigeria?

options.D: Learning new ways of life and languages

questions.explanation: The text mentions forced migration, creation of new towns, enslavement, cultural absorption, and learning new ways. Written constitutions are not mentioned as a consequence of pre-colonial warfare.

questions.stem: What was a key characteristic of the 'Nabo' system compared to 'Aro'?

options.A: Nabo participants were independent, while Aro participants were dependent on parents.
options.B: Nabo involved helping on personal farms, while Aro involved helping on father's farms.
options.C: Nabo participants were younger and dependent on their parents, unlike Aro participants who were independent.
options.D: Nabo was practiced year-round, while Aro was strictly seasonal.

questions.explanation: The text notes: 'Participants in Nabo are younger than those in Aro. The youths are still dependent on their parents or guardian in Nabo, but independent in Aro.' It also states youths worked on their father's farm in Nabo, versus personal farms in Aro.

questions.stem: The monetisation policy promoted by colonialism made giving and receiving of bribes _______
questions.explanation: Monetisation introduced a cash-based economy, making bribery and corruption easier compared to the barter system.

questions.stem: According to traditions, who founded the Itsekiri Kingdom?

options.C: Iginua, a son of the Oba of Benin from the fifteenth century

questions.explanation: The text states: 'Bini and Itsekiri traditions attribute the foundation of Itsekiri Kingdom to Iginua, a son of Oba of Benin who reigned in the fifteenth century.'

questions.stem: Nigerian cultural heritage is ________
questions.explanation: Nigerian cultural heritage, as described in the sessions, is diverse and extensive, including varied marriage rites, naming ceremonies, festivals, and traditions. Therefore, it is considered rich.

questions.stem: According to the text, what is placed over the door where an Efik girl resides during her fattening period to prevent the wicked water spirit Ndem from entering?

options.A: A special charm made by elders.
options.C: A woven mat with protective symbols.

questions.explanation: The text explicitly mentions: 'During this period, fresh palm leaves are tied over the door where the young girl resides to prevent wicked water spirit Ndem from entering.'

questions.stem: Among the Efik of James Town, what is the specific purpose of tying fresh palm leaves over the door where a young girl undergoing fattening resides?

options.A: To indicate that the girl is undergoing a sacred ritual.
options.B: To prevent wicked water spirit Ndem from entering.
options.C: To mark the duration of the fattening period for visitors.
options.D: To signify the girl's passage into womanhood.

questions.explanation: The text explains: 'During this period, fresh palm leaves are tied over the door where the young girl resides to prevent wicked water spirit Ndem from entering.'

questions.stem: What was the name of Bayajjida's son whose six sons established six of the Hausa Bakwai states?
questions.explanation: From Study Session 2, the text states: 'The union produced a son called Bawo, whose six sons established the states of Daura, Katsina, Kano, Rano, Zazzau and Gobir.'

questions.stem: The National Youth Service Corps Scheme was initiated to promote
questions.explanation: The NYSC scheme was primarily established after the Nigerian Civil War to foster unity and integration among Nigerian youths from different ethnic and geographical backgrounds.

questions.stem: Who said, We are quelling a rebellion, not fighting an external enemy?
questions.explanation: This famous statement was made by General Yakubu Gowon during the Nigerian Civil War, to emphasize that the conflict was an internal affair, not a war against another sovereign nation.

questions.stem: Which higher educational institution, established in 1827 and affiliated to Durham University in 1876, became the hub of intellectual activities in West Africa?
questions.explanation: The text states: "They also went a step further by establishing a higher school of their own, the Fourah Bay College that was established in 1827 and affiliated to Durham University in 1876. Fourah Bay became the hub of intellectual activities in West Africa..."

questions.stem: Who said, 'To keep Nigeria one is a task that must be done'?
questions.explanation: During the Nigerian Civil War, General Yakubu Gowon famously declared that 'To keep Nigeria one is a task that must be done.' This was his commitment to maintaining the unity of the country.

questions.stem: What were the four major Efik settlements that became collectively known as Calabar?
questions.explanation: From Study Session 2, the text lists the four major Efik settlements as Obio Oko (Creek Town), Atakpa (Duke Town), Obutong (Old Town), and Nsidung (Henshaw Town).

questions.stem: In Ikot Oku Nsit (Ibibio), how can a man marry from a family if no grown-up girl is available?

options.A: He must wait for a girl to be born
options.B: He draws a circle with white chalk on a pregnant woman's belly; if a girl is born, she is betrothed
options.C: He marries a woman from another family
options.D: He pays double the bride price

questions.explanation: The man draws a circle with white chalk on a pregnant woman's belly; if a baby girl is born, a raffia is tied to her hand, signifying she is chosen as a marriage partner.

questions.stem: A historical explanation of a city comprises its _______

options.D: Origins, growth and the interactions of the various groups in time perspectives

questions.explanation: A historical explanation of a city focuses on its origins, growth, and interactions over time, as noted in the study of urban culture.

questions.stem: During the Idana stage of Yoruba marriage, specific symbolic items are presented. Which of the following correctly pairs an item with its traditional symbolism?

options.A: Ireke (sugar cane) for protection against sickness.
options.B: Ataare (alligator pepper) for happiness in marriage.
options.C: Epo (palm oil) for resilience in marriage.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'The sugar and honey symbolize happiness in marriage; the kola for the couple's protection against sickness; the alligator pepper for them to have many children; and the palm oil for resilience in their marriage.' Therefore, palm oil (epo) for resilience is correct.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes how pre-colonial Nigerian societies addressed the education of their youths?

options.A: Through formal schooling systems imported from Europe.
options.B: By sending them abroad for higher education.
options.C: Through organized systems of apprenticeship and training in traditional occupations.
options.D: By relying solely on oral traditions and storytelling.

questions.explanation: The text mentions: 'The education of their youths was done through organised system of apprenticeship and training in the traditional occupations of farming, fishing, animal husbandry, the crafts, and trade.'

questions.stem: The earliest indication of the presence of Islam in Nigeria was in the ________ area?
questions.explanation: Study Session 6 states that the earliest indication of the presence of Islam in Nigeria was in Borno, which emerged out of the ancient Kanem-Borno Empire. The real process of Islamization began in the 11th century in this area.

questions.stem: According to the text, what animal behaviors were considered signs of abomination or impending death in parts of Igboland (Ngor Okpala or Imo State)?

options.A: A dog barking continuously at night.
options.B: A lion roaring in the village square at night or a wild cat/bat crying behind a sick man's house.
options.D: Birds flying into a house through a window.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'In Ngor Okpala, if a lion came out in the night to roar in the village square, it signified an abomination had been committed. In parts of Imo State, if a wild cat or a bat cried behind the house of a sick man it meant that person would die.'

questions.stem: What does it mean in Benin if someone says 'the Oba has been swallowed by the ground'?

options.A: The Oba has gone on a journey

questions.explanation: Among the Edo people, it is never said that the Oba had died; rather it is said that the Oba has been swallowed by the ground.

questions.stem: According to L.C. Dioka, what twin principles does culture merit?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'According to L.C. Dioka, culture more than anything else merits the twin principles of continuity and change.'

questions.stem: The major religious crisis in Northern Nigeria in the early 1980s was caused by the ________.
questions.explanation: The early 1980s in Northern Nigeria were marked by violent religious disturbances attributed to the Maitatsine sect, led by Mohammed Marwa Maitatsine. These outbreaks, particularly in Kano, involved clashes with security forces and significant loss of life, making it a major religious crisis of that era.

questions.stem: Among the Igbo, what does the name 'Chiemeka' mean?
questions.explanation: Chiemeka (often from 'Chi emeka') means 'God has done well,' reflecting the use of 'chi' (God) in Igbo names.

questions.stem: When crude oil export replaced agriculture in Nigeria, the culture of corruption also
questions.explanation: The shift from an agriculture-based economy to one dominated by crude oil export often led to a rapid influx of wealth, centralized power, and reduced accountability, which contributed to an 'escalation' of the culture of corruption in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which decade is referred to as the United Nations decade for women?
questions.explanation: Study Session 14 states that the Declaration of an International Decade for Women was 1975-1985. This led to debates on women's status and problems worldwide.

questions.stem: At the end of the Nigerian civil war, Gowon extended ________

options.B: The readiness to punish all offenders

questions.explanation: Gowon extended the olive branch with his policy of reconciliation after the war.

questions.stem: Some of the crafts women engaged in all but one of the following _______.
questions.explanation: While weaving, bead-making, and pottery were traditional crafts widely practiced by women in many Nigerian communities, 'banking' as a formal financial institution was not a traditional craft or engagement for women in the pre-colonial or early colonial context.

questions.stem: A historical explanation of a city comprises its ______.

options.D: Origins, growth and the interactions of the various groups in time perspectives

questions.explanation: A comprehensive historical explanation of a city involves understanding its origins, how it grew over time, and the dynamic interactions among different groups within it across various historical periods.

questions.stem: The evidence of earliest human habitation in Nigeria came from the artifacts excavated in ______.
questions.explanation: Archaeological findings at Iwo-Eleru in southwestern Nigeria have provided evidence of some of the earliest human habitation in the region, including ancient skeletal remains.

questions.stem: What was one dominant theme in Hausa history before 1800?

options.B: Recurrent warfare among various states to secure trans-Saharan trade

questions.explanation: The text notes 'one dominant theme in Hausa history in the period before 1800 was the recurrent issues of warfare among the various states' as each sought greater involvement in trans-Saharan trade.

questions.stem: The earliest indication of the presence of Islam in Nigeria was in which region?
questions.explanation: According to the text, 'the earliest indication of the presence of Islam in Nigeria was in Borno, which emerged out of the ancient Kanem–Borno Empire.'

questions.stem: Every production system has a corresponding
questions.explanation: A production system, which dictates how goods and services are created and distributed, is intrinsically linked to and supported by a corresponding political system that establishes laws, governance, and resource allocation.

questions.stem: What does the text identify as both a pre-colonial shaping element AND a dominant modern religion in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Islam is listed as one of the six pre-colonial cultural elements and is described as 'surely one of the two dominant religions practiced in Nigeria today.'

questions.stem: Which of the following were usually buried in the 'evil forest'?
questions.explanation: Study Session 5 states that lepers and those who died of smallpox were thrown into the evil forest. Those who died of accidents or at childbirth were also hurriedly buried.

questions.stem: The Indirect Rule system did not encourage the use of ___
questions.explanation: The British Indirect Rule system in Nigeria utilized existing traditional structures, including Native Treasuries, Native Authorities (emirs, chiefs, and their councils), and Native Courts, to administer local areas. However, it did not encourage the existence or use of independent 'Native Militias'; armed forces were centrally controlled by the colonial power.

questions.stem: During the anti-colonial struggle in Nigeria, which print media was mentioned as being of immense value in mobilising people against colonial rule?
questions.explanation: Section 10.3 mentions: 'In Nigeria, the Lagos Weekly Records published by the Jacksons and the Lagos Observer published by J. Bagan Benjamin were of immense value in mobilising the people against colonial rule and colonial policies.'

questions.stem: According to the text, what was one direct impact of Islam on Nigerian society related to urban development?

options.B: The active involvement in the process of urbanization and establishment of new towns
options.D: The abandonment of all traditional settlements

questions.explanation: The text states, 'We must emphasise that Islam recorded a direct impact on the Nigerian society through its active involvement in the process of urbanization. For example, under the stimulation of the Sokoto Caliphate, many villages were converted to towns and new towns were established as centers of commerce and industry.'

questions.stem: Kanem-Borno is another name for the __________
questions.explanation: Kanem-Borno is another name for the Kanuri Empire. Study Session 2 states that two prominent ethnic groups in the North East Zone are the Kanuri and Jukun, with the Kanuri establishing the state usually referred to as Kanem-Borno.

questions.stem: After the completion of all the marriage rites, the bride is expected to do which of these?
questions.explanation: After completing marriage rites, the bride traditionally goes to her husband's house to begin their life together.

questions.stem: The evidence of earliest human habitation in Nigeria came from the artifacts excavated in ________ ?
questions.explanation: The Nok culture, with artifacts radiocarbon dated to around 39,000 BC, provides the earliest evidence of human habitation in Nigeria.

questions.stem: The need for a new dimension to women's participation in Christianity led to the _________

options.A: Exclusion of male Christians from female-dominated churches
options.B: Overthrow of male bishops by female members of their church
options.C: Overthrow of male pastors by their wives

questions.explanation: Women seeking new dimensions of participation led to the establishment of churches founded by women.

questions.stem: Colonialism freed women from domestic violence by introducing and enforcing some laws at the district and provincial courts under the ___
questions.explanation: Under the system of Indirect Rule, the British colonial administration introduced its own legal frameworks and courts, which sometimes intervened in issues like domestic violence, thereby offering an alternative to traditional justice systems and potentially freeing women from certain forms of abuse.

questions.stem: The Indirect Rule system of administration in Nigeria promoted elements of _______

options.D: British/Western monetary culture and administrative system

questions.explanation: Study Session 15 states that the introduction of Indirect Rule system imposed elements of Western monetary culture and administrative system and abolished the ritual aspects of pre-colonial Nigerian communities.

questions.stem: Who were the purveyors of cultural nationalism in late nineteenth century Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'the purveyors of cultural nationalism in the late nineteenth century were all products of missionary schools.'

questions.stem: Chief Obafemi Awolowo was __________ Minister during the Civil War?
questions.explanation: During the Nigerian Civil War (1967-1970), Chief Obafemi Awolowo served as the Federal Commissioner for Finance and Vice President of the Federal Executive Council under General Yakubu Gowon.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of a communal society?

options.C: Few subgroups other than family and kinship units

questions.explanation: The text states a communal society has 'few subgroups other than family and kinship units' and 'a strong sense of group identity.'

questions.stem: A major contradiction noted in post-independence Nigeria regarding settlement patterns is:

options.A: The planned and equitable distribution of resources between urban and rural areas.
options.B: The decline of existing towns and the emergence of new, isolated settlements.
options.C: Uncontrolled urbanization and the abysmal neglect of rural areas.
options.D: The successful integration of rural economies into urban markets.

questions.explanation: The text highlights: 'Another contradiction of the post-independence Nigeria is between uncontrolled urbanisation and abysmal neglect of rural areas.'

questions.stem: When did secession groups called 'African' or 'Native' Churches begin to emerge in Nigeria?

options.A: First half of the nineteenth century
options.B: Last quarter of the nineteenth century
options.C: First half of the twentieth century
options.D: Last quarter of the twentieth century

questions.explanation: The text states: 'In the last quarter of the nineteenth century, secession groups called 'African' or 'Native' Churches also began to emerge.'

questions.stem: Ajayi Crowther wrote the Grammar and Vocabulary of the Yoruba Language in ______.
questions.explanation: Bishop Samuel Ajayi Crowther, a pioneer in the study and standardization of the Yoruba language, published his 'Vocabulary of the Yoruba Language' in 1843 and a grammar in 1852. The 1843 publication marked a significant step.

questions.stem: According to Study Session 3, how many elements that shaped Nigeria's culture in the pre-colonial era are identified?
questions.explanation: The text explicitly lists six elements: geography, economy, migration, inter-marriage, war, and Islam. Options A, B, and D are incorrect counts.

questions.stem: One of the following does not encourage corruption in Nigeria _______

options.B: Lack of basic necessities of life

questions.explanation: Transparent allocation of resources discourages corruption, while the others encourage it.

questions.stem: Sexual immoralities were enhanced by urbanization in ________
questions.explanation: Study Session 7 states that the unprecedented urbanization that occurred as a result of modern amenities in colonial towns and cities compelled many young men and women to leave the village for urban centers. The urban environment exposed them to liberal and individual values, leading to sexual immoralities such as prostitution, rape and sodomy.

questions.stem: The name Yoruba was first applied to which of the Yoruba sub-groups?
questions.explanation: The Hausa first used the term 'Yoruba' to refer specifically to the Oyo people; it was later adopted by missionaries for other groups.

questions.stem: What was the main purpose behind the colonial administration's emphasis on agricultural development in Nigeria?

options.B: To provide industrial raw materials for factories in Britain.
options.C: To promote diversification of the local economy.
options.D: To empower local farmers with modern techniques.

questions.explanation: The text indicates that the backbone of the colonial economy was agriculture, and 'The focus was simply to provide industrial raw materials for factories and industrial plants.'

questions.stem: According to W. Kornblum, what functions does a society organise cooperatively to carry out?

options.C: Reproduction, sustenance, shelter, defence, and disposal of the dead

questions.explanation: Kornblum sees society as organised to carry out 'the major functions of life, including reproduction, sustenance, shelter, defence and even the disposal of the dead.'

questions.stem: Gender refers to cultural construction of __________
questions.explanation: Gender refers to the cultural construction of male and female characteristics.

questions.stem: Which pollution is directly associated with generator set?
questions.explanation: Generator sets cause air pollution through the emission of exhaust fumes.

questions.stem: Which of these is a method of acquiring citizenship in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Naturalization is the legal process through which a foreigner can acquire Nigerian citizenship.

questions.stem: The establishment of Port Harcourt was to facilitate the
questions.explanation: Port Harcourt was established in 1912 primarily as a port to export coal, which was discovered in commercial quantities in Enugu. The railway line from Enugu to Port Harcourt was constructed for this purpose, making it a crucial hub for the colonial economy.

questions.stem: A major contribution of Christianity to politics in Nigeria was its _________
questions.explanation: Christianity contributed to political development through human rights advocacy, especially during military regimes.

questions.stem: Every production system has a corresponding:
questions.explanation: The document states that 'every production system has a corresponding political system or, more broadly speaking, civil society resting on it.'

questions.stem: The two major anti-corruption agencies in Nigeria are ________.
questions.explanation: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) and the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) are the two primary federal agencies responsible for combating corruption in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Among the Edo, what is the 'Ugbo Ogba' or 'strong foot'?

options.A: A dance performed at the wedding
options.B: A special present given to persuade a reluctant bride's father or brother
options.D: The final payment before the bride goes to her husband

questions.explanation: If a girl refuses marriage, Ugbo Ogba is a special present given to her father or brother to persuade her to go through with the process.

questions.stem: Chief Obafemi Awolowo was ________ Minister during the Civil War?
questions.explanation: Chief Obafemi Awolowo was the Federal Commissioner (Minister) of Finance during the Civil War.

questions.stem: A dependent economy is A ____
questions.explanation: A dependent economy is often characterized by a 'disarticulated' structure, meaning its various sectors are not well integrated or balanced internally, but rather oriented towards external markets and needs of a dominant external economy.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what has often been the basis for discrimination between and among cultures?

options.B: Differences in skin colour and physical appearance
options.C: Difference in the advancement of the technological component

questions.explanation: The text notes: 'the difference in the advancement of the technological component of the different cultures of the world has often been the basis for discrimination between and among cultures.'

questions.stem: Of all the Baptist missionaries that worked in Ogbomoso, Reverend C. E. Smith had greater and lasting influence on
questions.explanation: Reverend C. E. Smith was a significant Baptist missionary in Ogbomoso. His influence was particularly profound on Nathaniel David Oyerinde, who became a prominent Nigerian Baptist leader, educationist, and historian, often considered a protégé of Smith.

questions.stem: The fight against corruption in Nigeria has not been worsened by
questions.explanation: Spiritual forces are not a factor in corruption; tribalism, greed, and ethnicity are.

questions.stem: The first-half of the 20th century witnessed the following African Churches except the _________
questions.explanation: Charismatic Renewals World (CRW) is a more recent Pentecostal church, not from the first half of the 20th century.

questions.stem: One major economic effect of corruption is _______
questions.explanation: Corruption leads to the embezzlement and diversion of public funds, depleting the national treasury and hindering development.

questions.stem: In pre-colonial Nigerian societies, what was identified as a major source of manpower for productive exercises?

options.B: The family unit, especially women with many children.
options.D: Captives acquired through warfare and raids.

questions.explanation: The text states: "The family unit was a major source of manpower in virtually every facet of productive exercise. Labour was mostly supplied by women, especially those who had been privileged to have many children."

questions.stem: The first Executive President of Nigeria was ________?
questions.explanation: Alhaji Shehu Shagari was the first Executive President of Nigeria under the 1979 constitution.

questions.stem: The Nigerian Head of State who organised FESTAC was ________ ?
questions.explanation: General Olusegun Obasanjo organized FESTAC '77 (Festival of Arts and Culture) in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Beyond being a personal affair, what major national problem has religion become in Nigeria?

options.B: A threat to national stability and survival

questions.explanation: The text asserts, 'Although religion is presumed to be a personal affair, it has become a major problem threatening the stability and survival of the nation.'

questions.stem: Which section of the Nigerian Constitution recognizes a Sharia Court of Appeal as a compromise during the Sharia imbroglio?
questions.explanation: The document mentions, 'a sort of compromise was reached with the Muslims having Section 275 which recognizes a Sharia Court of Appeal'.

questions.stem: In associational society, what happens to the pervasive role of tradition?

options.A: It strengthens and becomes more important
options.C: It remains unchanged from communal societies
options.D: It becomes the only source of law

questions.explanation: The text states: 'the pervasive role of tradition is broken' in associational society, allowing more individual choice and formal, codified rules.

questions.stem: Seclusion in purdah may ______
questions.explanation: Study Session 14 states that some women suffer the curtailment of their personal freedom because they are secluded in purdah. Purdah is a practice that restricts women's mobility and participation in public life.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly defines the 'forces of production' in the pre-colonial context, as described in the text?

options.A: The combination of land and capital.
options.B: The combination of the means of production and labour input.
options.C: The total output of goods and services in a society.
options.D: The collective effort of the community in agricultural activities.

questions.explanation: The text states: "The combination of the means of production and labour input constitutes the forces of production."

questions.stem: Colonialism freed women from domestic violence by introducing and enforcing some laws at the district and provincial courts under the __________
questions.explanation: Colonialism introduced laws under Indirect Rule that helped free women from domestic violence.

questions.stem: In principle, the British Indirect Rule system in Nigeria favoured ________
questions.explanation: Indirect Rule allowed local traditional rulers to maintain autonomy under British supervision.

questions.stem: What did Pentecostals accuse some mainstream clergy of being affiliated with?

options.B: Freemasons and local esoteric cults like the Ogboni Confraternity

questions.explanation: The text states that 'the fact that few of the clergy in these mainstream churches were said to be Freemasons and, or affiliated with local esoteric cults (such as the Yoruba Ogboni Confraternity) did not help matters.'

questions.stem: _______ was regarded as the Amirul Mumineen (leader of the faithful) in Kanem-Borno in the 16th century?
questions.explanation: Study Session 6 states that Mai Idris Alooma (1570-1602) was widely acknowledged as the Amirul Mumineen (leader of the faithful) in Kanem-Borno.

questions.stem: Which European traders first attempted to introduce Christianity to southern Nigeria in the late fifteenth century?
questions.explanation: The text states that Catholic Portuguese traders attempted to introduce Christianity to the southern parts of what later became Nigeria from the late fifteenth century up till the seventeenth century.

questions.stem: Which state governor first introduced the Sharia Penal Code in 1999, according to the document?

options.B: Ahmed Sanni Yerima of Zamfara State

questions.explanation: The text explicitly states: 'the first major and decisive step was taken in 1999, when the then Executive Governor of Zamfara State, Ahmed Sanni Yerima, introduced the Sharia Penal Code.'

questions.stem: Amongst the Ibibio, the death of a child was ascribed to ________.
questions.explanation: In some traditional Ibibio beliefs, unexplained or untimely deaths, especially of children, were often attributed to malevolent spiritual forces, such as witchcraft, rather than natural causes or simple misfortune.

questions.stem: How does culture differ from biological inheritance according to the text?

options.A: Culture is inherited biologically while behaviour is learned
options.B: Culture is not inherited biologically but learned in society
options.C: Both culture and biological traits are learned from parents
options.D: Culture is inherited only through maternal lineage

questions.explanation: The text states culture 'is not inherited biologically but learned in any given society or community.' This is a fundamental distinction the author emphasises.

questions.stem: What 'internal Pentecostalization' have mainstream churches embraced in recent times?

options.B: Changes in music and dance during worship

questions.explanation: The text states that mainstream churches have embraced 'internal Pentecostalization... in the area of music and dance during worship, probably to keep their youth from leaving the church.'

questions.stem: Which distinct marriage practice, uncommon in other Nigerian communities mentioned in the text, is observed among the Tiv?

options.A: Payment of bride price in livestock only.
options.B: Marriage by capture is the primary method.
options.C: Bride exchange, where families with grown-up daughters and sons could exchange them in marriage.
options.D: Negotiation of bride price using broom sticks, where the payment is never completed at once.

questions.explanation: The text mentions: 'You will also note that there is also bride exchange among the Tiv, which is not practiced among other Nigerian communities. Families with grown up daughters and sons could exchange their daughters in marriage.' While broomsticks for bride price is also mentioned for Tiv, bride exchange is explicitly stated as 'not practiced among other Nigerian communities'.

questions.stem: In Hausaland, the people most often relegated to the harvesting of agricultural crops were __________
questions.explanation: Study Session 11 states that in the Hausa states, the peoples most often relegated to the tending and harvesting of agricultural crops were captives.

questions.stem: Among the Urhobo, after traditional marriage, where is the bride taken for spiritual blessing?

options.B: To the ancestral shrines of both families

questions.explanation: The girl's family takes her to her ancestral shrines for blessing and to cut ancestral links, then at her husband's house, she is taken to his ancestral shrine for blessing and guidance.

questions.stem: Besides medical and healthcare, banking, engineering, and academia, in what other occupations are Nigerians abroad noted to be prominent, according to the text?

options.B: Police, cab drivers, and operation of small businesses
options.C: Professional sports, music, and film production

questions.explanation: Page 3 states: "Nigerians are also prominent in several other occupations, such as the police, cab drivers as well as the operation of small businesses."

questions.stem: What was the primary economic system in pre-colonial Nigerian society, as described in the text?

options.A: A capitalist system focused on profit-making.
options.B: A communal economic system aimed at widening social relationships.
options.C: A feudal system based on land ownership and tenancy.
options.D: A mercantilist system centered on trade and exports.

questions.explanation: The document notes: "You must bear in mind, that pre-colonial Nigerian society was based on a communal economic system. Economic activities were carried out with the intention of widening social relationships, rather than making money."

questions.stem: 20th century indigenous Pentecostal Churches in Nigeria included all except the ________.
questions.explanation: The Christian Missionary Society (CMS) was a much older, primarily Anglican-based missionary organization, largely foreign-founded, and predates the emergence of what are specifically termed '20th-century indigenous Pentecostal churches' in Nigeria. The others are indeed indigenous Pentecostal or Evangelical movements of the 20th century.

questions.stem: What occupation did coastal area inhabitants in pre-colonial Nigeria typically engage in?
questions.explanation: The text states that 'occupants of coastal areas often emerged as fishermen, engaged in canoe making and consumed mostly fish.'

questions.stem: Among the Tiv, what specific items would a husband send to his wife's family to indicate that she was not a virgin at the time of marriage?

options.A: A broken pot or a piece of torn cloth.
options.B: A small block of moulded salt with a hole in it, or a piece of cloth with a hole at the center.
options.C: A feather from a vulture or a piece of charcoal.
options.D: A calabash filled with bitter herbs or an empty basket.

questions.explanation: The text details: 'If a girl is not found to be a virgin at the time of marriage, the husband would send a special message to her family. He would buy a small block of moulded salt, make a hole in it and send it to the family of the girl or he could use a piece of cloth and cut a hole at the centre and send it to the family of the girl.'

questions.stem: Before the 1930s, one of the following was not an urban centre.
questions.explanation: Abuja was developed much later as Nigeria's capital city, officially becoming the capital in 1991. Before the 1930s, Enugu, Lagos, and Calabar were already significant urban centers due to colonial administration, trade, and resource exploitation.

questions.stem: What was the main difference between Aro and Nabo group farming methods?

options.A: Aro involved relatives, while Nabo involved age-mates.
options.B: Aro involved working on personal farms, while Nabo involved working on fathers' farms.
options.C: Participants in Aro were younger and dependent, while Nabo participants were independent.
options.D: Aro was seasonal, while Nabo was continuous.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'The difference is that youths worked on their father's farm in Nabo, rather than on their personal farms in Aro. Participants in Nabo are younger than those in Aro. The youths are still dependent on their parents or guardian in Nabo, but independent in Aro.' Option B captures the core distinction in where the labor was applied, and implicitly the independence of the participants.

questions.stem: The following were some of the outspoken women leaders during colonial rule except ________
questions.explanation: Efunsetan Aniwura was a pre-colonial Iyalode of Ibadan, not a colonial-era women's leader.

questions.stem: Muhammed Shitta Bey, a Muslim Creole, made a significant contribution to the Islamic community in Lagos during the 1890s. What was this contribution?

options.A: He established the first Islamic school in Lagos.
options.B: He founded the first Islamic bank in Nigeria.
options.C: He donated 400 pounds for the building of a mosque in Lagos.
options.D: He translated the Quran into Yoruba.

questions.explanation: Page 7 states: "Prominent among these was Muhammed Shitta Bey, a Muslim Creole who gave a whopping 400 pounds for the building of a mosque in Lagos in the 1890s."

questions.stem: What was the ruling dynasty of Kanem-Borno from the eleventh century called?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'Its ruling dynasty from the eleventh century was referred to as the Saifawa because it claimed descent from a legendary figure called Saif.'

questions.stem: Before the 1930s, one of the following was not an urban centre ________.
questions.explanation: Abuja was developed much later as Nigeria's capital city, with its construction beginning in the 1980s. Calabar, Lagos, and Enugu were all significant urban centers with colonial origins or substantial pre-colonial importance by the 1930s.

questions.stem: In a communal society, what type of roles do members typically perform?
questions.explanation: The text states that members of a communal society 'perform inclusive rather than segmental role' and 'necessarily interact with one another in a variety of contexts.'

questions.stem: Which architectural style, prominent in Central Lagos from the late nineteenth century, was introduced by African returnees from Brazil?
questions.explanation: The document states: 'They introduced Brazilian-style architecture which became prominent in Central Lagos from the late nineteenth century onwards.' (Page 4)

questions.stem: In pre-colonial Nigeria, what primarily determined the production engagements of different areas and groups?

options.A: The demands of external trade partners.
options.C: The policies set by a central government.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'The production engagements of the different areas and groups were dictated by their natural environments and geography.'

questions.stem: One effect of corruption in Nigeria is _______
questions.explanation: Corruption leads to election rigging and undermines democratic processes.

questions.stem: The Itsekiri oral tradition credits the founding of the kingdom to ________?
questions.explanation: Itsekiri tradition attributes the founding of their kingdom to Iginua, a son of the Oba of Benin.

questions.stem: Trade associations are also known as?
questions.explanation: Study Session 7 states that both men and women formed trade associations known as guilds, that enforced trade rules, regulations, disciplines and price controls.

questions.stem: What is the major difference between inclusive roles and segmental roles?

options.A: Inclusive roles are paid while segmental roles are voluntary
options.B: Inclusive roles span multiple contexts of interaction while segmental roles are specific and unrelated
options.C: Inclusive roles are only for leaders while segmental roles are for common people
options.D: Inclusive roles are modern while segmental roles are traditional

questions.explanation: In communal societies with inclusive roles, people interact across many contexts. In associational societies with segmental roles, people play 'many different and frequently unrelated roles' in separate contexts.

questions.stem: One of the major umbrella Christian organisations in Nigeria is the:
questions.explanation: The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) is indeed the largest and most recognized ecumenical body that represents Christians in Nigeria. It comprises various Christian denominations and serves as their united voice on national issues.

questions.stem: Who was the Vice-Chairman to Gowon in the Federal Executive Council (FEC) of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Chief Obafemi Awolowo served as the Vice-Chairman of the Federal Executive Council under General Yakubu Gowon. He was also the Federal Commissioner for Finance.

questions.stem: Early 20th century foreign Pentecostal Churches in Nigeria included all except the _________
questions.explanation: The Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG) is an indigenous Nigerian church, not a foreign one.

questions.stem: What does the African Church phenomenon underscore about any societal experiment?

options.C: The enduring relevance of indigenous components

questions.explanation: The text states that the African Church phenomenon 'underscores the enduring relevance of indigenous components in any societal experiment, be it political, economic, social or religious.'

questions.stem: What was the most important economic activity in pre-colonial Nigerian kingdoms and empires?

options.A: Mining gold and other precious metals.
options.B: Extensive international trade through established routes.
options.C: Agriculture, employing a large number of people.

questions.explanation: The document states, 'Agriculture was an important economic activity in the pre-colonial kingdom and empires. Although, there a number of other productive sectors, agriculture employed a large number of people.'

questions.stem: The colonial administration showed outright hostility towards industrialization primarily because:

options.A: The local population lacked the skills for industrial work.
options.B: Industrialization would compete with British industries and reduce demand for their products.
options.C: It was too expensive to set up industries in the colony.
options.D: The colonial government prioritized agricultural development exclusively.

questions.explanation: The text explains that industrialization would have 'defeated the basic aims of conquest and colonisation' by making raw materials unavailable for export to Britain and by producing substitutes for imported industrial products, thus competing with British industries.

questions.stem: Which society type is exemplified by the modern metropolis according to the text?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'Associational society, on the other hand, is exemplified by the modern metropolis.'

questions.stem: What process guarantees the transmission of culture to every individual born into a society?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'Socialisation is what guarantees the transmission of culture to every individual born into a society through learning and sharing.' The ITQ in the document also confirms this answer.

questions.stem: In the pre-colonial period, the growth of Kano was influenced by its status as a _________
questions.explanation: Kano grew as a major commercial centre in pre-colonial times, benefiting from its location on trans-Saharan trade routes. Study Session 2 discusses Kano as a leading Hausa state involved in trade.

questions.stem: The profound socio-cultural western influences on Nigeria include ________
questions.explanation: Religion (Christianity) and education (Western schooling) are profound socio-cultural Western influences.

questions.stem: Which of the following geo-political zones in Nigeria may have the least number of ethnic groups?
questions.explanation: The South-east zone is predominantly Igbo and has the least number of ethnic groups.

questions.stem: The concept of "the Bible and the Plough" was adopted by the Christian missions to promote ________

options.B: Training of artisans to produce farm tools
options.C: Production of enough ploughs for farming

questions.explanation: The concept promoted both agriculture (plough) and Christianity (Bible).

questions.stem: Which of the following was NOT a type of road category developed by the colonial administration in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The text lists three categories of roads: 'There were three categories of roads, namely, Trunk A, Trunk B and Minor roads.' Expressway roads are not mentioned.

questions.stem: Among some groups in Nigeria, a woman who commited adultery without confessing would not
questions.explanation: In certain traditional Nigerian belief systems, unconfessed adultery by a woman was believed to lead to complications in childbirth or the inability to bear children, often referred to as 'abiku' or other spiritual afflictions affecting reproductive health.

questions.stem: What are the four major Efik settlements that came to be collectively called Calabar?

options.C: Duke Town, Old Town, Creek Town, Henshaw Town

questions.explanation: The text states: 'The four major Efik settlements of Obio Oko (Creek Town), Atakpa (Duke Town), Obutong (Old Town) and Nsidung (Henshaw Town) came to be collectively called Calabar.'

questions.stem: How did the 'Owe' (working bee) method of group farming differ from 'Aro' in pre-colonial Yoruba societies?

options.A: Owe involved rotational labour exchange, while Aro did not.
options.B: Owe was practiced among relatives and in-laws to help a needy member, without rotational exchange.
options.C: Owe participants were younger and worked on their fathers' farms, unlike Aro.
options.D: Owe required monetary payment for participants, while Aro was based on feeding.

questions.explanation: The document states: "Owe (working bee) is the last of the group farming methods. This is practiced among relatives and in-laws. The object is to come together to help a needy member. There was no rotational labour exchange. It was simply giving a helping hand."

questions.stem: What did colonial expansion of western education enable some Nigerians to do?

options.A: Remain completely isolated from Western influence
options.B: Become educated, imbibe western mode of dressing, and new marital traditions

questions.explanation: The text states: 'Some Nigerians became educated, imbibed the western mode of dressing and even imbibed new marital traditions.'

questions.stem: Among some groups in Nigeria, a woman who committed adultery without confessing would not________?
questions.explanation: In some traditional beliefs, adultery without confession was thought to prevent a woman from bearing children.

questions.stem: Which states make up the North Central Zone?

options.A: Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Ondo, Osun, Ekiti
options.B: Edo, Delta, Bayelsa, Rivers, Cross River, Akwa Ibom
options.D: Kwara, Benue, Plateau, Niger, Nasarawa, Kogi

questions.explanation: The text lists Kwara, Benue, Plateau, Niger, Nasarawa, and Kogi States as comprising the North Central Zone, with Abuja also situated within the zone.

questions.stem: What does the text identify as characteristic of associational society's view of life?

options.A: Life has a strong collective character
options.C: Life is entirely determined by family
options.D: Life is focused only on religious matters

questions.explanation: The text states: 'Here, life has no collective character' in associational society, meaning individuals pursue their own goals without the strong group identity found in communal societies.

questions.stem: A major social effect of corruption is that it has not become an/a _________
questions.explanation: Corruption is an irritant, curse, and bane, but it is NOT a catalyst for growth; it hinders development.

questions.stem: The bride exchange phenomenon is common among which group? The
questions.explanation: Bride exchange, also known as 'sister exchange' or 'sara', was a traditional marriage practice among the Tiv people of central Nigeria.

questions.stem: According to Uche Nworah's comment in 2005, what is the 'only problem' for the generation of Nigerians born in new lands regarding their cultural identity?

options.A: They struggle to learn their native languages.
options.B: They are torn with the issue of double identity.
options.C: They completely reject Nigerian names and attire.
options.D: They refuse to set up community associations.

questions.explanation: Nigerians still maintain and promote their culture in their new countries of residence... the only problem is with the generation born in the new lands, who are torn with the issue of double identity.

questions.stem: Patriarchal structures do not hinder the elevation of women in the _________
questions.explanation: Study Session 4 states that within the African Indigenous Churches (AICs), patriarchal structures that had hitherto prevented women from playing leadership roles are gradually being de-emphasised. Women were ordained as clergy in the Church of the Lord, Aladura, recognized as prophetesses in C&S and CCC congregations, and as Lady Evangelists in CAC Churches.

questions.stem: The death of the old is often considered?
questions.explanation: The death of the old is often considered a 'good passage' as they have lived a full life.

questions.stem: The 'new' diaspora, particularly Nigerians in the West, are noted to constitute a high percentage of professionals in which of the following fields?

options.C: Medical and health care, banking, engineering, and academia

questions.explanation: Page 3 notes: "...Nigerians constitute a high percent of medical and health care workers, bankers, engineers and academics in the West, especially in the United States of America and the United Kingdom."

questions.stem: All except one of the following were widespread in pre-jihad Hausaland:

options.A: The practice of pouring libations on rocks
options.C: The practice of venerating trees and rocks

questions.explanation: Pre-jihad Hausaland, while predominantly Muslim, also featured various animistic and polytheistic practices, including the veneration of natural objects like trees and rocks and the pouring of libations. Christian missionary activities, however, became widespread much later during the colonial era, long after the Sokoto Jihad.

questions.stem: When was the city of Port Harcourt established?
questions.explanation: Study Session 13 states that Port Harcourt was formed in 1912 to facilitate the export of coal from the collieries discovered in Enugu in 1909.

questions.stem: Most traditional laws are not ________ to widows
questions.explanation: Most traditional laws are not favourable to widows.

questions.stem: In the pre-colonial times, several Nigerian communities comprised
questions.explanation: Prior to extensive colonial influence and modernization, most Nigerian communities were largely agrarian and self-sufficient, relying on local resources and production to meet their needs. While some large cities existed, the predominant model was self-sufficient traditional communities.

questions.stem: One of these is not a social cankerworm
questions.explanation: Nepotism, bribery, and corruption are all considered social cankerworms because they are detrimental practices that erode societal fairness, trust, and development. Egalitarianism, on the other hand, is the principle that all people are equal and deserve equal rights and opportunities, which is a positive societal value.

questions.stem: According to the document, what is the universal view of incest across all Nigerian communities mentioned?

options.A: It is considered a minor transgression that can be atoned for with a simple fine.
options.B: It is a great sacrilege, with different methods used to discourage it.
options.C: It is only an abomination if it results in offspring.
options.D: It is tolerated in certain circumstances, particularly within royal families.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'You will note that in all Nigerian communities, incest is a great sacrilege and different methods are used to deal with the offender so as to discourage the crime.'

questions.stem: Which of the following was NOT one of the three categories of roads developed by the colonial administration?
questions.explanation: The text specifies: 'There were three categories of roads, namely, Trunk A, Trunk B and Minor roads.' 'Local roads' is not listed as a distinct category.

questions.stem: What is the simple meaning of 'Boko Haram' in the Hausa language, as explained in the document?
questions.explanation: The document clarifies: '‘Boko Haram’ in Hausa language simply means ‘Western education is forbidden.’'

questions.stem: The first set of African liberated slaves to return home to West Africa from England in 1787 settled in which territory?
questions.explanation: The text mentions: "The first set of African liberated slaves to return home to West Africa came from England in 1787. They settled in Freetown in the territory that was later named Sierra Leone."

questions.stem: Nigerian cultural heritage is ________.
questions.explanation: The document states 'Q66. Nigerian cultural heritage is A. Rich ✓'. Nigerian culture is indeed rich and diverse, encompassing various ethnic groups, traditions, languages, and artistic expressions.

questions.stem: Which specific administrative body was established between 1910 and 1912 to oversee agricultural development in colonial Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'The Department of Agriculture was established from 1910 to 1912 to oversee agricultural development.'

questions.stem: Hausaland experienced the wave of Islamization during the reign of _______
questions.explanation: Sarki Yaji of Kano (1349-1385) was a key figure in the early wave of Islamization in Hausaland, as recorded in the Kano Chronicle.

questions.stem: Among the Yoruba, what was the primary distinguishing factor between the 'Aro' and 'Nabo' group farming methods?

options.A: Aro involved monetary payment, while Nabo did not.
options.B: Aro was for helping needy relatives, while Nabo was a rotational exchange.
options.C: Aro participants were independent and worked on personal farms, while Nabo participants were younger, dependent, and worked on fathers' farms.
options.D: Aro was seasonal with feasting, while Nabo was a year-round system.

questions.explanation: The text explains: 'The difference is that youths worked on their father's farm in Nabo, rather than on their personal farms in Aro. Participants in Nabo are younger than those in Aro. The youths are still dependent on their parents or guardian in Nabo, but independent in Aro.'

questions.stem: Paternalism was associated with the ________
questions.explanation: Paternalism (the belief that the colonizers knew what was best for Africans) was associated with the British.

questions.stem: What happened to cultures when one group conquered another in pre-colonial Nigeria?

options.B: Cultures were absorbed by more dominant ones

questions.explanation: The text states: 'Under such circumstances, cultures were absorbed by more dominant ones and people learned new ways of life and languages.'

questions.stem: All of the following are examples of 20th-century indigenous Pentecostal Churches in Nigeria, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The Christian Missionary Society (CMS) was a British-based Anglican missionary society founded in the late 18th century, playing a key role in introducing Christianity to Nigeria during the colonial period. It is not an indigenous Pentecostal church. The Redeemed Christian Church of God, Deeper Life Christian Ministry, and Church of God Missions are examples of prominent indigenous Pentecostal and Evangelical denominations that emerged and grew in Nigeria in the 20th century.

questions.stem: The General Babangida Administration did a lot to foster _____.

options.A: The intimidation and oppression of the Nigerian women
options.B: The exclusion women from political and economic affairs
options.C: The prosecution of feminists and womanist organization in Nigeria
options.D: The rights and image of Nigerian women

questions.explanation: The Babangida administration initiated several policies and programs, including the establishment of the National Commission for Women (which later became the Ministry of Women Affairs), aimed at improving the status, rights, and public image of Nigerian women.

questions.stem: What was the council of state in the Oyo Kingdom called?
questions.explanation: From Study Session 2, the text states: 'In the Oyo kingdom, the members of the council of state were called Oyo Mesi which was headed by the Bashorun.'

questions.stem: What tradition of Christianity contributed to politics in Nigeria through social activism and critique of bad governance?

options.C: Tradition of socio-political activism, human rights advocacy, and critique of social ills

questions.explanation: The text states: 'Another contribution of Christianity to politics in Nigeria is its tradition of socio-political activism, human rights advocacy and critique of social ills such as bad governance and corruption.'

questions.stem: Which Yoruba name is traditionally given to a child born during festivities?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'For instance, a child born during festivities will be named Abiodun'.

questions.stem: The railway lines developed by the colonial administration primarily ran in which direction across Nigeria?

options.B: North-South, connecting the coast to the northernmost end.
options.C: In a circular pattern around major agricultural regions.
options.D: South-East, linking mining areas to ports.

questions.explanation: The text describes: 'There were two lines. The western line from Iddo, Lagos to Kaura Namoda... The eastern line from Port Harcourt to Nguru... The western and eastern lines run from the coast to the northernmost end of the country...'

questions.stem: Patriarchal structures do not hinder the elevation of women in the:
questions.explanation: African Indigenous Churches (AICs) often provide more opportunities for women's leadership and spiritual roles, sometimes even allowing women to be founders or heads, in contrast to some older or more conservative mainstream denominations where patriarchal structures might be more pronounced.

questions.stem: What is the approximate number of Nigerians Dahitler estimated to be living abroad, including those with one Nigerian parent, on 28 July 2006?
questions.explanation: The text quotes Dahitler: "I would estimate at least 20 million. This figure includes those that have one Nigerian parent."

questions.stem: The creation of states in Nigeria would help to address the fear of ________
questions.explanation: The creation of states in Nigeria has historically been a response to ethnic minorities' fear of domination by larger ethnic groups. State creation was seen as a way to address these fears.

questions.stem: The transfer of ownership rights from the oil hosting communities to the federal government has deprived the communities of:

options.A: Land and water for production of goods and services.
options.B: Abled man power for economic development.
options.C: The fiscal revenue accruing from oil production.
options.D: Judicious spending of the oil wealth.

questions.explanation: The document states, 'The transfer of ownership rights from the oil hosting communities to the federal government has deprived the communities of the fiscal revenue accruing from oil production.'

questions.stem: While men dominated Christian services in various churches and denominations,

options.C: Young men managed the affairs of the house
options.D: Women played key roles in the traditional religion

questions.explanation: The question implies a contrast. While men might have dominated formal Christian services in colonial and post-colonial Nigeria, women often held significant influence and played crucial roles in traditional religious practices and beliefs, highlighting a different sphere of spiritual power and social agency.

questions.stem: The major motive of European colonial presence in the Nigerian area was ________
questions.explanation: The primary motive was economic exploitation, including obtaining raw materials and establishing markets for European goods.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a major feature of the technological component of culture?

options.A: It is intangible and exists only in beliefs
options.B: It is tangible, meaning it can be seen and touched
options.C: It is based solely on oral traditions
options.D: It cannot be diffused between cultures

questions.explanation: The text explicitly states: 'A major feature of this technological component of culture is that it is tangible. This means that it can be seen and touched.'

questions.stem: Modern functional facilities in a city should not include _______
questions.explanation: Modern cities should have standard infrastructure; unprotected ravines are hazards and not considered modern facilities.

questions.stem: Which states make up the South West Zone of Nigeria?

options.A: Sokoto, Kebbi, Zamfara, Katsina, Kaduna, Kano, Jigawa
options.B: Gombe, Bauchi, Yobe, Borno, Taraba, Adamawa
options.C: Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Ondo, Osun, Ekiti

questions.explanation: The text lists Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Ondo, Osun, and Ekiti States as comprising the South West Zone.

questions.stem: In some Edo communities, what happens to the new wife at conception?

options.A: She moves to her husband's ancestral shrine
options.B: She is sent back to her family and remains there until delivery
