questions.explanation: The document states: 'You will note that the Northern political class used the Sharia issue as a smokescreen to divert attention from their weakness and ineptitude.'

questions.stem: What is a major distinguishing feature of marriage among the Akoko Edo, compared to the Yoruba, when the girl or her parents do not agree to the union?

options.A: The marriage is simply called off without further action.
options.B: The girl's family must pay a fine to the suitor.
options.C: The girl could be abducted by the intending groom.
options.D: The suitor must find another mediating agent.

questions.explanation: The text highlights: 'In the case of the Akoko Edo, the situation is different. If the parent of the girl do not agree, the girl could be abducted by the intending groom.'

questions.stem: Why did the British initially have the erroneous impression that Igboland was under Aro political domination?

options.A: Because the Aro had a large army
options.B: Because the Aro controlled the Arochukwu oracle, giving them economic and political influence
options.C: Because the Aro had conquered all Igbo villages militarily
options.D: Because the Aro were appointed by the British

questions.explanation: The text states: 'the economic and political influence enjoyed by the Aro over Igboland during the precolonial period owed largely to their control of the oracle. It was this pre-eminence which at the beginning of colonial rule led the British to the erroneous impression that Igboland was under the political domination of the Aro.'

questions.stem: What does the prefix 'Nwa' mean in Igbo names, and what often follows it?

options.A: Nwa means 'father' and is followed by the season
options.B: Nwa means 'son or child' and is often followed by the market day
options.C: Nwa means 'wealth' and is followed by the village name
options.D: Nwa means 'god' and is followed by a prayer

questions.explanation: Nwa means son or child and is often followed by a market day (e.g., Nwaeke, Nwaafor) depending on when the child was born.

questions.stem: When did Nigerians first witness a major religious revolt by the sect known as Boko Haram, as described in the text?
questions.explanation: The text notes: 'You will observe that Nigerians woke up to a major religious revolt in July 2009, when a sect known as Boko Haram went on rampage in Bauchi.'

questions.stem: What type of animals did savannah area inhabitants typically rear according to the text?
questions.explanation: The text states that savannah inhabitants 'reared domesticated animals such as cattle, chickens.'

questions.stem: The pre-colonial insurance institutions like 'Apo Ijo', 'Otu', Esusu, and Aro aimed to:

options.C: Emphasize mutual responsibilities and alleviate poverty.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'There were diverse insurance institutions in pre-colonial Nigerian communities which emphasized mutual responsibilities and obligations while expressing a desire to alleviate poverty rather than indemnify.' They also functioned as 'credit and social security organisations'.

questions.stem: Beyond Ajayi Crowther's 'Grammar and Vocabulary of the Yoruba Language', which other significant historical work on Yoruba culture was produced by a Creole in 1897?
questions.explanation: The text mentions: "Ajayi Crowther wrote the Grammar and Vocabulary of the Yoruba Language in 1843 and Samuel Johnson wrote his famous History of the Yorubas in 1897..."

questions.stem: The remittances sent home by Nigerians in diaspora are noted to sum up to billions of Naira every year. What economic impact do analysts attribute to this financial stimulus?

options.A: It has led to a decrease in Nigeria's foreign reserves.
options.B: It has primarily funded luxurious lifestyles for family members.
options.C: It has contributed significantly to Nigeria's economic development.
options.D: It has caused an increase in Nigeria's external debt.

questions.explanation: Monies sent by Nigerians in diaspora sum up to billions of Naira every year and economic analysts state that such financial stimulus has contributed to Nigeria's economic development, especially in the past three decades.

questions.stem: There is no single definition of corruption because _______

options.A: The concept varies from one society to another

questions.explanation: Corruption is defined differently across societies due to cultural and contextual differences.

questions.stem: The 'Iwe Irohin' was published by?
questions.explanation: The 'Iwe Irohin' was Nigeria's first newspaper, published by the Church Missionary Society (CMS) in Abeokuta in 1859. This was a significant development in the spread of literacy and journalism.

questions.stem: What was one of the two essential features of Islam mentioned as crucial for understanding its influence on the Hausa community?

options.B: The degree to which Islam permeates other institutions in society
options.C: Its strict prohibition of all non-Islamic trade
options.D: Its isolation from the wider Islamic world

questions.explanation: The text highlights, 'The first was the degree to which Islam permeates other institutions in the society. As an important factor in the Emirate socio-political structure, Islam reflected in the daily routine of the social life through the five daily prayers, so also was the annual pilgrimage to Mecca and the Sharia legal system.'

questions.stem: What external influences altered the cultures of peoples in Nigeria according to the passage?

options.A: Only the slave trade and colonialism
options.C: The slave trade, colonialism, Islam, and Christianity

questions.explanation: The text explicitly lists 'the slave trade, colonialism, Islam and Christianity' as external influences that 'have equally altered definitively the cultures of peoples in Nigeria.'

questions.stem: Which pre-colonial element necessitated interactions in the Nigerian area through differences in natural endowments?
questions.explanation: The text states that 'Geographical specifications and differences in natural endowments necessitated interactions in the Nigerian area.' Migration, war, and Islam are separate elements.

questions.stem: Among the Yoruba, which stage of marriage involves bringing in a mediating agent (Alarina) to introduce the suitor and the intending bride?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'The second stage, the Alarina involves bringing in a mediating agent (usually, a woman, but may also be a man) who would mediate between the suitor and the intending bride by introducing them to each other.'

questions.stem: Nigeria occupies an area of ________ sq km
questions.explanation: Nigeria occupies an area of 923,768 square kilometers.

questions.stem: What aspects of traditional worship did some Aladura churches embrace that caused mainstream churches to regard them with mistrust?

options.B: Boisterous music and dance, ritual consultation with prophets, and use of white garments
options.C: Reading of the Psalms in Latin

questions.explanation: The text states that AICs were regarded with mistrust 'especially as some of those Aladura churches embraced certain aspects of traditional worship such as boisterous music and dance, ritual consultation with prophets... use of white garments, etc.'

questions.stem: Shitta Bey, a Muslim Creole, gave a whopping 400 pounds for the building of a mosque in Lagos in the __________
questions.explanation: Study Session 10 states that Muhammed Shitta Bey, a Muslim Creole, gave 400 pounds for the building of a mosque in Lagos in the 1890s. He also encouraged Muslims to acquire Western education.

questions.stem: The 'maroons' who joined the returnees in Sierra Leone in 1800 were from which island?
questions.explanation: Section 10.3 states: 'A third batch came from Jamaica in 1800 to join the returnees in Sierra Leone. They were called 'maroons' because of their having been abandoned in the mountains in Jamaica.'

questions.stem: The current anti-corruption institution in Nigeria was established by
questions.explanation: Chief Olusegun Obasanjo established the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) as a key anti-corruption institution during his presidency.

questions.stem: A child could be named after ________
questions.explanation: Children could be named after deities as a mark of reverence.

questions.stem: According to J F Ade Ajayi, the relics of early missionary activities in Nigeria included the:

options.C: Huge Cross at the Redemption Camp
options.D: Huge Cross in the centre of Old Warri

questions.explanation: The 'First Storey Building in Badagry' is historically recognized as a significant relic of early missionary activities in Nigeria.

questions.stem: What is the general title for a Yoruba king?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'Yoruba kingdoms were generally headed by a hereditary ruler referred to as Oba, that is, king.'

questions.stem: The legal system encourages corruption through the following ways except when it is _______

options.D: Capable of pursuing justice and equity

questions.explanation: Study Session 15 states that a legal system that is slow to address grievances, incapable of punishing offenders, or tilted towards rewarding the unjust promotes corruption. However, a system capable of pursuing justice and equity discourages corruption.

questions.stem: Which of the following was a primary reason for labor scarcity in pre-colonial Nigeria?

options.C: Rampant low life expectancy and infant mortality rates.
options.D: Abundant access to advanced farming tools.

questions.explanation: The text explicitly mentions: 'The reason for the relative scarcity of labour was the huge availability of land and demographic problems... coupled with the rapid population decline. In fact, labour shortage was a result of the rampant low life expectancy and infant mortality rate which generally shortened life span. There was also the several incidences of epidemics and diseases which claimed lives of children in addition to incessant raiding and kidnapping.'

questions.stem: One effect of corruption in Nigeria is:
questions.explanation: Corruption severely undermines democratic processes, often leading directly to election rigging, which compromises the fairness and credibility of elections.

questions.stem: In most Nigerian communities, stealing was often discouraged through which of the following?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'Discouraged' is the only option that logically completes the sentence to describe how stealing was treated in most Nigerian communities.

questions.stem: A diplomatic advantage of the end the Nigerian Civil War was that ________

options.A: Nigeria could disintegrate at any given time
options.B: The West should be prepared to recolonise Africa
options.C: The Black man was capable of resolving his crisis

questions.explanation: The resolution of the civil war showed that Africans could resolve their own crises without external intervention.

questions.stem: The National Youth Service Corps Scheme was initiated to promote ____
questions.explanation: The NYSC scheme was established in 1973 after the Nigerian Civil War, primarily to foster unity and national integration among Nigerian youths by deploying them to different parts of the country.

questions.stem: Initially, the British adopted the attitude of ________ during the Nigerian Civil War.

options.C: Direct support for the Federal Government

questions.explanation: Britain initially maintained neutrality but later supported the Federal Government.

questions.stem: Samuel Ajayi Crowther's missionary activities were largely concentrated in which area, leading to a 'missionary revolution'?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'Crowther's missionary activities were concentrated in the Delta area, particularly Bonny where a missionary revolution was carried out...' (Page 6)

questions.stem: What is described as 'a social heritage that exists consciously only within the human society'?
questions.explanation: The text concludes its discussion of culture by stating: 'It is a social heritage that exists consciously only within the human society,' distinguishing humans from other animals.

questions.stem: Which cultural component is concerned with the creation of tools, materials, techniques, and machinery?
questions.explanation: The technological component 'is concerned with the creation of tools, materials, techniques, and machinery' as stated in the section on technological culture.

questions.stem: All of the following except one facilitated British conquest of Eastern Nigeria.

options.A: The collaborative efforts of some Igbo leaders

questions.explanation: The British conquest of Eastern Nigeria was facilitated by several factors, including their superior military technology (firearms), internal disunity among local communities, and at times, the cooperation of certain local leaders. 'Divine assistance' is not a historical or material factor.

questions.stem: The Indirect Rule system of administration in Nigeria promoted elements of ________.

options.B: British/Western monetary culture and administrative system

questions.explanation: Indirect Rule, while appearing to use local structures, ultimately served to integrate the colonial territories into the British imperial system, imposing Western administrative principles and monetized economies while adapting them to local contexts.

questions.stem: If a Tiv girl is found not to be a virgin at marriage, what symbol does the husband send to her family?

options.B: A piece of cloth with a hole cut in the center or a block of moulded salt with a hole

questions.explanation: The husband sends a small block of moulded salt with a hole or a piece of cloth with a hole at the centre to shame the family for their daughter not being a virgin.

questions.stem: In spite of regional differences, traditional education equipped individuals to

options.C: Fit usefully into their society workspace
options.D: Defeat the Europeans when they came to Nigeria

questions.explanation: Traditional education systems across various Nigerian communities, despite their regional differences, aimed at socializing individuals to effectively integrate and function within their respective societies. This included vocational training, moral instruction, and cultural transmission, all geared towards making individuals productive members of their community.

questions.stem: What accusation did Pentecostal leaders face from mainstream churches in the 1980s and 1990s?
questions.explanation: The text states that 'Pentecostal leaders were accused of 'sheep stealing' especially in the 80s and 90s due to the attraction the movement held for young people.'

questions.stem: All of the following except one facilitated British conquest of Eastern Nigeria ________

options.A: The collaborative efforts of some Igbo leaders

questions.explanation: Divine assistance was not a factor in British conquest; the other options were.

questions.stem: In which culture is the prospective bride given a cup of palm-wine for her groom? The ________
questions.explanation: In Igbo culture, the bride is given a cup of palm-wine to present to her groom during marriage rites.

questions.stem: What did savannah area inhabitants in pre-colonial Nigeria typically engage in?

options.B: Cultivation, rearing domesticated animals like cattle and chickens

questions.explanation: The text states that those who inhabit the savannah areas 'engaged in cultivation and consumption of agricultural produce, reared domesticated animals such as cattle, chickens.'

questions.stem: Who introduced western education to Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'although western education was introduced by Christian missionaries, the colonial government later expanded to the nooks and crannies of the Nigerian area.'

questions.stem: On matters of faith, the following Christian group could be considered the most intolerant _________
questions.explanation: Study Session 4 states that 'Of all these Christian groups, Pentecostals were, and still remain the most intolerant, insisting that all others needed to be 'born again' before they could be considered serious Christians.'

questions.stem: The payment of ________ was/is an important aspect of marriage ceremony amongst most Nigerian communities
questions.explanation: Bride price (or bride wealth) is an important aspect of marriage ceremonies in most Nigerian communities.

questions.stem: All except one of the following were widespread in pre-jihad Hausaland.

options.A: The practice of pouring libations on rocks
options.C: The practice of venerating trees and rocks

questions.explanation: Pre-jihad Hausaland (before the Sokoto Jihad of the early 19th century) was characterized by a mix of animistic traditional religious practices, including the veneration of natural objects (trees, rocks) and polytheism, alongside the gradual spread of Islam. Christian missionary activities did not become widespread in this region until much later, primarily during the colonial era.

questions.stem: Among the Ibibio, if a child is born at night and a shadow from the moon appears, it is interpreted as:

options.A: A sign of prosperity and good fortune.
options.B: An indication that the child will be a great leader.
options.D: A blessing from the moon deity.

questions.explanation: The text notes: 'Among the Ibibio, if a child is born at night, any appearance of a shadow from the moon is interpreted as a bad omen.'

questions.stem: According to the text, what is the primary reason marriage is considered indispensable in Nigerian culture?

options.A: It is a source of wealth and social status
options.B: Childlessness is treated as a calamity and unmarried persons are derided
options.C: It is required by colonial laws
options.D: It guarantees a place in the afterlife

questions.explanation: The text states that an unmarried person is treated as an object of derision and childlessness is seen as a calamity, making marriage indispensable.

questions.stem: The following are processes involved in marriage ceremony amongst Nigerian communities except ________
questions.explanation: Slavery is not a process in marriage ceremonies; the other options are traditional steps.

questions.stem: One impact of Nigerian Pentecostalism on females is that it has gradually ______.

options.A: Broken the yoke of men 's control of church finances
options.B: Broken religious barriers that hitherto hindered women 's rise to leadership positions

questions.explanation: Pentecostalism in Nigeria has, in many instances, provided new avenues for women to assume leadership roles within the church, breaking some traditional religious barriers.

questions.stem: Who said, "To keep Nigeria one is a task that must be done"?
questions.explanation: General Yakubu Gowon famously stated that keeping Nigeria one was a task that must be done.

questions.stem: The National Youth Service Corp (NYSC) was established in ______.
questions.explanation: The National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) was established in 1973 by military decree to involve Nigerian graduates in nation-building and development.

questions.stem: A diplomatic advantage of the end the Nigerian Civil War was that ________.

options.A: Nigeria could disintegrate at any given time
options.C: The West should be prepared to recolonise Africa
options.D: The Black man was capable of resolving his crisis

questions.explanation: The successful resolution of the Nigerian Civil War by Nigerians themselves, without external intervention dictating the outcome, was seen as a significant diplomatic achievement demonstrating African self-reliance and capability to manage internal conflicts.

questions.stem: Why did the British move a batch of African returnees from Nova Scotia in North America to Freetown, Sierra Leone, in 1792?

options.A: To establish a new trading post for goods
options.B: To escape religious persecution in Nova Scotia
options.C: For fear of being victimized by the independent United States of America
options.D: To facilitate their integration into local African communities

questions.explanation: Section 10.3 explains: 'The British moved them to Nova Scotia after the war for fear of being victimised by the independent United States of America. They were eventually moved to Freetown from Nova Scotia.'

questions.stem: The 'new' diaspora's impact on homeland development has come in the form of individual and collective efforts, including those by Nigerians in Diaspora Organization (NIDO) groups in areas such as:

options.A: Military defense and foreign policy formulation.
options.D: Global sports management and entertainment production.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'The different NIDO groups have identified needs in different areas such as education, health and infrastructure development.' (Page 7)

questions.stem: Which Yoruba sub-group was the term 'Yoruba' first applied to by the Hausa?
questions.explanation: From Study Session 2, the ITQ states: 'The name Yoruba was first applied to which of the Yoruba sub-groups?' with the answer being Oyo.

questions.stem: According to the text, what contributed significantly to the institution of democratic rule in Nigeria in 1999?

options.C: The leadership of mainstream churches, human rights groups, and civil society bodies

questions.explanation: The text states: 'When democratic rule was eventually instituted in 1999, it was clear that the leadership of the mainstream churches and human rights groups as well as other concerned civil society bodies had contributed significantly to it.'

questions.stem: The Igala occupy which part of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Igala people are located in the North-central zone of Nigeria, primarily in Kogi State.

questions.stem: What items are typically presented to the girl's family as part of the Yoruba Idana ceremony?

options.B: Honey, kola nut, sugar cane, alligator pepper, and palm oil

questions.explanation: The items include oyin (honey), obi (kola nut), ireke (sugar cane), ataare (alligator pepper), and epo (palm oil).

questions.stem: What did the Portuguese connection with the slave trade do to their missionary efforts?

options.B: It had no effect on missionary work

questions.explanation: The text states that 'the connection of these early Portuguese with the inhuman slave trade did not help matters' in terms of their missionary efforts.

questions.stem: One obstacle to administrative and political unitarism in Nigeria is the country's
questions.explanation: Nigeria is known for its vast ethnic, linguistic, and religious 'heterogeneity' (diversity), which often presents challenges to achieving complete administrative and political uniformity or unitarism.

questions.stem: Colonial women's organizations protested against ________
questions.explanation: Study Session 7 states that women organizations protested discrimination, exploitation, inequality, oppression, women's taxation, high market dues, denial of higher education, and overzealous and high-handed warrant chiefs.

questions.stem: Among the Edo, what do the couple do with their big toes in goat blood during the marriage ritual?

options.A: They wash the blood off immediately
options.B: They dip their big toes into the blood as prayers are said
options.D: They sprinkle the blood on their heads

questions.explanation: The couple stands at the entrance, each with a foot on the doorstep, and dips their big toes into the goat's blood while prayers are said for their marital journey.

questions.stem: The backbone of the colonial economy was:
questions.explanation: The text clearly states, 'The backbone of the colonial economy was agriculture.'

questions.stem: What does the text suggest about the pre-colonial history of Nigerian peoples regarding war?

options.B: It is replete with the stories of many wars

questions.explanation: The text states: 'the pre-colonial history of peoples who lived in the Nigerian area is replete with the stories of many wars.'

questions.stem: At the Kampala peace talks of May 1968, Biafra requested a ________

options.A: Punishment of the Federal Government of Nigeria
options.D: Recognition of its ability to create states

questions.explanation: At the Kampala talks, Biafra requested a ceasefire before negotiations could begin.

questions.stem: In the "constitutional village monarchies" of Onitsha, Oguta, Osommari and Aboh, the ruler is known as the
questions.explanation: In these Igbo communities, the traditional ruler is known as the Obi.

questions.stem: What was the main political authority in a typical Ijaw village before the arrival of Europeans?

options.B: The assembly of all adult males presided over by the Amanyanabo

questions.explanation: The text states: 'The main political authority in the village was the assembly of all adult males which was presided over by the Amanyanabo who owed his office to the fact that he was the head of the lineage which discovered or founded the village site.'

questions.stem: The major religious crisis in Northern Nigeria in the early 1980s was caused by the
questions.explanation: The Maitatsine riots of 1980 in Kano were caused by the Maitatsine group led by Muhammad Marwa.

questions.stem: What was the Structural Adjustment Programme (SAP) mentioned in the text?

options.B: An impoverishing economic policy that Christian leaders opposed

questions.explanation: The text refers to the 'impoverishing Structural Adjustment Programme (SAP)' that Christian leaders opposed alongside human rights abuses during the Babangida and Abacha regimes.

questions.stem: Which Hausa state inflicted military defeats on Katsina and Kano to control trans-Saharan trade?
questions.explanation: The text states that Zamfara, while it was the leading Hausa state, 'inflicted military defeats on Katsina and Kano, thereby controlling the trans-Saharan trade in Hausaland.'

questions.stem: The women organizations protested discrimination, exploitation, women's taxation, etc under the __________
questions.explanation: Women's protests like the Aba Women's Riot occurred during the colonial period against British policies.

questions.stem: How was the education of youths typically carried out in pre-colonial Nigerian societies?

options.A: Through formal public schools established by leaders.
options.B: By sending them to neighboring empires for advanced studies.
options.C: Through an organized system of apprenticeship and training in traditional occupations.
options.D: Primarily through storytelling and oral traditions only.

questions.explanation: The document mentions: 'The education of their youths was done through organised system of apprenticeship and training in the traditional occupations of farming, fishing, animal husbandry, the crafts, and trade.'

questions.stem: What formed the 'backbone' of the colonial economy in Nigeria, as stated in the document?

options.C: Agriculture, primarily to provide industrial raw materials.
options.D: The development of a robust service sector.

questions.explanation: The document clearly states: 'The backbone of the colonial economy was agriculture. The focus was simply to provide industrial raw materials for factories and industrial plants.'

questions.stem: Unlike their rural counterparts, Nigerian cities are more prone to _________
questions.explanation: Study Session 13 states that cities in Nigeria are more prone to crimes and criminality than their rural counterparts. Crimes such as armed robbery, prostitution, hooliganism, and burglary are rife in cities.

questions.stem: Which two print media publications were highlighted for their immense value in mobilising people against colonial rule and policies in Nigeria?

options.A: The Nigerian Tribune and Daily Times.
options.B: The West African Pilot and Comet.
options.C: The Lagos Weekly Records and The Lagos Observer.
options.D: The Nigerian Chronicle and National Concord.

questions.explanation: The document states: 'In Nigeria, the Lagos Weekly Records published by the Jacksons and the Lagos Observer published by J. Bagan Benjamin were of immense value in mobilising the people against colonial rule and colonial policies.' (Page 6)

questions.stem: One obstacle to administrative and political unitarism in Nigeria is the country's ________
questions.explanation: Nigeria's ethnic and cultural heterogeneity creates obstacles to unitarism.

questions.stem: In 2005, Uche Nworah commented on the Nigerian cultural presence abroad. Which of these was NOT highlighted by him as a reflection of this cultural presence?

options.D: Speaking native languages with one another

questions.explanation: Section 10.2 quotes Uche Nworah stating that Nigerians abroad sustain ethnic group consciousness, set up community associations, wear traditional attires, bear Nigerian names, and speak native languages. He specifically notes 'the only problem is with the generation born in the new lands, who are torn with the issue of double identity,' implying that complete assimilation is not the general reflection of cultural presence, but rather the maintenance of distinctiveness.

questions.stem: When was Enugu founded?
questions.explanation: Enugu was founded in 1909 following the discovery of coal in the Udi ridge.

questions.stem: Which of these was a prominent and successful business woman in Ibadan?
questions.explanation: Study Session 7 states that in the nineteenth century, Efunsetan Aniwura, the Iyalode of Ibadan, was a successful business woman and activist per excellence. She is a prominent figure in Ibadan history.

questions.stem: The establishment of Port Harcourt was to facilitate the ___
questions.explanation: Port Harcourt was established by the British colonial administration primarily as a deep-water port to facilitate the export of coal, which had been discovered in commercial quantities in Enugu and was transported to the port via a newly constructed railway.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors contributed to boosting the status of Muslims in Yorubaland during the 19th century?

options.B: Influx of liberated slaves to Lagos and Badagry
options.D: The decline of the Sokoto Caliphate

questions.explanation: The text lists, 'First was the influx of the liberated slaves to Lagos and Badagry and a few other places. Most of these returnees were skilled and talented artisans. Some of them had become relatively wealthy and influential.' This was one of two key factors.

questions.stem: The Indirect Rule system did not encourage the use of ________?
questions.explanation: The Indirect Rule system was based on using existing traditional institutions such as Native Authorities, Native Courts, and Native Treasuries. Native Militias were not a formal feature of the Indirect Rule system, as the colonial government maintained control over military and police forces.

questions.stem: What is a notable difference in the hospitality arrangements during the Igala marriage feast compared to most other Nigerian communities?

options.A: The bride's family is responsible for entertaining all guests.
options.B: The groom's family brings all necessary supplies, cooks, and serves everyone, including the bride's family.
options.C: The entire community contributes food and labor equally.
options.D: No feasting or elaborate entertainment takes place; it's a simple ceremony.

questions.explanation: The text highlights: 'Among the Igala, it is the family of the man that entertains everybody. They bring all necessary things from firewood, food items, plates, cups and spoons to the bride's family. They also bring those who cook and served the food. The girl's family would only look on and be served like other visitors and never render any assistance.'

questions.stem: Among the Ibibio, what is interpreted as a bad omen if a child is born at night?

options.B: Any appearance of a shadow from the moon

questions.explanation: Among the Ibibio, if a child is born at night, any appearance of a shadow from the moon is interpreted as a bad omen.

questions.stem: How did colonial trading firms primarily repatriate resources from Nigeria to Britain?

options.A: By reinvesting all profits in local infrastructure.
options.B: Through fair and transparent trade practices.
options.C: By fixing arbitrarily low prices for Nigerian produce and high prices for imported goods.
options.D: By offering competitive wages to local laborers.

questions.explanation: The document states that resources were 'mobilised and repatriated by the firms to Britain through criminally low prices offered Nigerian producers and through scandalously high prices demanded for imported items.'

questions.stem: The concept of “autochthones” or “stateless societies” was used by British colonial scholars to describe Nigerian communities with _______ institutions?
questions.explanation: British colonial scholars often used terms like 'stateless societies' to describe communities, particularly in the Igbo region, that lacked a centralized political authority and functioned through diffused power structures, which they contrasted with hierarchical systems.

questions.stem: The Confluence State consists of ________ rivers
questions.explanation: Kogi State (the Confluence State) is where the Niger and Benue rivers meet.

questions.stem: What is identified as the most significant economic change in post-colonial Nigeria?

options.A: The rapid growth of small and medium-sized enterprises.
options.B: A renewed focus on traditional agricultural methods.
options.C: The emergence and dominance of the petroleum sector.
options.D: Extensive foreign direct investment in manufacturing.

questions.explanation: The text explicitly mentions: 'The most significant, if not the sole change, in the economy of post-colonial Nigeria has been the emergence and dominance of the petroleum sector.'

questions.stem: One effect of corruption in Nigeria is ________.
questions.explanation: Corruption often manifests in the manipulation of democratic processes. Election rigging, which involves illicitly altering the results of an election, is a direct and common effect of widespread corruption, undermining the fairness and legitimacy of the electoral system.

questions.stem: Which states were established by the six sons of Bawo?

options.A: Daura, Katsina, Kano, Rano, Zazzau, Gobir
options.B: Zamfara, Kebbi, Gwari, Yauri, Nupe, Jukun
options.C: Biram, Daura, Kano, Katsina, Zaria, Gobir
options.D: Sokoto, Kebbi, Zamfara, Katsina, Kano, Jigawa

questions.explanation: The text lists the six states as Daura, Katsina, Kano, Rano, Zazzau, and Gobir, established by the six sons of Bawo.

questions.stem: Christianity was first introduced to the Southern part of Nigeria during the _________
questions.explanation: Christianity was first introduced to the southern part of Nigeria by Portuguese Catholic traders in the 15th century.

questions.stem: Which characteristic of political economy as a discipline specifically recognizes the inevitability of change and transformation leading to new systems of economic and social organisation?

options.A: First, it recognises the primacy of the economy.
options.B: Second, it recognises the necessity for continuous expansion of productive forces.
options.C: Third, the Marxist variant of political economy particularly recognizes the inevitability of change and transformation.
options.D: Fourth, political economy takes a comprehensive view of phenomena.

questions.explanation: The text explicitly states: 'Third, the Marxist variant of political economy particularly recognizes the inevitability of change and transformation which lead to successive emergence of new and better systems of economic and social organisation.'

questions.stem: Which of the following is identified as an indigenous church group in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: African Indigenous Churches (AICs) are church denominations that originated in Africa, often characterized by a blend of traditional African cultural elements with Christian worship and doctrine. They represent a significant part of Nigeria's religious landscape, distinct from colonial-era mission churches.

questions.stem: When was Christianity re-introduced into Nigeria in a way that bore lasting fruits?

options.B: First half of the nineteenth century
options.C: Last quarter of the nineteenth century

questions.explanation: The text states that 'it was in the first half of the nineteenth century that European and American missionaries re-introduced Christianity into the country. It was this second attempt that bore lasting fruits.'

questions.stem: Before the 1930s, one of the following was not an urban centre _______.
questions.explanation: Abuja was developed as Nigeria's new capital city in the late 20th century, becoming an urban center much later than Calabar, Lagos, and Enugu, which had established urban histories before the 1930s.

questions.stem: If a chosen girl in Edo tradition refuses to go through the marriage process, what special present might her father or brother receive to persuade her?

options.C: A plot of land for farming.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'Should she refuse to go through the marriage process, a special present called Ugbo Ogba or the strong foot would be given to her father or brother to persuade her to go through the marriage process.'

questions.stem: Nigerians in the West, particularly in the United States and the United Kingdom, constitute a high percentage in which of the following professional fields?

options.B: Medical and health care, banking, engineering, and academia

questions.explanation: The document states that "Nigerians constitute a high percent of medical and health care workers, bankers, engineers and academics in the West, especially in the United States of America and the United Kingdom."

questions.stem: In what year did Nigeria return to civilian rule and liberal democracy?
questions.explanation: Nigeria returned to civilian rule in 1999 with the election of President Olusegun Obasanjo.

questions.stem: A situation that encourages pressure from ethnic members to subvert due process is _______
questions.explanation: Nepotism involves favoring family or ethnic members, leading to pressure to subvert due process for their benefit.

questions.stem: The early Christian missionary activities in Nigeria had a three pronged approach, namely
questions.explanation: The three Cs of missionary activity were Christianization, Commerce, and Civilization.

questions.stem: Diaspora refers to the physical and cultural presence of Nigerians ______.
questions.explanation: The term 'diaspora' specifically refers to the dispersion of a people from their original homeland, hence 'Nigerians outside Nigeria'.

questions.stem: Diaspora refers to the physical and cultural presence of Nigerians ___
questions.explanation: The term 'diaspora' specifically refers to the dispersion of a people from their original homeland. Therefore, the Nigerian diaspora refers to Nigerians and people of Nigerian descent living outside of Nigeria.

questions.stem: In which year did Zamfara State, under Governor Ahmed Sanni Yerima, introduce the Sharia Penal Code, marking a major step in the Sharia legal system in the Fourth Republic?
questions.explanation: The text states, 'the first major and decisive step was taken in 1999, when the then Executive Governor of Zamfara State, Ahmed Sanni Yerima, introduced the Sharia Penal Code.'

questions.stem: In traditional Igbo funeral ceremonies, which categories of people were typically thrown into the 'evil forest' upon their death?

options.B: Lepers, those who died of smallpox, lunatics, or women who died at child birth.

questions.explanation: The text explicitly states: 'You will note that lepers and those who died of small pox were thrown into the evil forest. Those who died of accidents, lunatics or women who died at child birth were hurriedly buried.' The evil forest was for those whose deaths were considered unnatural or abominable.

questions.stem: What does the document suggest was the underlying reason why the Northern political class used the Sharia issue as a 'smokescreen'?

options.B: To attract international aid for religious projects
options.C: To divert attention from their weakness and ineptitude
options.D: To unify all Northern states under one religious banner

questions.explanation: The text states: 'You will note that the Northern political class used the Sharia issue as a smokescreen to divert attention from their weakness and ineptitude.'

questions.stem: According to J F Ade Ajayi, the relics of early missionary activities in Nigeria included the ______.

options.A: Huge Cross in the centre of Old Warri
options.B: Huge Cross at the Redemption Camp

questions.explanation: The First Storey Building in Badagry, erected in 1845, is widely recognized as a significant relic of early missionary activities in Nigeria, serving as the mission house for the Church Missionary Society.

questions.stem: The founder of the royal dynasties of Benin with a link with Ife was ______?
questions.explanation: Oral traditions and historical accounts widely credit Oranmiyan, a prince from Ife, as the founder of the Benin dynasty. He is said to have established the royal lineage that ruled the Benin Kingdom.

questions.stem: The major motive of European colonial presence in the Nigeria area was ______.
questions.explanation: While other factors were present, the primary motive for European colonial presence in Nigeria, like many other African territories, was economic exploitation, including access to raw materials and markets.

questions.stem: One of the major umbrella Christian organisations in Nigeria is the ____
questions.explanation: The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) is widely recognized as the primary umbrella organization for various Christian denominations and churches in Nigeria.

questions.stem: In the context of Political Economy as a discipline or method of inquiry, what is recognized as the 'foundation of society'?

options.C: The primacy of the economy and material production.

questions.explanation: The text notes that Political Economy 'recognises the primacy of the economy and material production as the foundation of society.'

questions.stem: The establishment of 'Nigerian Native Churches' was an indication that Nigerians could

options.B: Be patient with Nigerian collaborators of colonialism
options.D: Throw off the yoke of 'spiritual or religious' colonialism

questions.explanation: Study Session 4 states that the establishment of African or Native Churches demonstrated that African churchmen and clergy could successfully throw off the yoke of spiritual or religious colonialism. This was significant because white missionaries were in close league with colonial authorities.

questions.stem: All of the following are aspects of our cultural heritage except _______.
questions.explanation: Matriculation ceremonies are modern academic rituals marking a student's formal enrollment in a university or college. Funeral, marriage, and naming ceremonies are deeply rooted traditional cultural practices.

questions.stem: What caused the Jukun to migrate southwards to the Lower Benue region by the mid eighteenth century?

options.B: External pressure from the Bata and Chamba

questions.explanation: The text states that 'external pressure by such neighbouring groups as the Bata and Chamba caused them to migrate southwards to the Lower Benue region by the mid eighteenth century.'

questions.stem: While men dominated Christian services in various churches and denominations, __________

options.A: Young men managed the affairs of the house
options.C: Women played key roles in the traditional religion

questions.explanation: While Christianity was male-dominated, women held influential positions and roles in traditional religious practices.

questions.stem: A regime of quick and easy money in Nigeria did not encourage _______
questions.explanation: The culture of quick and easy money encourages deviousness, laziness, and corruption, not diligence.

questions.stem: What religious element is listed as one of the six pre-colonial cultural shaping factors?
questions.explanation: The text explicitly includes Islam as the sixth element among geography, economy, migration, inter-marriage, war, and Islam.

questions.stem: According to the text, which region had the earliest indication of the presence of Islam in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The text states, 'the earliest indication of the presence of Islam in Nigeria was in Borno, which emerged out of the ancient Kanem–Borno Empire.' This highlights Kanem-Borno as the region with the earliest Islamic presence.

questions.stem: When crude oil export replaced agriculture in Nigeria, the culture of corruption also ________.
questions.explanation: The sudden influx of wealth from crude oil exports, often referred to as the 'oil boom', led to a significant increase in opportunities for corruption as resources became concentrated and rent-seeking behavior intensified, thereby escalating the culture of corruption.

questions.stem: In parts of Kogi State, why is it prohibited to whistle at night?
questions.explanation: In parts of Kogi State, it was prohibited to whistle at night because it would bring evil spirit.

questions.stem: The profound socio-cultural western influences on Nigeria include _____.
questions.explanation: Western influences, particularly through colonialism, profoundly impacted Nigerian society by introducing Christianity and Western-style education, which reshaped social structures, values, and knowledge systems.

questions.stem: What direct impact of Islam on Nigerian society is highlighted in the text concerning urbanization?

options.B: The stimulation of urbanization, leading to conversion of villages to towns and establishment of new towns.
options.D: The destruction of existing urban centers.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'We must emphasise that Islam recorded a direct impact on the Nigerian society through its active involvement in the process of urbanization. For example, under the stimulation of the Sokoto Caliphate, many villages were converted to towns and new towns were established as centers of commerce and industry.'

questions.stem: Nigerians in Diaspora Organization (NIDO) was established by Nigerians in various parts of the world with what primary objective?

options.A: To lobby foreign governments for relaxed immigration policies
options.B: To promote Nigerian cultural festivals globally
options.C: To coordinate individual and collective development efforts in the homeland
options.D: To facilitate international trade and investment for personal gain

questions.explanation: Page 7 states: "...Nigerians in different parts of the world have organised themselves into groups called Nigerians in Diaspora Organization (NIDO) in parts of Africa, the Americas, Asia, Australia, Europe and the Middle East. The different NIDO groups have identified needs in different areas such as education, health and infrastructure development. They have assisted government at different levels with information and, in some instances, resources for some projects, thereby contributing to the improvement the overall quality of life."

questions.stem: During colonialism, Owerri grew rapidly from a market town into a beehive of all except _________
questions.explanation: Study Session 13 states that when Owerri was designated as a state capital, it grew rapidly from a market town into a beehive of political, administrative, commercial and social activities. Religious pilgrimages and activities are not mentioned as a factor.

questions.stem: What factor hindered the first Portuguese attempt to introduce Christianity to Nigeria?

options.A: Lack of Portuguese interest in conversion
options.B: The connection of the Portuguese with the inhuman slave trade

questions.explanation: The text states that 'the connection of these early Portuguese with the inhuman slave trade did not help matters,' along with the fact that the new religion found it impossible to displace traditional religion.

questions.stem: Who was the first black man to be consecrated as an Anglican Bishop?
questions.explanation: The text states that Samuel Ajayi Crowther was 'the first black man to be consecrated as an Anglican Bishop.'

questions.stem: At the Kampala peace talks of May 1968, Biafra requested a ______.

options.B: Punishment of the Federal Government of Nigeria
options.D: Recognition of its ability to create states

questions.explanation: During the Kampala peace talks in 1968, Biafra's primary demand was the recognition of its sovereignty as an independent nation, which was a fundamental point of contention.

questions.stem: Federal control of crude oil production has deprived host communities of __________

options.A: The fiscal revenue accruing from oil production
options.B: Judicious spending of the oil wealth
options.C: Land and water for production of goods and services
options.D: Abled man power for economic development

questions.explanation: Federal control of oil revenues has deprived oil-producing communities of fiscal benefits they could have used for development.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not anti-social?
questions.explanation: Diligence is a positive virtue, not anti-social like nepotism, corruption, or narcissism.

questions.stem: The major motive of European colonial presence in the Nigerian area was ______.
questions.explanation: While other factors played a role, the primary driver for European, particularly British, colonization of Nigeria was economic. This included access to raw materials (like palm oil, rubber, tin), markets for manufactured goods, and investment opportunities.

questions.stem: The sociological analysis of a city comprises its various _______

options.B: Social compositions and their interactions with one another

questions.explanation: The sociological analysis of a city examines its social groups and their interactions.

questions.stem: Amongst the Ibibio, the death of a child was ascribed to ________ ?
questions.explanation: Among the Ibibio, the death of a child was often ascribed to witchcraft.

questions.stem: Which of these were the 3Rs Agenda after post-Nigerian Civil War?
questions.explanation: After the Nigerian Civil War, the government implemented the 3Rs Agenda: Reconciliation, Rehabilitation, and Reconstruction to heal the nation, rebuild infrastructure, and reintegrate the war-affected regions.

questions.stem: To fight corruption, Nigerians need not __________

options.B: Adopt the right value and attitude to life

questions.explanation: Nigerians should NOT relent; they should continue promoting anti-corruption programs.

questions.stem: Between the 15th and 19th centuries, millions of people were forced out of the Nigerian area through the __________
questions.explanation: Millions were forcibly taken out of Nigeria through the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade.

questions.stem: Among the Ibibio, what traditional practice follows the payment of the bride price and precedes the bride joining her husband?

options.A: A lengthy period of community service by the bride.
options.B: The 'fattening' period, which marks the passage from girlhood to womanhood.
options.C: A series of complex negotiations with the mother-in-law.
options.D: A ritual abduction by the groom's friends.

questions.explanation: The text indicates: 'You will note that after the payment of the bride price, fattening begins. This marks the passage from girlhood to womanhood and qualifies the lady to marry.'

questions.stem: The features of the foreign Pentecostal Churches initially excluded _______

options.A: Willingness of white priests to subordinate themselves to African leadership
options.B: Mistreatment and humiliation of black priests
options.C: Reluctance of white missionaries to affirm the leadership qualities of black priests

questions.explanation: White priests were unwilling to subordinate themselves to African leadership, causing tensions.

questions.stem: In parts of Igboland, who was forbidden from marrying an outcast (osu)?
questions.explanation: In parts of Igboland, it was an abomination for a free born (Diala) to marry an outcast (osu).

questions.stem: The manhood test for marriage amongst the Hausa is called ____
questions.explanation: "Sharo" is a traditional Fulani (closely associated with some Hausa communities) test of manhood involving flogging, often performed as a rite of passage, including for marriage eligibility.

questions.stem: Who assumed headship of the Church of God Missions in Benin after her husband's death?
questions.explanation: The text states that 'on the death of their husbands, some wives have assumed the headship of large ministries as exemplified by the cases of Bishop Margaret Idahosa of the Church of God Missions, Benin.'

questions.stem: If a Tiv girl is a virgin at marriage, what does the husband send to the mother-in-law?

options.B: A goat to be slaughtered with great rejoicing

questions.explanation: The husband buys a goat and sends it to the mother-in-law, who invites all the women in the community and slaughters the goat with great rejoicing.

questions.stem: The seven states established by Bayajida's legitimate sons were known as
questions.explanation: The seven legitimate states founded by Bayajida's sons were known as the Hausa Bakwai.

questions.stem: The administration of land in most pre-colonial societies was entrusted with which of these?
questions.explanation: Study Session 7 states that the administration of land was entrusted to the chiefs and rulers on behalf of the society. Land was given to men for the asking, for farming purposes.

questions.stem: All of the following are aspects of our cultural heritage except ________
questions.explanation: Study Session 5 discusses marriage, naming, and funeral ceremonies as key aspects of cultural heritage. Matriculation ceremonies are academic events, not traditional cultural heritage.

questions.stem: In Yoruba marriage traditions, what do sugar and honey symbolize when presented as part of the Idana ceremony?
questions.explanation: The text specifies: 'The sugar and honey symbolize happiness in marriage; the kola for the couple's protection against sickness; the alligator pepper for them to have many children; and the palm oil for resilience in their marriage.'

questions.stem: What is unique about the Igalia marriage ceremony regarding who provides food and cooking?

options.B: The groom's family brings all food items, cooking utensils, and cooks for everyone

questions.explanation: Unlike other Nigerian communities, the groom's family brings firewood, food, plates, cooks, and serves everyone; the bride's family only watches and is served.

questions.stem: One of the crises of the colonial regime in Nigeria was ________
questions.explanation: The colonial regime was characterized by a spiral of repression against resistance movements.

questions.stem: A dependent economy is A _______
questions.explanation: Study Session 9 states that a dependent economy is a disarticulated one. It lacks internal inter-sectoral interdependence and symbiosis, and therefore cannot achieve internal macroeconomic stability.

questions.stem: The attitude of white priests in the foreign Pentecostal Churches in Nigeria led to the establishment of the _______
questions.explanation: Discrimination by white missionaries led to the establishment of African-led secessionist churches.

questions.stem: Generally, women engaged in a variety of crafts such as dyeing, pottery, cosmetics, bead-making?
questions.explanation: Historically and culturally in many Nigerian societies, 'women' were traditionally involved in various crafts like dyeing, pottery, cosmetics, and bead-making, contributing significantly to the local economy and cultural heritage.

questions.stem: According to the text, how do the different Nigerians in Diaspora Organization (NIDO) groups primarily contribute to Nigeria's development?

options.A: By establishing new political parties in Nigeria.
options.B: By identifying needs in education, health, and infrastructure, and assisting government with information and resources.
options.C: By encouraging Nigerians to remain permanently in their host countries.
options.D: By focusing solely on cultural exchange programs without direct development aid.

questions.explanation: The different NIDO groups have identified needs in different areas such as education, health and infrastructure development. They have assisted government at different levels with information and, in some instances, resources for some projects, thereby contributing to the improvement the overall quality of life.

questions.stem: What are the traditional names for the first son and first daughter, respectively, among the Ibibio people, as stated in the text?
questions.explanation: The text specifies: 'The first son is usually named Akpan, the first daughter Adieba'.

questions.stem: Which African church was founded in Lagos in 1888?
questions.explanation: The text lists 'the Ebenezer Baptist Church founded in Lagos in 1888' as one of the African or Native churches.

questions.stem: In Edo marriage, what is the purpose of the special present called Ugbo Ogba or 'the strong foot'?

options.A: To signify the completion of bride price payment.
options.B: To bless the couple's marital journey.
options.C: To persuade a girl or her father/brother to agree to the marriage process if she initially refuses.
options.D: To mark the bride's transition into womanhood.

questions.explanation: The text describes: 'Should she refuse to go through the marriage process, a special present called Ugbo Ogba or the strong foot would be given to her father or brother to persuade her to go through the marriage process.'

questions.stem: Which of the following was identified as a primary 'pull factor' for Nigerian emigration during the colonial and post-colonial periods?

options.B: Existence of 'greener pastures' in advanced countries
options.D: Land alienation by the colonial government

questions.explanation: The document states: "The 'pull factor' was mainly the existence of 'greener pastures' abroad, especially in advanced countries of North America and Europe..."

questions.stem: In the Akoko Edo marriage tradition, what unusual circumstance might lead to the abduction of the intending bride?

options.A: If the groom's family cannot afford the bride price.
options.B: If the girl refuses the union, even if her father agrees.
options.C: If the parents of the girl do not agree, but the girl's mother might assist in the abduction.
options.D: If the girl is a minor and her consent cannot be obtained.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'If the parent of the girl do not agree, the girl could be abducted by the intending groom. If her father does not agree and the mother agrees, the mother would aid or assist in the abduction.'

questions.stem: What was the main role of major British firms like the United African Company and John Holt and Company during the colonial era regarding trade in Nigeria?

options.A: They primarily focused on manufacturing industrial goods within Nigeria.
options.B: They organised indigenous markets for local produce.
options.C: They bought up African produce for export and imported/distributed industrial goods and consumables.
options.D: They established banks and financial institutions for local entrepreneurs.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'The British firms bought up African produce and organised their export. They also were responsible for the importation and distribution of industrial goods and consumables in Nigeria.'

questions.stem: Why did traditional political elite and merchant princes, such as King Kosoko of Lagos and King Jaja of Opobo, resist British merchants moving into the hinterland?

options.A: They wanted to form their own trade alliances with other European powers.
options.B: Their lucrative middleman positions were threatened by British advocacy of free penetration and free trade.
options.C: They feared a loss of cultural identity due to British influence.
options.D: They preferred to maintain traditional subsistence economies without external trade.

questions.explanation: The text indicates: '...their lucrative middleman positions were threatened by British advocacy of free penetration and free trade. In the ensuing conflict of commercial interests, British merchants appealed to their home government which responded with military support.'

questions.stem: The Aba women riot of 1929 was essentially meant to protect the interest of women in the society against ________

options.A: Conflict between Igbo leaders and colonial officials
options.B: Oppressive policies of the colonial government
options.C: Non-recognition of women in the village assembly

questions.explanation: The Aba Women's Riot was a protest against oppressive colonial policies, particularly taxation and warrant chiefs.

questions.stem: What symbolic item presented during Yoruba Idana represents happiness in marriage?
questions.explanation: During Idana, honey and sugar cane symbolize happiness in marriage; kola is for protection, alligator pepper for many children, palm oil for resilience.

questions.stem: One urban nucleus was not directly influenced by colonial railway lines:
questions.explanation: Ile-Ife was a traditional cultural centre and not directly influenced by colonial railway lines.

questions.stem: A direct opposite of the Indirect Rule system of administration was ________ ?
questions.explanation: The Assimilation system (used by the French) was the direct opposite of Indirect Rule.

questions.stem: Which Egba leader, who had fought on the side of the British during the American revolutionary war, negotiated with the Sierra Leone Company for the settlement of liberated slaves from Nova Scotia?
questions.explanation: It is noteworthy that Thomas Peters, an Egba, who had fought on the side of the British during the American revolutionary war, was among the leaders who negotiated with the directors of the Sierra Leone Company in England which led up to the settlement of the liberated slaves from Nova Scotia in Sierra Leone.

questions.stem: The Federal Government's use of "police action" during the Nigerian civil war was to ______.

options.D: Make Ojukwu leader of the Eastern Region

questions.explanation: The Nigerian Federal Government referred to its military operations against Biafra as 'police action' with the stated aim of suppressing the secessionist movement, capturing its leader Emeka Ojukwu, and preserving the unity of Nigeria.

questions.stem: In some societies, a dead child was mutilated to alter which of these ______?

options.C: Outbreak of disease in the land

questions.explanation: In some traditional African beliefs, the mutilation of a dead child was performed to prevent its spirit from re-incarnating, particularly if the child was believed to be an 'ogbanje' or 'abiku' – a child believed to repeatedly die and be reborn to the same mother.

questions.stem: Lt-Col Odumegwu Ojukwu's interpretation of the Aburi agreements was:
questions.explanation: The text indicates that Ojukwu's interpretation of the Aburi agreements emphasized 'Extreme decentralisation'.

questions.stem: European and American missionaries re-introduced Christianity to Nigeria in the _________
questions.explanation: Christianity was re-introduced to Nigeria in the 19th century by European and American missionaries.

questions.stem: When was coal discovered in Enugu?
questions.explanation: Coal was discovered in Enugu in 1909 by geologist Albert Ernest Kitson.

questions.stem: The first set of African liberated slaves to return home to West Africa came from England and settled in Freetown in the territory that was later named Sierra Leone in what year?
questions.explanation: The first set of African liberated slaves to return home to West Africa came from England in 1787. They settled in Freetown in the territory that was later named Sierra Leone.

questions.stem: The “Iwe Irohin” was published by?
questions.explanation: “Iwe Irohin fun awon Eko ati Yoruba” (Newspaper for the Egba and Yoruba) was the first indigenous language newspaper in Nigeria, published by the Church Missionary Society (CMS) in Abeokuta, starting in 1859.

questions.stem: What commission of the Catholic Church defended human rights during military regimes?

options.B: The Justice, Development and Peace Commission

questions.explanation: The text states that 'the Catholic Church, through its Justice, Development and Peace Commission valiantly defended human rights' during military regimes.

questions.stem: Chief Ernest Shonekan Interim National Government in Nigeria lasted for ________ ?
questions.explanation: Chief Ernest Shonekan's Interim National Government lasted for 82 days (August 26 - November 17, 1993).

questions.stem: Which of these was/is the significance of a lion roaring at night in the village square amongst the Ngor Okpala people?

options.C: A marriage ceremony was taking place

questions.explanation: Study Session 5 states that in Ngor Okpala, if a lion came out in the night to roar in the village square, it signified an abomination had been committed. This is part of the cultural heritage of abominations and sacrileges.

questions.stem: According to local traditions, from where did Bayajjida flee before arriving in Daura?
questions.explanation: The text states that Bayajjida 'is said to have fled from Baghdad, his homeland, to Kanem-Borno, and then to Daura in Hausaland.'

questions.stem: The functions of the Ulama included all except ___
questions.explanation: The Ulama are Muslim scholars and religious authorities whose functions primarily revolve around interpreting Islamic law, providing legal and spiritual guidance, and serving as guardians of religious traditions. 'Conquest of the faithful' is not typically a direct function of the Ulama as a scholarly body.

questions.stem: What two key areas did the Creoles embrace, which later played a significant role in their contributions to West Africa?

options.A: Traditional religious worship and indigenous learning.

questions.explanation: The document states: 'The Creoles embraced the Christian faith and Western education.' (Page 5)

questions.stem: Trade associations perform all of the following except
questions.explanation: Trade associations enforced rules and disciplined members, not exploited them.

questions.stem: In pre-colonial Hausa states, which group was most often relegated to tending and harvesting agricultural crops?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'In the Hausa states, the peoples most often relegated to the tending and harvesting of agricultural crops were captives.'

questions.stem: Women could not be ordained as bishops/prophetesses in the _________
questions.explanation: Study Session 4 states that women were ordained as clergy in the Church of the Lord, Aladura; recognized as prophetesses in C&S and CCC congregations; and as Lady Evangelists in CAC Churches. However, the Catholic Church does not ordain women as bishops.

questions.stem: The National Youth Service Corps Scheme was initiated to promote ________
questions.explanation: The NYSC was created to promote national integration and unity among Nigerian youth.

questions.stem: The ethnic Ijaw are concentrated mainly in the following states:
questions.explanation: The Ijaw people are predominantly found in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria, with significant populations concentrated in Delta and Bayelsa states.

questions.stem: Who founded the Fresh Party and contested unsuccessfully for president in 2003 and 2007?
questions.explanation: The text states that 'Rev. Chris Okotie unsuccessfully contested twice (in 2003 and 2007) as a presidential aspirant on the ticket of the Fresh Party founded by him.'

questions.stem: Titles such as Erelu, Iyalode and Iyaloja were held by prominent
questions.explanation: The titles Erelu, Iyalode, and Iyaloja are traditionally associated with prominent Yoruba women, reflecting their significant roles in society.

questions.stem: The Ogbomoso Peoples Institute was formally opened in October 1938 with Eyo Ita as its __________
questions.explanation: Eyo Ita served as the first principal of the Ogbomoso Peoples Institute when it opened in 1938.

questions.stem: Among the Ijaw, what does it mean if a drowned person does not float?

options.B: The water spirit was holding him

questions.explanation: If an Ijaw drowned in water and did not float, it meant that the water spirit was holding him.

questions.stem: Lt-Col Odumegwu Ojukwu's interpretation of the Aburi agreements was ________
questions.explanation: Ojukwu interpreted the Aburi agreements as endorsing extreme decentralisation and greater autonomy for regions.

questions.stem: The text distinguishes between the 'old' and 'new' diaspora. What is the primary characteristic that defines the 'old' diaspora?

options.A: Africans who voluntarily migrated for economic opportunities post-independence.
options.B: People of African descent involuntarily shipped as slaves to Europe and the Americas.
options.C: Nigerians living abroad as professionals in the 21st century.
options.D: Descendants of African traders who settled in other African countries.

questions.explanation: The text defines 'Old' diaspora as 'people of African descent who were involuntarily shipped as slaves to Europe and the Americas from the fifteenth century to the mid-nineteenth century'.

questions.stem: The involvement of people in production naturally led to __________
questions.explanation: Production leads to surplus, which naturally leads to exchange and trade between communities.

questions.stem: In some parts of Igboland, it was an abomination for a free born to marry a/an ________
questions.explanation: In some parts of Igboland, it was an abomination for a free-born to marry an outcast (Osu).

questions.stem: Women made independent decisions to engage in both__________ which in turn brought prosperity to their family and local communities
questions.explanation: Women engaged in both local and long-distance trade, which brought prosperity to their families and communities.

questions.stem: From which site were the remains of the earliest Homo Sapiens in West Africa excavated?
questions.explanation: The text explicitly states that the remains of the earliest Homo Sapiens in West Africa were excavated at Iwo Eleru in Ondo State.

questions.stem: According to Johnson's description, what was a notable characteristic of Yoruba Calabash dressers in the nineteenth century?

options.A: They exclusively made musical instruments from calabashes.
options.B: They were always found in rows in market places, plying their trade, tracing or cutting all sorts of geometrical figures.
options.C: Their primary craft was dyeing calabashes for textile production.
options.D: They only worked for the royal family, creating decorative pieces.

questions.explanation: The text quotes Johnson: 'Calabash dressers are always found in a row in market places, plying their trade; all sorts of geometrical figures are traced or cut in calabashes; some designs are exquisitely beautiful.'

questions.stem: Who was the first Muslim ruler of the Seifawa dynasty in Kanem-Borno, marking the real process of Islamization in the 11th century?
questions.explanation: The document specifies, 'The real process of Islamizaton began in the 11th century, when Kanem produced the first Muslim ruler Umme Jilme (1075-85) of the Seifawa dynasty.'

questions.stem: What did inter-marriage ensure among different ethnic groups in pre-colonial Nigeria?

options.B: That groups remained linked to one another, fostering ties for generations
options.C: The elimination of all traditional customs

questions.explanation: The text states that inter-marriage 'ensured that different groups in the Nigerian area continued to be linked to one another, thus fostering ties for generations to come.'

questions.stem: The leadership of Kanem-Borno before the Shehu was called the
questions.explanation: Before the rise of the El-Kanemi dynasty and the establishment of the Shehu as the paramount ruler, the traditional title for the ruler of the Kanem-Borno Empire was 'Mai'. The Mai was an ancient title reflecting the historical roots of the kingdom.

questions.stem: Hausaland experienced the wave of Islamization during the reign of
questions.explanation: Sarki Rumfa of Kano, who reigned in the 15th century, played a pivotal role in consolidating and spreading Islam in Hausaland, introducing many Islamic administrative and social practices.

questions.stem: All except of one of the following were widespread in pre-jihad Hausaland _______.

options.A: The practice of pouring libations on rocks
options.C: The practice of venerating trees and rocks

questions.explanation: Before the Fulani Jihad (early 19th century), Hausaland was largely Islamic and animist. Christian missionary activities were not widespread until much later, primarily during the colonial era.

questions.stem: Who said, 'We are quelling a rebellion, not fighting an external enemy'?
questions.explanation: This famous statement was made by General Yakubu Gowon, the then Head of State of Nigeria, during the Nigerian Civil War (also known as the Biafran War, 1967-1970). It underscored the federal government's perspective that the conflict was an internal affair against secessionists.

questions.stem: Benjamin Nnamdi Azikiwe argued that education should ______.

options.A: Be first point of reforms in post-war reconstruction in British West Africa
options.B: Be used only in the church and religious assemblies
options.C: Be rejected in order to promote indigenous culture
options.D: Be given only to the Igbos and the Nupe

questions.explanation: Nnamdi Azikiwe, a prominent nationalist leader, strongly advocated for education as a crucial tool for socio-economic development and a primary area for reform in post-war reconstruction.

questions.stem: What was the title of the Kanuri king in Kanem-Borno?
questions.explanation: From Study Session 2, the text states: 'The Kanuri king was addressed as Mai.'

questions.stem: Among the Ibibio, specifically in Ikot Oku Nsit, how could a man symbolically choose a baby girl from a pregnant woman to be his future marriage partner?

options.A: By gifting the pregnant woman a special wrapper.
options.B: By drawing a circle with white chalk on her belly and tying a piece of raffia to the baby's hand if it's a girl.
options.C: By presenting a dowry to the pregnant woman's family in advance.
options.D: By performing a naming ceremony for the unborn child.

questions.explanation: The text explains: 'if a man wishes to marry from a particular family and could not find a grown up girl, he could approach a pregnant woman from that family and draw a circle with a white chalk on her belly. Should a baby girl be born, a piece of raffia would be tied to the baby's hand signifying the choice of the girl as a marriage partner.'

questions.stem: The concept of 'the Bible and the Plough' was adopted by the Christian missions to promote ________

options.A: Training of artisans to produce farm tools
options.B: Production of enough ploughs for farming

questions.explanation: 'The Bible and the Plough' was a missionary concept that combined evangelism with agricultural development. Missionaries promoted both Christian education and farming skills as part of their civilizing mission.

questions.stem: One of these cities was not established as a major trado-cultural centre _______
questions.explanation: Kaduna was a colonial administrative city, not a traditional cultural centre.

questions.stem: According to Ely Chinoy, what does the ideological component of culture encompass?

options.B: Only economic systems and trade practices
options.C: A varied and complex array of social phenomena
options.D: Only political ideologies and governance structures

questions.explanation: The text quotes Ely Chinoy stating that the ideological component 'encompasses a varied and complex array of social phenomena,' not just one narrow aspect.

questions.stem: What was the major organ of government among the Igbo called?
questions.explanation: From Study Session 2, the text states: 'the council of elders called Amala was the major organ of government in this area.'

questions.stem: A dependent economy is characterized as which of the following?
questions.explanation: A dependent economy, particularly in the context of post-colonial nations, is often described as 'disarticulated'. This means its various sectors are not well-integrated or balanced, often serving external interests (e.g., exporting raw materials) rather than internal development needs.

questions.stem: All of the following except one facilitated British conquest of Eastern Nigeria

options.A: The collaborative efforts of some Igbo leaders

questions.explanation: The British conquest was facilitated by strategic factors like superior weaponry, disunity among local communities, and sometimes collaboration from local leaders. Divine assistance is not a recognized historical factor.

questions.stem: A major reason given for the Fulani Jihad of 1804 was the level of

options.A: Syncretic practices among the Habe rulers
options.B: Religious experiences among the Habe rulers
options.C: Synthesis of the social system in Hausaland
options.D: Religious purity among the Habe rulers

questions.explanation: The Fulani Jihad led by Uthman Dan Fodio was primarily motivated by a desire to purify Islam in Hausaland, combating what he perceived as 'syncretic practices' (mixing Islamic beliefs with traditional African religions) among the Habe rulers and the populace.

questions.stem: What characterises an associational society in terms of social roles?
questions.explanation: Associational society is 'characterised by a marked division of labour and a proliferation of social roles' where individuals 'play many different and frequently unrelated roles.'

questions.stem: Which states make up the South East Zone of Nigeria?

options.A: Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Ondo, Osun, Ekiti
options.B: Edo, Delta, Bayelsa, Rivers, Cross River, Akwa Ibom
options.D: Kwara, Benue, Plateau, Niger, Nasarawa, Kogi

questions.explanation: The text lists Anambra, Enugu, Imo, Ebonyi, and Abia States as comprising the South East Zone.

questions.stem: According to the text, why did the British colonial administration maintain an outright hostility to industrialisation in Nigeria?

options.A: They lacked the technological expertise to develop industries in the colony.
options.B: Industrialisation would have competed with British industries and reduced the supply of raw materials for export.
options.C: The colonial administration prioritized agricultural development exclusively.
options.D: They believed industrialisation was not suitable for tropical climates.

questions.explanation: The text explains: 'Thus, industrialisation of the colony would have defeated the basic aims of conquest and colonisation. Raw materials produced by Nigerian farmers and the mineral products of the colony would not have been readily available for export as they would have been used mostly to feed the home industries. Besides, industries in the colony would have produced substitutes for imported industrial products and consumables.'

questions.stem: How many Northern States had adopted the Sharia legal system by the time the document was written?
