questions.explanation: Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other Ogoni activists were executed on November 10, 1995, by the military government of General Sani Abacha.

questions.stem: By what century had Islam become indigenous to many peoples in the Nigerian area?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'Islam had not always been indigenous to many of the peoples in the Nigerian area until the nineteenth century.' The ITQ in the document confirms answer B (19th century).

questions.stem: The pre-colonial labour system in many communities in Nigeria did not attract __________
questions.explanation: Pre-colonial labour was communal and did not attract wages or remuneration.

questions.stem: A major reaction to the OAU suggestion of peaceful settlement of the Nigerian crisis during the civil war by the Biafran delegation in 1968 was to ________
questions.explanation: The Biafran delegation staged a walkout from the OAU peace conference in 1968, rejecting the suggestion of a peaceful settlement.

questions.stem: What is the relationship between the individual and culture according to the text?

options.A: Individuals are born with complete cultural knowledge
options.B: Culture is instilled into the mind of the young by education, intuition, and long unconscious conditioning
options.C: Individuals create their own culture completely independently
options.D: Culture has no influence on individual development

questions.explanation: The text states culture 'is instilled into the mind of the young not only by education and intuition but also by the long unconscious conditioning whereby each individual becomes the person he ultimately is.'

questions.stem: The Tripoli-Fezzan-Bilma trans-Saharan trade route ended in
questions.explanation: The Tripoli-Fezzan-Bilma route connected North Africa to the Lake Chad region, ending in the Kanem-Borno Empire.

questions.stem: How was Samuel Ajayi Crowther's death described in relation to white CMS agents?

options.B: As covered by a 'cloud of persecution and humiliation'
options.C: As a martyrdom for the faith
options.D: As a natural death at old age

questions.explanation: The text states: 'Crowther's death was said to have been covered by a 'cloud of persecution and humiliation' from white CMS agents after he had served the mission for almost five decades.'

questions.stem: Nigeria has reached a situation of _______

options.A: The budding of the culture of corruption
options.C: The prevalence of the culture of corruption

questions.explanation: Nigeria has reached a situation of the prevalence of the culture of corruption.

questions.stem: What impact has the emphasis on the petroleum sector had on industrialisation in post-colonial Nigeria, according to the text?

options.A: It generated significant linkage effects, boosting local industrial growth.
options.B: It diverted the attention of the ruling elite from the necessity of industrialisation.
options.C: It led to a self-sufficient economy, reducing reliance on metropolitan countries.
options.D: It enabled Nigeria to refine all its crude oil domestically.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'Expansion of oil production has not generated any linkage effect, for example on industrialisation. On the contrary, the emphasis on petroleum has diverted the attention of the ruling elite from the necessity of industrialisation.'

questions.stem: What happens to the role of religion in everyday life in associational societies according to the general pattern?
questions.explanation: The text states that in associational societies, 'the role of religion in everyday life wanes gradually' as part of the general pattern of secularisation.

questions.stem: The Brazilian returnees settled mainly in __________
questions.explanation: Brazilian returnees settled mainly in Lagos and Abeokuta in the 19th century.

questions.stem: In its broadest form, how does the text define society?

options.A: Only large nations with defined borders
options.B: Any kind of relationship entered into by man, whether inclusive or exclusive

questions.explanation: The text defines society in its broadest form as 'any kind of relationship entered into by man whether inclusive or exclusive, organised or unorganised, direct or indirect, conscious or unconscious, cooperative or antagonistic.'

questions.stem: How did Pentecostals describe mainstream churches in the 1980s?

options.B: As 'dead' congregations with no power and anointing
options.C: As the most faithful to scripture
options.D: As true successors of the apostles

questions.explanation: The text states that 'in the 1980s, they [Pentecostals] derided mainstream churches as 'dead' congregations with no power and anointing.'

questions.stem: The culture of corruption is established when _______

options.B: A people accept corruption as a way of life

questions.explanation: Study Session 15 states that when people perceive corruption as a way of life, then the culture of corruption is established in that society. If corruption becomes the rule rather than the exception, the society can be said to have embraced the culture of corruption.

questions.stem: The two major anti-corruption agencies in Nigeria are:
questions.explanation: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) and the Independent Corrupt Practices and other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) are Nigeria's primary agencies responsible for investigating and prosecuting corruption-related offenses. APC and PDP are political parties, while NAPTIP focuses on human trafficking.

questions.stem: Among the Tiv, what does the husband do to shame the family if the bride is not a virgin?

options.B: He sends a block of moulded salt with a hole or a cloth with a hole to her family
options.C: He demands double the bride price back

questions.explanation: He buys a small block of moulded salt, makes a hole in it, or uses a piece of cloth with a hole at the centre, and sends it to the girl's family as a sign of shame and loss.

questions.stem: What is the first stage of the Yoruba marriage process, involving background checks on the prospective wife?
questions.explanation: Ifojusode is the stage where the suitor's family investigates the background of the prospective wife to ensure no hereditary ailments or problems.

questions.stem: What happens during the Igalia wedding feast when the bride disappears?

options.B: The groom organizes a search party and must pay a demanded amount to her friends
options.C: The bride's father returns the bride price

questions.explanation: The groom searches for the bride, and her friends demand a certain amount of money that the husband must pay before she leaves with him.

questions.stem: Which theorist described culture as a 'complex whole which includes knowledge, beliefs, art, morals, customs and other capabilities acquired by man as a member of society'?
questions.explanation: The text explicitly attributes this definition to E.B. Taylor, distinguishing it from the definitions provided by Kluckhohn, Igbo, and Chinoy.

questions.stem: Of all the Baptist missionaries that worked in Ogbomoso, Reverend C. E. Smith had greater and lasting influence on __________
questions.explanation: Reverend C.E. Smith had a lasting influence on N.D. Oyerinde, who was his student.

questions.stem: What happens to the range of alternative patterns of behaviour in a communal society?

options.C: It is the same as in associational societies
options.D: It focuses only on economic choices

questions.explanation: The text states: 'the range of alternative patterns of behaviour open to individuals is inevitably restricted' in a communal society due to tradition and custom.

questions.stem: Which intra-Muslim crisis is cited as a 'classical case' and occurred in Kano in 1980?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'The Maitatsine riots of Kano in 1980 were another classical case of intra-Muslim crisis.'

questions.stem: Women have largely been ___ in Nigerian politics.
questions.explanation: Historically and contemporarily, women in Nigeria have faced significant barriers to political participation and have largely been marginalized in leadership and decision-making roles within the political landscape.

questions.stem: Most of the languages spoken in Nigeria are under the ___ group of languages.
questions.explanation: The Kwa group of languages is a major branch of the Niger-Congo language family, which includes many languages spoken in Nigeria, such as Yoruba and Igbo.

questions.stem: Who among these rulers was associated with the following programmes: DFFRI, MAMSER, NDE?
questions.explanation: These programmes (Directorate of Food, Roads and Rural Infrastructure, Mass Mobilization for Self-Reliance, Social Justice, and Economic Recovery, and National Directorate of Employment) were all initiated during the military regime of General Ibrahim Babangida.

questions.stem: During the elaborate fattening process among the Efik of James Town, what is tied over the door to prevent the wicked water spirit Ndem from entering?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'During this period, fresh palm leaves are tied over the door where the young girl resides to prevent wicked water spirit Ndem from entering.'

questions.stem: In all Nigerian communities mentioned, what is considered a great sacrilege?
questions.explanation: The text states that in all Nigerian communities, incest is a great sacrilege and different methods are used to deal with the offender.

questions.stem: The term 'diaspora' is derived from the Greek word 'diaorropa'. What does 'diaorropa' mean?
questions.explanation: According to Section 10.1 Introduction, the term 'diaspora' is derived from the Greek word diaorropa, which means 'scattering or dispersion'.

questions.stem: What was the major challenge of the Better Life Programme?

options.C: Neglect of all members of the society

questions.explanation: The Better Life Programme was criticized for neglecting urban middle-class women.

questions.stem: Before the colonization of Nigeria, the different peoples and empires:

options.A: Were already existing as federal republic of Nigeria.
options.B: Were members of the Ecowas and African Union.
options.C: Organised their production to meet their basic subsistence needs of food, clothing and shelter.
options.D: Had been waiting for the Europeans to come and teach them how to manage their economy.

questions.explanation: The text mentions, 'before the colonization of Nigeria, the different peoples and empires organised their production to meet their basic subsistence needs of food, clothing and shelter.'

questions.stem: In which state of Nigeria are the Affade ethnic group found?
questions.explanation: The Affade (Bade) ethnic group is found in Borno State, Nigeria.

questions.stem: The Ebenezer Baptist Church was founded in Lagos in _______
questions.explanation: Study Session 4 explicitly states that the Ebenezer Baptist Church was founded in Lagos in 1888. It was one of the splinter groups established by Nigerians seeking African leadership in the church.

questions.stem: The leadership of the Church of God Mission, Benin is headed by ___________
questions.explanation: Bishop Margaret Idahosa is the head of the Church of God Mission in Benin.

questions.stem: One effect of corruption in Nigeria is _____.
questions.explanation: Corruption undermines democratic processes. One of its most direct effects on elections is vote buying, manipulation of results, and other illicit practices that lead to election rigging, thereby compromising the integrity of the electoral system.

questions.stem: Queen Amina of Zaria was most important as a __________
questions.explanation: Queen Amina is historically known as a formidable warrior and military leader who expanded the Zaria kingdom.

questions.stem: From approximately what century did Fulani clans begin migrating out of their original homeland?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'Those of the Fulani who inherited the pastoral and nomadic legacy of their forebears began to migrate out of the River Senegal valley region from about the twelfth century.'

questions.stem: The 'old' diaspora, as defined in the text, primarily refers to people of African descent who were involuntarily shipped as slaves during which historical period?
questions.explanation: Page 4 defines: "'Old' diaspora refers to people of African descent who were involuntarily shipped as slaves to Europe and the Americas from the fifteenth century to the mid-nineteenth century..."

questions.stem: African Indigenous Churches sometimes derided mainline Churches for being _________

options.C: Dead congregations with no power and anointing

questions.explanation: Pentecostal and African Indigenous Churches criticized mainline churches as being spiritually 'dead' and lacking power.

questions.stem: What was the earliest tool created and used by man mentioned in the text?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'The earliest tool created and used by man was made of stone, for example, the stone axe followed by bronze and iron implements.'

questions.stem: The Brazilian returnees who settled in Nigeria mainly influenced the homeland in the area of:
questions.explanation: According to the text, 'The Brazilian returnees settled mainly in Lagos and Abeokuta. Their influence was essentially in the area of culture and social development.' (Page 4)

questions.stem: In pre-colonial manpower development, how did boys typically acquire skills for occupational development?

options.A: They attended formal schools established by the community leaders.
options.B: They were sent to live with other men as apprentices or took to their fathers' occupations.
options.C: They learned through trial and error, without formal guidance.
options.D: Skills were primarily inherited through spiritual means.

questions.explanation: The document explains: "In most cases, boys were brought up to take to their father's occupation. In some other cases, they were sent to live with other men as apprentices to learn various vocations and life etiquette."

questions.stem: What significant cultural event did the African returnees from Brazil introduce to Lagos and its environs?
questions.explanation: Section 10.3 states: 'The African returnees from Brazil also introduced the Brazilian carnival to Lagos and its environs.'

questions.stem: Who founded the first secondary school in Nigeria, the CMS Grammar School, Bariga, Lagos, established in 1859?
questions.explanation: The text clearly states: 'the first secondary school in Nigeria, the CMS Grammar School, Bariga, Lagos, which was established in 1859, was founded by Thomas Babington Macaulay, an Anglican clergyman who had been trained in Sierra Leone and England.' (Page 6)

questions.stem: According to the text, what do people express when they approve or disapprove of a conduct such as indecent dressing?

options.B: Their shared values from the ideological component

questions.explanation: The text states: 'When people approve or disapprove of a conduct as earlier noted in the case of indecent dressing, they are simply expressing this shared value' from the ideological component.

questions.stem: The title Amirul Mumineen, meaning 'leader of the faithful,' was widely acknowledged for which ruler during the peak of Islamization in Borno (1570-1602)?
questions.explanation: The text notes, 'The islamization of Borno reached its peak during the reign of Mai Idris Alooma (1570-1602), who was widely acknowledged as the Amirul Mumineen (leader of the faithful).'

questions.stem: Who lost his bid for Vice-President in 2011 on the platform of the Congress for Progressive Change (CPC)?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'Tunde Bakare also lost his bid for the post of Vice-President in 2011 on the platform of the Congress for Progressive Change [CPC].'

questions.stem: The backbone of the colonial economy was __________
questions.explanation: Agriculture was the backbone of the colonial economy, providing raw materials for export.

questions.stem: What was the name of the son born to Bayajjida and the Queen of Daura?
questions.explanation: The text states that the union between Bayajjida and the Queen of Daura 'produced a son called Bawo,' whose six sons established the six core Hausa states.

questions.stem: What does the name 'Boko Haram' literally mean in the Hausa language, as described in the text?
questions.explanation: The document clearly states, '‘Boko Haram’in Hausa language simply means ‘Western education is forbidden.’'

questions.stem: Among the Ibibio, why is a child's body mutilated if the child dies?
questions.explanation: The Ibibio believe that no child or young person dies without enemy or spirit involvement, and mutilation prevents the child's re-incarnation.

questions.stem: The Nigerian Civil War ended in
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Civil War officially ended in January 1970 with the surrender of Biafran forces.

questions.stem: All the following played noticeable roles in the introduction of American education in Nigeria except
questions.explanation: Nnamdi Azikiwe, N.D. Oyerinde, and Eyo Ita were all prominent figures who studied in the United States and significantly influenced the development and introduction of American educational models and philosophies in Nigeria. Clement Isong, while an important figure in Nigerian history (e.g., as Governor of the Central Bank), is not typically associated with the direct introduction of American education.

questions.stem: Which of these materials is required in naming a child among the Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Honey is traditionally used in Yoruba naming ceremonies as a symbol of sweetness and good fortune.

questions.stem: How is chastity before marriage traditionally tested among the Fulani, as mentioned in the text?

options.A: The bride must pass a public interrogation by the village elders.
options.B: A white sheet is spread on the bed on the first night, and its staining with blood signifies purity.
options.C: The bride undergoes a spiritual cleansing ritual to prove her innocence.
options.D: The groom’s family observes the bride’s behavior during courtship for any suspicious signs.

questions.explanation: The text explicitly states: 'On the first night of the marriage, a white sheet would be spread on the bed. If it is stained with blood, the bride and her family would be highly respected, for that implies that the lady was not defiled before marriage.'

questions.stem: The Jihad against the Habe rulers in the early 19th century was led by _________
questions.explanation: Shehu Usman dan Fodio led the Fulani Jihad against the Habe rulers, resulting in the establishment of the Sokoto Caliphate.

questions.stem: The leadership of Kanem-Borno before the Shehu was called
questions.explanation: The rulers of the Kanem-Borno Empire were traditionally known as 'Mai' before the rise of the Shehu dynasty. The titles Sultan and Emir are more commonly associated with other Islamic caliphates and emirates.

questions.stem: The manhood test for marriage amongst the Hausa is called ________ ?
questions.explanation: Study Session 5 states that among the Fulani, marriage is a rigorous process and a young man must pass the manhood test called sharo. This is also practiced among the Hausa.

questions.stem: Colonialism freed women from domestic violence by introducing and enforcing some laws at the district and provincial courts under the
questions.explanation: The British colonial administration in Nigeria largely operated through the system of Indirect Rule, where existing local structures were utilized, though often modified, to implement colonial policies, including changes to customary law regarding women's rights.

questions.stem: Despite regional differences, how did traditional or indigenous education among groups like the Yoruba, Hausa, and Igbo primarily equip individuals?

options.A: To compete aggressively for individual economic success.
options.B: To fit usefully into their society and achieve self-sustenance.
options.C: To challenge existing political leaders and promote dissent.
options.D: To defeat foreign invaders with superior military tactics.

questions.explanation: The text mentions, 'traditional or indigenous education among people especially the Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo equipped individuals to fit usefully into their society. Youths learnt and professionalized different skills for self-sustenance while contributing to kinship and the development of their societies.'

questions.stem: Urbanization in colonial cities in Nigeria led to increase in all but one of the following ______.
questions.explanation: Colonial urbanization led to the development of infrastructure like railroads for transport, as well as modern amenities such as cinema houses and hotels for entertainment and accommodation. Adire fabrics, while a significant part of Nigerian culture and commerce, are a traditional craft whose production wasn't primarily driven by or exclusively increased by colonial urbanization in the same way as the other options.

questions.stem: What did the British do to the Arochukwu shrine at the beginning of colonial rule?

options.A: They preserved it as a heritage site
options.C: They converted it to a church

questions.explanation: From Study Session 2, the text states: 'one of the earliest measures taken by the colonial authorities was the destruction of the Arochukwu shrine.'

questions.stem: Diaspora refers to the physical and cultural presence of Nigerians __________
questions.explanation: Diaspora refers to Nigerians living outside Nigeria, maintaining cultural and physical connections to their homeland.

questions.stem: The Federal Government's use of 'police action' during the Nigerian civil war was to ________

options.B: Make Ojukwu leader of the Eastern Region

questions.explanation: The Federal Government's use of 'police action' was aimed at capturing Ojukwu and ending the secession of Biafra. This military campaign was designed to reunify Nigeria.

questions.stem: Non-material contributions of parents to new couples could include:
questions.explanation: Non-material contributions refer to support that is not monetary or tangible goods. Prayers for blessings are a common and significant non-material contribution from parents, offering spiritual and moral support to new couples for a successful marriage. Cash, jewelry, and food are all material contributions.

questions.stem: In pre-colonial Nigerian societies, economic activities were primarily carried out with the intention of:

options.A: Generating huge monetary profits for individuals.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'Economic activities were carried out with the intention of widening social relationships, rather than making money.' This highlights the communal and social orientation of the pre-colonial economic system.

questions.stem: Some of the earliest 'Nigerian Native Pentecostal Churches' included the _______
questions.explanation: Study Session 4 states that the second half of the twentieth century saw the growth and explosion of indigenous Pentecostal churches such as the Redeemed Christian Church of God, Deeper Life Christian Ministry, Church of God Missions, Living Faith Ministries, etc. The others are earlier African or Native Churches from the late 19th century.

questions.stem: Who expanded western education to the nooks and crannies of the Nigerian area?
questions.explanation: The text states that 'the colonial government later expanded [western education] to the nooks and crannies of the Nigerian area.'

questions.stem: How did inter-marriage solidify relationships between different ethnic groups?

options.B: Through marital ties that linked groups across generations

questions.explanation: The text states: 'marital ties solidified relationships between and among different groups... fostering ties for generations to come.'

questions.stem: Which is a major aspect of corruption in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Nepotism, or favoring family and friends, is a major form of corruption in Nigeria.

questions.stem: When was the concept of remuneration (wages) for labour introduced into the Nigerian economy?

options.A: During the pre-colonial era with the rise of wealthy farmers.
options.B: With the development of local markets and inter-town trade.
options.C: With the coming of British colonial policies in the twentieth century.
options.D: As part of the indigenous education system for skill acquisition.

questions.explanation: The text explicitly states: 'The introduction of remuneration for labour came with the coming of the British colonial policies in the twentieth century.'

questions.stem: Which Hausa state rose to prominence at the beginning of the eighteenth century and crushed Zamfara in 1762?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'Gobir rose to prominence at the beginning of the eighteenth century and in 1762 inflicted a crushing defeat on Zamfara to become the most powerful Hausa state.'

questions.stem: Which of the following would be considered part of the ideological component of culture?

options.A: The stone axe used for hunting
options.C: The belief that hard work is virtuous
options.D: The technique for building a house

questions.explanation: The ideological component refers to ideas, beliefs, and values. The belief that hard work is virtuous is a value or idea. The stone axe is technological, respecting elders is sociological, and house-building techniques are technological.

questions.stem: In the pre-colonial period, people kept large families in order to __________

options.A: Prepare for war against their enemies
options.B: Compete as the biggest family in their town

questions.explanation: Large families were kept to ensure adequate labour supply for farming and other activities.

questions.stem: What hindered gender solidarity amongst women following independence? Select one:
questions.explanation: Following independence, divisions along political party lines, religious beliefs, and ethnic identities often overshadowed the potential for a unified women's movement, thereby hindering gender solidarity.

questions.stem: Which type of organization typically fights human trafficking, child abuse, and domestic violence in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) play a crucial role in advocating for human rights, providing support to victims, and raising awareness about issues such as human trafficking, child abuse, and domestic violence in Nigeria. They often work independently or in collaboration with government agencies to address these societal challenges.

questions.stem: During the military era in Nigeria, the Christian church demonstrated willingness not to _________

options.C: Protest the violation of human rights
options.D: Assist the government in the persecution of Christians

questions.explanation: The Christian church was active in opposing undemocratic governments and protecting human rights, not assisting in persecution.

questions.stem: Muhammed Shitta Bey, a Muslim Creole, made a significant contribution in the 1890s by financing the construction of what in Lagos?
questions.explanation: The document highlights: "Prominent among these was Muhammed Shitta Bey, a Muslim Creole who gave a whopping 400 pounds for the building of a mosque in Lagos in the 1890s."

questions.stem: One obstacle to administrative and political unitarism in Nigeria is the country’s which of the following?
questions.explanation: Nigeria's vast 'heterogeneity' (diversity in terms of ethnicity, language, religion, and culture) is a significant obstacle to achieving complete administrative and political unitarism, as different groups often have competing interests and identities.

questions.stem: One impact of Nigerian Pentecostalism on females is that it has gradually

options.A: Broken the yoke of men 's control of church finances
options.B: Broken religious barriers that hitherto hindered women 's rise to leadership positions

questions.explanation: Nigerian Pentecostalism has often been associated with a more egalitarian approach to gender roles within the church, allowing women to break traditional barriers and ascend to leadership positions that were previously closed off to them in older, more conservative denominations.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an exception to the general pattern of associational societies noted in the Nigerian context?

options.A: The role of religion in Nigerian cities is increasing rather than decreasing
options.B: Nigerian cities have no division of labour
options.C: Family ties are stronger in Nigerian cities than in rural areas
options.D: There is no formal regulation in Nigerian cities

questions.explanation: The text notes: 'Yet we know that the role of religion in Nigerian cities is increasing rather than decreasing, indicating that there are variations in this broad category of society.'

questions.stem: Which ethnic group encouraged the groom family to entertain both families at the point of marriage?
questions.explanation: The text explicitly states that the groom's family entertains during Igala marriage rites, not the Yoruba.

questions.stem: A unique aspect of marriage among the Igala is that, unlike other Nigerian communities where the bride's family entertains, whose family traditionally entertains everybody?

options.C: The eldest family in the village.
options.D: Both families contribute equally to the entertainment.

questions.explanation: The text notes: 'Among the Igala, it is the family of the man that entertains everybody. They bring all necessary things from firewood, food items, plates, cups and spoons to the bride's family.'

questions.stem: Lt-Col Odumegwu Ojukwu's interpretation of the Aburi agreements was characterized by which of the following?
questions.explanation: Lt-Col Odumegwu Ojukwu, representing the Eastern Region of Nigeria, strongly advocated for extreme decentralization or confederalism during the Aburi Accord negotiations in 1967. He sought significant autonomy for the regions, which contrasted with the federal government's desire for a stronger central authority. His interpretation contributed to the political tensions leading to the Nigerian Civil War.

questions.stem: While men dominated Christian services in various churches and denominations, _________.

options.C: Young men managed the affairs of the house
options.D: Women played key roles in the traditional religion

questions.explanation: The document indicates 'Q83. While men dominated Christian services in various churches and denominations, D. Women played key roles in the traditional religion ✓'. This highlights a contrast: despite the male dominance in many Christian settings, women historically held significant and often powerful positions within indigenous traditional religious practices in Nigeria.

questions.stem: What was the most prominent integrative mechanism among the disparate Igbo communities?

options.C: The Arochukwu oracle called Ibinu Ukpabi
options.D: The Umuada daughters of the land

questions.explanation: The text states: 'The most prominent in this regard was the oracle among the Aro called Ibinu Ukpabi, generally referred to as the Arochukwu oracle.'

questions.stem: __________ is credited as the ancestor of the Hausa?
questions.explanation: Bayajidda is the legendary figure credited as the ancestor of the Hausa states.

questions.stem: Which Christian woman distinguished herself as Director-General of NAFDAC and Minister of Information?
questions.explanation: The text lists 'Professor (Mrs.) Dora Akunyili (former Director-General of the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration, and former Federal Minister of Information)' as a Christian woman in public service.

questions.stem: Which of the following constituted the major source of manpower in virtually every facet of productive exercise in pre-colonial Nigerian communities?

options.B: Slaves acquired through trade and raids.
options.C: The family unit, especially women with many children.

questions.explanation: The text explicitly mentions, 'The family unit was a major source of manpower in virtually every facet of productive exercise. Labour was mostly supplied by women, especially those who had been privileged to have many children.'

questions.stem: The major religious insurgency that affected Nigeria since 2009 was caused by the activities of the __________
questions.explanation: Study Session 6 notes that in July 2009, a sect known as Boko Haram went on a rampage in Bauchi, which later spread to neighboring states. The group was believed to have been established in 2002 by Mohammed Yusuf in Maiduguri. This marks the major insurgency from that period.

questions.stem: In which pre-colonial religion did women play key roles in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Women played important roles in traditional religions as priestesses, mediums, and in various cults.

questions.stem: Who is credited with establishing the Boko Haram group and in which city was it believed to have been established?

options.A: Shehu Usman dan Fodio in Sokoto

questions.explanation: The text indicates: 'The group was believed to have been established in 2002 by one Muhammed Yusuf in Maiduguri, Borno State.'

questions.stem: In the Yoruba marriage tradition, what do the symbolic items of sugar and honey represent during the Idana ceremony?
questions.explanation: According to the text, during the Idana ceremony among the Yoruba, 'The sugar and honey symbolize happiness in marriage'.

questions.stem: How did the various peoples and empires in Nigeria organize their production before colonial rule?

options.A: They focused primarily on export-oriented cash crops.
options.B: They were waiting for Europeans to teach them economic management.
options.C: They organized production to meet basic subsistence needs like food, clothing, and shelter.
options.D: They established a federal republic with a centralized economic plan.

questions.explanation: The text explicitly states: 'You must remember, that before the colonization of Nigeria, the different peoples and empires organised their production to meet their basic subsistence needs of food, clothing and shelter.'

questions.stem: What constitutional section was included as a compromise for Christians in the Nigerian Constitution, stating that 'the government of the Federation or a State shall not adopt any religion as a State religion'?
questions.explanation: The document explains the compromise: 'a sort of compromise was reached with the Muslims having Section 275 which recognizes a Sharia Court of Appeal and the Christians having Section 10 which states that ‘the government of the Federation or a State shall not adopt any religion as a State religion.'

questions.stem: Which of these was a limitation of pre-colonial traditional education in Nigeria, as identified in the document?

options.A: It lacked a strong emphasis on character development.
options.B: It did not provide vocational training for specialized skills.
options.C: The absence of writing meant reliance on memory, leading to potential loss of knowledge if custodians died.
options.D: It discouraged communal learning in favor of individual instruction.

questions.explanation: The text notes: "However, it had its limitations. For example, in the absence of writing, people depended on the power of their memory to retain and transmit all learned ideas to future generations. However, memory could fail, and when a custodian of some useful information or skill died, all was lost."

questions.stem: Benjamin Nnamdi Azikiwe argued that education should __________

options.A: Be given only to the Igbos and the Nupe
options.B: Be rejected in order to promote indigenous culture
options.C: Be used only in the church and religious assemblies
options.D: Be first point of reforms in post-war reconstruction in British West Africa

questions.explanation: Azikiwe believed education was fundamental and should be the starting point for post-war reconstruction and development.

questions.stem: Which pre-colonial manufacturing product from Northern Nigeria and Mali was described as superior to any in the world by the fifteenth century?
questions.explanation: The text explicitly states: 'For example, leather works from Northern Nigeria and Mali were superior to any in the world by the fifteenth century.'

questions.stem: Political Economy as a discipline or method of inquiry recognizes

options.A: The primacy of the economy and material production as the foundation of society
options.B: The gross capital expenditures as the basis for development
options.C: The exploitation of one group by another powerful group
options.D: The monopolization of means of production in the hands of the lower class

questions.explanation: Political Economy is an academic discipline that studies the interrelationships between individuals, society, and markets. It fundamentally recognizes the central role of economic activity and material production in shaping social structures and political power.

questions.stem: According to the document, when did religion become a serious source of conflict in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'We must emphasise that religion was not a serious source of conflict in Nigeria until the late 1970s.' This indicates that it *became* a serious source of conflict *after* this period.

questions.stem: The political economy of colonialism was __________
questions.explanation: Study Session 9 states that the political economy of colonialism was exploitative, through and through. The economy was structured and organized to feed Britain with raw materials and to serve as a dumping ground for her industrial goods.

questions.stem: What does the text say about the changes in Nigerian Christianity?

options.A: They have been random and unexplained
options.B: They have been historically conditioned, reflecting responses to local and foreign stimuli
options.C: They have been dictated by Rome
options.D: They have been uniform across all denominations

questions.explanation: The text states that changes in Nigerian Christianity 'have also been historically conditioned, reflecting the evolution of various expressions of the faith in response to both local and foreign stimuli.'

questions.stem: What were the 'Umuada' or 'Umuokpu' among the Igbo, and what function did they serve?

options.A: Male warriors who defended the village
options.B: Daughters of the land who maintained contact with their homeland and helped settle disputes
options.C: Age grades that carried out development projects
options.D: Oracle priests who judged legal cases

questions.explanation: The text states: 'Umuada or Umuokpu (daughters of the land), who although now married, also maintained frequent contacts with their homeland. The 'Umuada' were especially useful in the settlement of family and community disputes.'

questions.stem: How does Nigeria's cultural policy officially define culture?

options.A: The artistic expressions of a people including music and dance
options.B: The political system evolved by a community for governance
options.C: The totality of the way of life evolved by a people to meet environmental challenges
options.D: The economic activities that sustain a population

questions.explanation: The official Nigerian cultural policy states culture is 'the totality of the way of life evolved by a people in their attempt to meet the challenges of living in their environment.' Other options describe only subsets of culture.

questions.stem: Corruption could be categorised as all except _________
questions.explanation: Megalomania is a personality disorder, not a category of corruption.

questions.stem: The Obligation of the Princes was written for which Hausa leader?
questions.explanation: The Obligation of the Princes (Tajud-din) was a treatise written by Al-Maghili for Sarki Rumfa of Kano.

questions.stem: ________ was a common marriage practice among Cross River people?
questions.explanation: Study Session 5 states that among the Efik and Ibibio of Cross River area, fattening was a common marriage practice. This marked the passage from girlhood to womanhood and qualified the lady to marry.

questions.stem: According to the text, what does the phrase 'culture is dynamic' mean?

options.B: Culture changes continuously, shedding some features and acquiring new ones

questions.explanation: The text states culture 'changes continuously, shedding some features and acquiring new ones' as part of its dynamic nature, which contrasts with being static.

questions.stem: What was the primary function of the Moor Plantation established in Ibadan between 1912 and 1916?

options.A: To serve as a training center for British colonial administrators.
options.B: To cultivate exotic crops for export to Britain.
options.C: To serve as an experimentation station for the dissemination of technical knowledge to local farmers.
options.D: To function as a military base for suppressing local rebellions.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'The Moor Plantation was established in Ibadan between 1912 and 1916. The plantation was an experimentation station for the dissemination of technical knowledge to local farmers.'

questions.stem: According to the passage, what is the universal medium of cultural transmission?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'a major medium of transmission of culture which is universal is language which can either be written or spoken.'

questions.stem: Generally, __________ engaged in a variety of crafts such as dyeing, pottery, cosmetics, bead-making?
questions.explanation: Women were primarily engaged in crafts like dyeing, pottery, cosmetics, and bead-making in pre-colonial societies.

questions.stem: Urban culture includes the

options.B: Various practices, belief systems, social forms, etc. of city dwellers

questions.explanation: Urban culture is a broad concept encompassing all the distinctive ways of life, social interactions, norms, values, practices, and belief systems that characterize people living in cities, distinguishing them from rural populations.

questions.stem: Among the Igbo, what is the consequence if the bride price is not paid during a marriage?

options.A: The marriage is not recognized as traditional.
options.B: Any offspring from such a union would belong to the family of the girl.
options.C: The groom's family must perform additional services.
options.D: The bride must remain in her family home.

questions.explanation: The document states: 'If the bride price is not paid, any offspring from such a union would belong to the family of the girl.'

questions.stem: In Igbo naming ceremonies, what is the significance of names that begin with the prefix 'Chi-' (e.g., Chi-gozie, Chi-nyere, Chi-emeka)?

options.A: They indicate the order of birth, such as first or last child.
options.B: They refer to the market day on which the child was born.
options.C: They express connection or gratitude to God ('Chi' referring to God).
options.D: They signify a child born under unusual circumstances.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'In most communities, chi referring to God is used for names – Chi-gozie, God blesses, Chi-nyere God has given, Chi-emeka, God has done well.'

questions.stem: Urbanization in colonial cities in Nigeria led to increase in all but one of the following ________
questions.explanation: Adire fabrics (locally made) were already present and not an increase caused by colonial urbanization.

questions.stem: Among the Ibibio, what are twins named?
questions.explanation: The text states that among the Ibibio, twins are named Mfon.

questions.stem: 'Egba Omo Oduduwa', a pan-Yoruba organisation was formed 1945 in ________ ?
questions.explanation: The pan-Yoruba organization 'Egba Omo Oduduwa' was formed in London in 1945. This is a notable fact about Nigerian nationalist movements abroad.

questions.stem: The manhood test for marriage amongst the Hausa is called what?
questions.explanation: Amongst some Hausa sub-groups, particularly the Fulani, a traditional manhood test for marriage involving flogging is known as 'Sharo'.

questions.stem: According to the text, in pre-colonial Igbo marriage, what ritual was performed by the young lady upon arriving at her husband's house to address pre-marital chastity?

options.A: She would swear an oath of fidelity before the village elders.
options.B: She would offer sacrifices to the family god for a clean slate.
options.C: She was made to reveal all those with whom she had any intimate relationship since her betrothal before senior daughters of the village, followed by a fowl sacrifice.
options.D: She would undergo a purification bath witnessed by her new family.

questions.explanation: The text mentions: 'We must emphasise that during the pre-colonial period, as soon as the young lady came to her husband's house, she would be made to reveal all those with whom she had any intimate relationship since her betrothal. She would make such confessions before the senior daughters of the village, who would assemble for such a purpose, holding a fowl before the family god. The fowl was later killed for cleansing.'

questions.stem: Kaduna became the capital of Nigeria's former Northern Region in _________
questions.explanation: Study Session 13 states that Kaduna was founded by the British in 1913 to serve as its administrative headquarters in North Nigeria. It became the capital of Nigeria's former Northern Region in 1917.

questions.stem: Regarding the Efik (James Town) marriage customs, what is a notable characteristic of the second period of fattening mentioned in the text?

options.A: It is a short, week-long period focused on spiritual cleansing.
options.B: It brings the lady into womanhood and can last up to five years, depending on wealth, after which the bride price is paid.
options.C: It involves communal dancing and public displays of wealth.
options.D: It is solely for physical conditioning and diet control.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'You will note also that the second period of fattening brings the lady into womanhood. It would last up to five years depending on the wealth of the future husband or the family. After this, the bride price is paid and she would go with her husband.'

questions.stem: When was cultural nationalism embraced and nurtured within the Church in Nigeria?

options.B: Last quarter of the nineteenth century and opening decades of the twentieth century

questions.explanation: The text states: 'A significant milieu in the history of Nigerian Christianity was witnessed in the last quarter of the nineteenth century and opening decades of the twentieth century. This was the period when cultural nationalism was embraced and nurtured within the Church.'

questions.stem: Which of the following describes a pre-colonial chastity tradition in Igbo marriage?

options.A: The bride had to undergo a public vow of chastity.
options.B: The bride was made to confess all intimate relationships since her betrothal before senior daughters of the village.
options.C: A special cleansing ritual was performed by the groom's family to ensure chastity.
options.D: Only virgin brides were allowed to participate in the Igba Nkwụ.

questions.explanation: The text mentions: 'during the pre-colonial period, as soon as the young lady came to her husband's house, she would be made to reveal all those with whom she had any intimate relationship since her betrothal. She would make such confessions before the senior daughters of the village, who would assemble for such a purpose, holding a fowl before the family god.'

questions.stem: All except one of the following were widespread in pre-jihad Hausaland _______.

options.A: The practice of pouring libations on rocks
options.D: The practice of venerating trees and rocks

questions.explanation: Pre-jihad Hausaland was characterized by various indigenous religious practices, including polytheism, animism, and the veneration of natural objects. Christian missionary activities, however, only gained significant traction much later, primarily during the colonial period, and were not widespread in pre-jihad Hausaland.

questions.stem: According to Uche Nworah in 2005, a significant cultural challenge for the generation of Nigerians born in new lands, stemming from their parents maintaining cultural practices, is the issue of:
questions.explanation: Page 2 quotes Uche Nworah: "...the only problem is with the generation born in the new lands, who are torn with the issue of double identity."

questions.stem: The evidence of earliest human habitation in Nigeria came from the artifacts excavated in _____?
questions.explanation: Archaeological discoveries at Iwo-Eleru in Ondo State have yielded skeletal remains dating back over 11,000 years, providing some of the earliest evidence of anatomically modern human habitation in Nigeria.

questions.stem: On 30th May 1967, the independence of ________ was proclaimed.
questions.explanation: On May 30, 1967, Lt. Colonel Odumegwu Ojukwu proclaimed the independence of the Republic of Biafra from Nigeria, leading to the Nigerian Civil War.

questions.stem: In the pre-colonial times, several Nigerian communities comprised ________.
questions.explanation: Before colonialism, many Nigerian communities were largely agrarian and self-sufficient, relying on local resources and traditional practices for their sustenance and governance, rather than being part of large, interconnected urban or metropolitan systems.

questions.stem: Seclusion in purdah may
questions.explanation: Purdah is a practice of secluding women from public observation, often involving veiling and restricting their movement and interactions outside the home. By its very nature, seclusion limits women's autonomy, public participation, and overall freedom, rather than enhancing it or contributing to their empowerment or political involvement.

questions.stem: The two major anti-corruption agencies in Nigeria are?
questions.explanation: EFCC and ICPC are the two major anti-corruption agencies in Nigeria.

questions.stem: In the post-colonial period, the culture of corruption in Nigeria has _________

options.D: Spiraled to all segments of the Nigerian state

questions.explanation: Corruption has spiraled to all segments of Nigerian society in the post-colonial period.

questions.stem: What was the constitutional compromise reached in Nigeria regarding Sharia law and state religion, as described in the document?

options.A: Section 275 recognized a Sharia Court of Appeal, and Section 10 stated no state religion.
options.B: Sharia law was completely expunged from the Constitution.
options.C: All states were mandated to adopt Sharia law.
options.D: Only the Federal government could establish Sharia courts.

questions.explanation: The text explains: 'a sort of compromise was reached with the Muslims having Section 275 which recognizes a Sharia Court of Appeal and the Christians having Section 10 which states that 'the government of the Federation or a State shall not adopt any religion as a State religion.''

questions.stem: A major social effect of corruption is that it has not become a/an _________
questions.explanation: Study Session 15 states that corruption has become an irritating part of the culture of Nigerians and a curse on the nation. It is not a catalyst for growth; it hinders development.

questions.stem: Sarki Rumfa of Hausaland worked with a major chronicler named _________
questions.explanation: Study Session 6 states that during the reign of Sarki Rumfa (1463-1499), he requested the famous Algerian scholar, Abdul Karim Al-Maghilli to prepare a treatise for him to facilitate his administration.

questions.stem: What cultural phenomenon was introduced to Lagos and its environs by the Brazilian returnees, featuring music, dance, and exotic costumes?
questions.explanation: The African returnees from Brazil also introduced the Brazilian carnival to Lagos and its environs. The carnival featured music and dance with exotic costumes.

questions.stem: The ethnic Ijaw are concentrated mainly in the following states ________
questions.explanation: The Ijaw people are mainly concentrated in Delta and Bayelsa states.

questions.stem: The technological component of culture is also known as which of the following?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'The technological component otherwise called material culture, for instance, highlights the cumulative experience and innovations of a people.'

questions.stem: In most Nigerian communities, stealing was ________?
questions.explanation: Stealing was discouraged and condemned in most Nigerian communities.

questions.stem: Who described the towns and cities of Nigeria as "crucial nodes or swellings in the spatial economy"?
questions.explanation: Akin Mabogunje, a renowned Nigerian geographer, described cities as nodes in the spatial economy.

questions.stem: A dependent economy is A
questions.explanation: A dependent economy often refers to one that is externally oriented and lacks internal linkages, meaning its various sectors are not well-integrated to support domestic growth, thus being 'disarticulated'.

questions.stem: What was the primary aim of collecting tolls in pre-colonial Nigerian societies?

options.B: To regulate trade routes and ensure fair prices.
options.C: To generate revenues for public treasuries and private purses of chiefs.
options.D: To fund the education of youth in trade.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'The primary aim of collecting tolls was to have revenues. Public treasuries merged with the private purses of the chiefs: revenues were collected and spent to satisfy both private desires and public needs'.

questions.stem: Kanem-Borno's location at the terminus of which trade route facilitated its early trading relations and exposure to Islam?
questions.explanation: The document states, 'Situated at the terminus of the trans-Sahara trade route which ran from Tripoli through Fezzan and Bilma, the area had enjoyed considerable trading relations with merchants coming from North Africa.'

questions.stem: Which Mai of Kanem-Borno marked the apogee of the Kanuri state in the sixteenth century?
questions.explanation: From Study Session 2, the text states: 'The sixteenth century marked the apogee of the Kanuri state under Mai Idris Aloma, who died in c. 1603.'

questions.stem: The failure to successfully introduce Christianity to Nigeria in the initial period was due to all except _________

options.A: Concentration on the slave trade by the Europeans

questions.explanation: Arab missionaries were not involved in spreading Christianity; this is not a reason for its failure.

questions.stem: According to the text, was Islam originally indigenous to many Nigerian peoples before the nineteenth century?

options.B: No, it had not always been indigenous until the nineteenth century
options.D: The text does not address this

questions.explanation: The text explicitly states: 'Islam had not always been indigenous to many of the peoples in the Nigerian area until the nineteenth century.'

questions.stem: In Ikot Oku Nsit (Ibibio), how could a man signify his choice of a baby girl as a future marriage partner from a pregnant woman?

options.A: By tying a piece of raffia to the pregnant woman's wrist.
options.B: By drawing a circle with white chalk on the pregnant woman's belly.
options.C: By presenting gifts to the pregnant woman's family.
options.D: By performing a special dance for the pregnant woman.

questions.explanation: The document explains: 'if a man wishes to marry from a particular family and could not find a grown up girl, he could approach a pregnant woman from that family and draw a circle with a white chalk on her belly.'

questions.stem: What were the 'Umuada' or 'Umuokpu' among the Igbo known for?

options.B: Settlement of family and community disputes

questions.explanation: From Study Session 2, the text states: 'The 'Umuada' were especially useful in the settlement of family and community disputes.'

questions.stem: The cultural examination of a city explains its _______

options.C: Various cultural components and their relationship with one another

questions.explanation: The cultural examination of a city explains its various cultural components and their relationships.

questions.stem: Which states make up the South South Zone of Nigeria?

options.A: Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Ondo, Osun, Ekiti
options.B: Gombe, Bauchi, Yobe, Borno, Taraba, Adamawa
options.C: Edo, Delta, Bayelsa, Rivers, Cross River, Akwa Ibom

questions.explanation: The text lists Edo, Delta, Bayelsa, Rivers, Cross River, and Akwa Ibom States as comprising the South South Zone.

questions.stem: Gowon led Nigerians out of the civil war on the side of ________
questions.explanation: General Gowon fought to keep Nigeria as 'One Nigeria' during the civil war.

questions.stem: Nigeria emerged as one entity in the
questions.explanation: Modern Nigeria was formed in 1914 when the Northern and Southern Protectorates were amalgamated by Lord Lugard, creating a single colonial entity.

questions.stem: The death of a young person is usually ______.
questions.explanation: In most cultures, the death of a young person is considered a tragic event and is met with profound grief and mourning, as it represents a life cut short and unfulfilled potential.

questions.stem: The 'Creole' culture that emerged in Sierra Leone from the diverse peoples who settled there was a fusion of cultures that particularly embraced which two main aspects?

options.A: Traditional African religions and indigenous education

questions.explanation: The document describes: "The Creoles embraced the Christian faith and Western education."

questions.stem: What are the two broad types of societies identified by sociologists in the text?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'sociologists have come up with two types of societies in their broadest forms. They are communal and associational societies.'

questions.stem: Colonialism discriminated against Nigerians by encouraging _______
questions.explanation: Colonialism enforced segregated reservations for Europeans, separating them from African populations and promoting discrimination.

questions.stem: Among the Igbo, who has the privilege of naming a child?

options.B: The eldest man in the compound

questions.explanation: The privilege of naming a child is reserved for the eldest man in the compound among the Igbo.

questions.stem: A major reason given for the Fulani Jihad of 1804 was the level of _________

options.A: Religious experiences among the Habe rulers
options.B: Religious purity among the Habe rulers
options.C: Syncretic practices among the Habe rulers
options.D: Synthesis of the social system in Hausaland

questions.explanation: The jihad was launched against the syncretic practices of the Habe rulers, which mixed Islam with traditional beliefs.

questions.stem: The following church/ministry in Nigeria was not founded by a woman

options.B: The Daughters of Deborah International Ministry
options.C: The Redeemed Christian Church of God

questions.explanation: The Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG) was founded by Rev. Josiah Akindayomi, a man.

questions.stem: When crude oil export replaced agriculture in Nigeria, the culture of corruption also _________
questions.explanation: Study Session 15 states that when crude oil export replaced agriculture as the main foreign exchange earner, the culture of hard work was relegated and the new era of quick and easy money made some people lazy, cunning and corrupt. Corruption escalated.

questions.stem: Which Hausa state rose to prominence at the beginning of the eighteenth century?
questions.explanation: From Study Session 2, the text states: 'Gobir rose to prominence at the beginning of the eighteenth century and in 1762 inflicted a crushing defeat on Zamfara.'

questions.stem: Among the Yoruba, which items are offered for prayers during a naming ceremony?
questions.explanation: In naming a child among the Yoruba, items such as honey and kola are offered for prayers.

questions.stem: The sociological aspect of culture is otherwise called which of the following?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'The sociological aspect of culture, otherwise called institutions, relates to the rules or norms which govern behaviour.'

questions.stem: The concept of “autochthones” or “stateless societies” was used by British colonial scholars to describe Nigerian communities with ____ institutions?
questions.explanation: British colonial scholars often categorized Nigerian societies based on their political structures. 'Stateless societies' or 'autochthones' were terms used to describe communities, particularly in the Igbo and Tiv regions, that lacked a single, overarching centralized authority like a monarch or emir. Instead, they were governed by decentralized systems, such as councils of elders, age-grade associations, or lineage heads.

questions.stem: Which of these was the immediate consequence of adultery amongst the Hausa?
questions.explanation: Adultery in Hausa culture often resulted in divorce.

questions.stem: What ultimately resulted from economic specialization and inter-dependence among pre-colonial Nigerian ethnic groups?

options.C: Trade that made access to produce from other areas possible

questions.explanation: The text states that specialization and inter-dependence 'ultimately led to trade that made access to produce from other areas possible.'

questions.stem: Which Edo-speaking groups are mentioned as non-centralized societies with political administration at the town or village level?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'The Ishan, Ivbiosakon (Owan), Etsako in Edo State, and the Urhobo and Isoko in Delta State are now usually linguistically classified as Edo-speaking groups. Unlike the 'Edo proper,' however, these were non-centralized societies.'

questions.stem: In the traditional Nigerian society, those who engaged in corrupt acts were
questions.explanation: In traditional Nigerian society, corruption was frowned upon, and offenders were openly shamed.

questions.stem: Which pre-colonial element encouraged linguistic and economic interactions through population movement?
questions.explanation: The text states that 'the migration of people from one place to another encouraged linguistic and economic interactions' that contributed to cultural evolution.

questions.stem: Which action by General Ibrahim Babangida, mentioned in the text, indicated a setback in the fight against corruption?

options.A: Establishing the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC).
options.B: Freeing detained civilian governors and reversing the confiscation of ill-gotten properties.
options.C: Prioritizing economic growth sustainability and food security.
options.D: Intervening in Liberian and Sierra Leonean crises through ECOMOG.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'To win the support of the political elite, General Babangida freed all detained civilian governors of the Alhaji Shagari administration. Besides, he reversed the confiscation of the ill-gotten properties of the military governors of the General Gowon administration. But it turned out that General Babangida was simply paving the way for the looting of public wealth by him and members of his administration.'

questions.stem: Gowon led Nigerians out of the civil war on the side of
questions.explanation: General Yakubu Gowon's rallying cry and ultimate goal throughout the Nigerian Civil War was the preservation of a united Nigeria, encapsulated by the slogan 'To keep Nigeria one is a task that must be done.'

questions.stem: In Islamic practices, men conducted prayers while women and children
questions.explanation: In many Islamic prayer settings, men typically lead or form the main congregational rows, while women and children follow specific instructions, often praying separately or behind the men.

questions.stem: Amongst the Yoruba, the parent of a dead child is usually discouraged from seeing the ________
questions.explanation: Study Session 5 states that in Yoruba land, parents do not see the corpse of their children because children are expected to bury their parents and not the other way round. The death of children is associated with witchcraft and other forms of evil.

questions.stem: What triggered cultural nationalism within Nigerian churches?

options.A: The translation of the Bible into local languages
options.B: The discriminatory practices of white missionaries
options.D: The abolition of the slave trade

questions.explanation: The text states that cultural nationalism 'was triggered by the discriminatory practices of white missionaries in the mainstream churches.'

questions.stem: The economic status of a city goes a long way to determine its
questions.explanation: The economic status of a city directly impacts its financial health, which includes its ability to generate revenue, manage its finances, and provide services to its residents. While other factors are important, economic status is most directly tied to financial well-being.

questions.stem: Before the 1930s, one of the following was not an urban centre
questions.explanation: Abuja was developed much later as Nigeria's capital city, primarily from the 1970s onwards. Calabar, Lagos, and Enugu were all significant urban centers or colonial administrative hubs well before the 1930s.

questions.stem: What enhanced the new Pentecostal wave in Nigeria during the second half of the twentieth century?

options.B: The activities of young people in Campus Fellowships
options.C: The establishment of the Christian Association of Nigeria
options.D: The translation of the Bible into Yoruba

questions.explanation: The text states: 'A new Pentecostal wave was enhanced by the activities of young people in Campus Fellowships, some of which later became the founders of various Pentecostal ministries.'

questions.stem: What was the most important political society among the Efik?
questions.explanation: From Study Session 2, the text states: 'effective authority was exercised through membership in political societies, the most important of which was the Ekpe.'

questions.stem: Which Nigerian governor first introduced the Sharia Penal Code in 1999/2000?
questions.explanation: Ahmed Sanni Yerima of Zamfara State introduced the Sharia Penal Code in 1999.

questions.stem: Alaafin and Oyo, Mai and Kanem Borno. Based on this which of the following is correct?

options.A: Etsu and Igala, Attah and Nupe
options.B: Attah and Igala, Etsu and Nupe
options.C: Aku and Jukun, Attah and Nupe
options.D: Obi and Onitsha, Etsu and Igala

questions.explanation: In Nigeria, the ruler of the Igala people is called the Attah, and the ruler of the Nupe people is called the Etsu. The pattern shows the pairing of ruler title with ethnic group.

questions.stem: Which of the following women did not distinguish herself through selfless service to her community?

options.B: Queen Kambasa of Bonny city State

questions.explanation: Omo Naija of Lagos is not a historically recognized figure; the others are documented for their contributions.

questions.stem: What type of diet did coastal area inhabitants in pre-colonial Nigeria typically have?
questions.explanation: The text states that coastal inhabitants 'consumed mostly fish' due to their proximity to water bodies.

questions.stem: The first attempt to introduce Christianity to Southern Nigeria was undertaken by the _______
questions.explanation: Study Session 4 states that the first attempt to introduce Christianity was by Catholic Portuguese traders to the southern parts of what later became Nigeria in the late fifteenth century up till the seventeenth century.

questions.stem: The concept of “autochthones” or “stateless societies” was used by British colonial scholars to describe Nigerian communities with ___ institutions?
questions.explanation: 'Stateless societies' was a term used by British colonial anthropologists to describe communities, particularly in Eastern Nigeria, that lacked a highly centralized, monarchical, or hierarchical political structure. Instead, they had more diffused, segmentary, or non-centralized political institutions.

questions.stem: In some pre-colonial societies, which of the following had elaborate funerals?
questions.explanation: Royals (kings, chiefs) received elaborate funerals in pre-colonial societies.

questions.stem: Who was the first Muslim ruler of the Seifawa dynasty in Kanem, mentioned as beginning the real process of Islamization in the 11th century?
questions.explanation: The text states, 'The real process of Islamizaton began in the 11th century, when Kanem produced the first Muslim ruler Umme Jilme (1075-85) of the Seifawa dynasty.'

questions.stem: Among the Yoruba, what was the 'Aro' system primarily known for?

options.A: A system of individual wealth accumulation and trade.
options.B: A form of labour exchange among age-mates on a rotational basis.
options.C: A method of punishing individuals who refused to participate in community projects.
options.D: A system where slaves were employed for continuous farm work.

questions.explanation: The text describes 'Aro' as 'a form of labour exchange among age-mates. These youngsters tacitly vow to help one another on individual's farm in rotation.'

questions.stem: All of these could determine the name of a child except ________

options.A: Order of birth of a child

questions.explanation: A child's name is determined by factors like birth order, time, or place of birth, but not by the child's own choice.

questions.stem: A regime of quick and easy money in Nigeria did not encourage
questions.explanation: A culture of 'quick and easy money' often fosters laziness, corruption, and dishonest practices (deviousness) as people seek wealth without effort, thereby discouraging diligence and hard work.

questions.stem: Crude oil was struck at Otuakeme village near Oloibiri in present-day Bayelsa State in 1956, while production began in earnest in:
questions.explanation: The text states, 'Crude oil was struck at Otuakeme village near Oloibiri in present-day Bayelsa State in 1956, while production began in earnest in 1958.'

questions.stem: Which educational institution, established in Sierra Leone in 1827 and later affiliated with Durham University, became a crucial hub for intellectual activities and professional training in West Africa?

options.C: West African College of Arts and Science

questions.explanation: Page 6 mentions: "They also went a step further by establishing a higher school of their own, the Fourah Bay College that was established in 1827 and affiliated to Durham University in 1876. Fourah Bay became the hub of intellectual activities in West Africa..."

questions.stem: At the end of the Nigerian civil war, Gowon extended

options.D: The readiness to punish all offenders

questions.explanation: At the end of the Nigerian Civil War, General Yakubu Gowon famously declared 'No Victor, No Vanquished' and extended an 'olive branch' to the defeated Biafrans, emphasizing reconciliation and rehabilitation.

questions.stem: In the Yoruba marriage ceremony, during the Idana stage, various symbolic items are presented. Which of the following items are said to symbolize happiness in marriage?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'The sugar and honey symbolize happiness in marriage'. Kola is for protection, alligator pepper for many children, and palm oil for resilience.

questions.stem: What was the effect of colonialism on the notion of ethnic groups in Nigeria?

options.B: It established the notion of ethnic groups
options.C: It had no effect on ethnic identity
options.D: It created a single ethnic identity

questions.explanation: The text explicitly states that 'it was colonialism that established the notion of ethnic groups in Nigeria.'

questions.stem: Which of the following accurately describes the role of slavery in the pre-colonial Nigerian labour system?

options.A: It was a minor means of labour recruitment primarily for domestic servants.
options.B: It was an important means of labour recruitment for both domestic and agricultural activities.
options.C: Slaves were highly remunerated workers with control over their persons.
options.D: Slavery was rarely practiced and largely confined to specific, small regions.

questions.explanation: The text says, 'Apart from this arrangement, the other means of labour recruitment was slavery, and the slave trade. In fact, slavery was an important means of labour recruitment both for domestic and agricultural activities.' It further clarifies that slaves worked without remuneration and lacked control over their person.

questions.stem: In the traditional Nigerian society, those who engaged in corrupt acts were _______.
questions.explanation: Traditional Nigerian societies often relied on communal values and public accountability, where corrupt acts were met with social disapproval and public shaming as a deterrent.

questions.stem: Committing adultery was seen as ________?
questions.explanation: Adultery was considered an abomination in traditional societies.

questions.stem: Which of the following forgotten aspects of Nigerian culture may have something useful for present generation?
questions.explanation: Chastity within and outside marriage is a positive value that can still be useful today.

questions.stem: Who founded the CMS Grammar School, Bariga, Lagos, the first secondary school in Nigeria, in 1859?
questions.explanation: In the area of education, the first secondary school in Nigeria, the CMS Grammar School, Bariga, Lagos, which was established in 1859, was founded by Thomas Babington Macaulay, an Anglican clergyman who had been trained in Sierra Leone and England.

questions.stem: The process by which a child learns things about his/her culture is __________
questions.explanation: Socialization is the process through which a child learns the culture, values, and norms of their society.

questions.stem: Which state was the first to introduce the Sharia Penal Code in 1999, having a 'spiral effect' on other Northern states?
questions.explanation: The text clearly states: 'the first major and decisive step was taken in 1999, when the then Executive Governor of Zamfara State, Ahmed Sanni Yerima, introduced the Sharia Penal Code.'

questions.stem: Women could not be ordained as bishops/prophetesses in the ......
questions.explanation: The Catholic Church traditionally does not ordain women as bishops.

questions.stem: Federal control of crude oil production has deprived host communities of which of the following?

options.A: Judicious spending of the oil wealth
options.B: Abled man power for economic development
options.C: The fiscal revenue accruing from oil production
options.D: Land and water for production of goods and services

questions.explanation: The federal control of crude oil production in Nigeria has often led to the host communities being deprived of the fiscal revenue that accrues from the oil production, leading to issues like underdevelopment and environmental degradation in these areas.

questions.stem: When did Nigerians first 'wake up to a major religious revolt' initiated by the Boko Haram sect, according to the text?
questions.explanation: The document states: 'You will observe that Nigerians woke up to a major religious revolt in July 2009, when a sect known as Boko Haram went on rampage in Bauchi.'

questions.stem: During the months when agricultural ground was too dry or between harvests, people in pre-colonial agricultural societies often engaged in secondary occupations such as:

options.B: Mining gold and trading goods for items like cloth, cattle, salt, or metals.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'Among these agricultural peoples, however, the workers often sought out other occupations during the months when the ground was too dry or in the periods between harvests. Among the more common secondary occupations were mining gold and engaging in trading activities. Many agricultural peoples produced one or more food crops, which were sold to their neighbors for other items such as cloth among other items. There were also those that sold goods or traded with other non-agrarian African groups for cattle, salt, or metals.'

questions.stem: The major motive of European colonial presence in the Nigerian area was ____
questions.explanation: While other factors like religion and 'civilizing missions' were present, the overarching and primary motive for European colonialism in Nigeria and Africa generally was economic exploitation of resources and markets.

questions.stem: Urban culture includes the _______

options.A: Various practices, belief systems, social forms, etc. of city dwellers

questions.explanation: Urban culture encompasses the various practices, beliefs, and social forms of city dwellers.

questions.stem: Who was the first military Head of State in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Major General Aguiyi Ironsi was the first military Head of State in Nigeria (1966).

questions.stem: Among some groups in Nigeria, a woman who committed adultery without confessing would not be able to:
questions.explanation: In some traditional Nigerian beliefs, unconfessed adultery by a woman was believed to have spiritual consequences, including the inability to bear children or difficulties during childbirth, which could even result in death for the mother or child. Confession was often seen as a way to avert such calamities.

questions.stem: Islam was only practised in which of these regions in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Islam was practiced in northern and western Nigeria, but not exclusively in any one region only.

questions.stem: The structure of ownership of the means of production is termed:
questions.explanation: The text explicitly defines 'property relations' as the structure of ownership of the means of production, which determines the distribution of wealth.

questions.stem: What unique ritual is performed in some Edo communities involving the couple's feet and goat's blood during marriage?

options.A: They wash their feet in a river for purification.
options.B: They step on a sacred stone to symbolize unity.
options.C: They dip their big toes into the blood of a slaughtered goat at the entrance of the house for marital blessings.
options.D: The bride's feet are painted with palm oil for fertility.

questions.explanation: The document states: 'The couple would stand and hold hands at the entrance of the house with each foot on the door step. They would dip their big toes into the blood of the goat as prayers are said for their marital journey.'

questions.stem: What unique form of marriage exists among the Tiv that is not practiced among other Nigerian communities?

options.C: Bride exchange between families with grown-up daughters and sons

questions.explanation: Families with grown-up daughters and sons can exchange their daughters in marriage; a young man with a mature sister can exchange her for another girl.

questions.stem: What remarkable artistic legacy of the Benin Kingdom is mentioned in Study Session 2?
questions.explanation: From Study Session 2, the text states: 'A remarkable legacy of the Benin Kingdom is the extant corpus of art works cast in brass.'

questions.stem: What was the name of the seventh Hausa state (Hausa Bakwai) established through an earlier marriage?
