questions.explanation: From Study Session 2, the text states: 'A seventh state was Biram which was established by another son of Bayajjida through an earlier marriage to the daughter of the King of Kanem-Borno.'

questions.stem: A dependent economy is a ......
questions.explanation: A dependent economy is disarticulated, lacking internal linkages and integration.

questions.stem: Education has enabled women to

options.A: Destroy the society through various agitations
options.B: Make lasting and meaningful contributions to national development
options.C: Compete unfavourably with the men in political issues
options.D: Dominate their husbands and male folks in the family

questions.explanation: Education has enabled women to make lasting and meaningful contributions to national development.

questions.stem: How did pre-colonial Nigerian states generate revenue from commercial activities?

options.A: By imposing high taxes on all local agricultural produce.
options.B: Through a system of tax levies on goods, gifts to rulers, dues in markets, and tolls for trade across boundaries.
options.C: By owning all major trading enterprises and monopolizing profits.
options.D: Mainly by selling slaves to foreign traders.

questions.explanation: The text details: "The rulers of different kingdoms and empires pursued an intelligent policy: they levied a tax when goods were brought into or taken out of their territory. Traders had to pay twice on salt... traders not only offered gifts to rulers but paid dues in the markets, different types of levies, and tolls when they engaged in trade that transcended boundaries."

questions.stem: The functions of the Ulama included all except _______.
questions.explanation: The Ulama are scholars of Islamic law and theology whose roles typically involve guardianship, providing legal support, and interpreting religious knowledge. 'Conquest of the faithful' is not a primary function of religious scholars but rather a military or political endeavor.

questions.stem: The functions of the Ulama included all except _________
questions.explanation: The Ulama were scholars, not conquerors. Their functions included legal support, guardianship, and interpretation.

questions.stem: The Tripoli-Fezzan-Bilma trans-Saharan trade route ended in ______.
questions.explanation: The Tripoli-Fezzan-Bilma trans-Saharan trade route was one of the major arteries of trade across the Sahara, connecting North Africa to the Central Sudan, with Kanem-Borno being a significant southern terminus.

questions.stem: What was a notable characteristic of traditional education in pre-colonial Nigerian societies regarding employment?

options.A: It often led to high levels of unemployment due to limited opportunities.
options.B: It ensured individuals were equipped to fit usefully into their society, resulting in no cases of unemployment.
options.C: It focused solely on intellectual development, neglecting vocational skills.
options.D: It trained people primarily for positions of leadership and governance.

questions.explanation: The text states: "Traditional or indigenous education among people especially the Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo equipped individuals to fit usefully into their society... There were, however, no cases of unemployment."

questions.stem: Which pre-colonial element is described as 'surely one of the two dominant religions practiced in Nigeria today'?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'Islam is surely one of the two dominant religions practiced in Nigeria today' (along with Christianity).

questions.stem: ________ have fought human trafficking, child abuse and domestic violence in Nigeria.
questions.explanation: Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) have been instrumental in fighting human trafficking, child abuse, and domestic violence.

questions.stem: In which Aladura church were women ordained as clergy?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'women were ordained as clergy in the Church of the Lord, Aladura' as an example of women's empowerment within AICs.

questions.stem: Slavery was also an important __________ both for domestic and agricultural activities
questions.explanation: Study Session 11 states that slavery was an important means of labour recruitment both for domestic and agricultural activities. Slavery was a system based on forcing people to work for another person without any remuneration.

questions.stem: What distinguishes the 'old' diaspora from the 'new' diaspora in the African context, as defined in the text?

options.A: The 'old' diaspora involved voluntary migration for economic reasons, while the 'new' was involuntary.
options.B: The 'old' diaspora refers to people involuntarily shipped as slaves, while the 'new' describes voluntary post-independence migrants.
options.C: The 'old' diaspora was primarily for educational pursuits, while the 'new' was for political asylum.
options.D: The 'old' diaspora stayed within Africa, while the 'new' moved to Europe and the Americas.

questions.explanation: The text clarifies: '“Old" diaspora refers to people of African descent who were involuntarily shipped as slaves... while “new” diaspora is used to describe Africans who went voluntarily in search of the "golden fleece" in different parts of the world, especially in the post-independence period.' (Page 4)

questions.stem: Many of the Warrant Chiefs were not associated with

options.B: Freeing offenders in their courts after taking bribes
options.D: Putting their communities first before their selfish interest

questions.explanation: Warrant Chiefs, appointed by the British colonial administration, often gained notoriety for corruption, abuse of power, and self-enrichment, rather than prioritizing their communities' well-being.

questions.stem: What is the primary reason for giving names such as Ogunsanya, Sangosanya, and Oyafunke in Yoruba naming ceremonies?

options.A: To reflect the peculiar circumstances of the birth.
options.B: To honor the memory of a departed parent or family member.
options.C: To demonstrate belief in and devotion to specific gods or deities.
options.D: To express the parents' financial status at the time of birth.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'A child could also be named after the gods or deities, such as Ogunsanya, Ogunyinka, Ogunsiji, Ogunmola, Sangosanya, Sangodele, Oyafunke, Oyawale, Fashina, Fabunmi, Fawole, Oshunfunke, Oshunkoya, Oshuntokun, Eshubiyii, Eshugbayi, Orishabunmi,Orishatola, etc. Names such as these are given by adherents of the different gods or deities to demonstrate their belief in the gods.'

questions.stem: ________ exchange was common among the Tiv people.
questions.explanation: Bride exchange was a practice common among the Tiv people.

questions.stem: One effect of corruption in Nigeria is ______.
questions.explanation: Corruption significantly undermines democratic processes, with election rigging being a direct consequence. This distorts the will of the people and leads to a lack of accountability in governance.

questions.stem: Political Economy as a discipline or method of inquiry recognizes:

options.A: the gross capital expenditures as the basis for development.
options.B: the primacy of the economy and material production as the foundation of society.
options.C: the monopolization of means of production in the hand of the lower class.
options.D: the exploitation of group by another powerful group.

questions.explanation: One of the key recognitions of Political Economy as a discipline is 'the primacy of the economy and material production as the foundation of society.'

questions.stem: The leadership of Kanem-Borno before the Shehu was called the ________
questions.explanation: The rulers of Kanem-Borno before the Shehu dynasty were called the Mai.

questions.stem: The early Christian missionary activities in Nigeria had a three-pronged approach, namely:
questions.explanation: Early Christian missionaries often pursued a strategy of 'Christianization, Commerce, and Civilization.' This involved religious conversion, promoting legitimate trade (commerce), and introducing Western forms of education, governance, and social norms (civilization) alongside their evangelistic efforts.

questions.stem: The Aba Women Riot was _______
questions.explanation: The Aba Women's Riot of 1929 was crushed by British colonial forces.

questions.stem: What was the primary function of the railway system developed by the colonial administration in Nigeria?

options.A: To transport military personnel and equipment.
options.B: To facilitate the transportation of agricultural produce to ports.
options.C: To connect major industrial centers across the country.
options.D: To enable quick movement of colonial officials between cities.

questions.explanation: The section 'The Development of Transport System' begins with: 'To facilitate the transportation of agricultural produce, the colonial administration embarked on railway development.'

questions.stem: What was the royal title of the Nupe king?
questions.explanation: From Study Session 2, the text states: 'The term Etsu became the royal title' for the Nupe kingdom.

questions.stem: Corruption in Nigeria is a _______
questions.explanation: Corruption is complex and multifaceted, manifesting in various forms across different sectors.

questions.stem: The Nupe women traders during the pre-colonial period were noted for their _______.

options.A: Involvement in both local and long distance trade

questions.explanation: Nupe women were known for their significant economic activities during the pre-colonial era, actively participating in both local markets and engaging in long-distance trade networks, which contributed to their economic power and social influence.

questions.stem: What is the name for a first son among the Ibibio?
questions.explanation: Among the Ibibio, the first son is usually named Akpan, and the first daughter Adieba.

questions.stem: What caused the Amanyanabo's role to metamorphose from a ritual function to a political office among the Ijaw?

options.C: The invasion by the Benin Kingdom
options.D: The jihad of Uthman dan Fodio

questions.explanation: The text states: 'With the advent of Atlantic trade, villages or communities which succeeded in gaining greater control of commerce with the Europeans became nuclei of new states, and the Amanyanabo metamorphosed into a political official.'

questions.stem: Benjamin Nnamdi Azikiwe argued that education should ________.

options.A: Be first point of reforms in post-war reconstruction in British West Africa
options.B: Be used only in the church and religious assemblies
options.C: Be rejected in order to promote indigenous culture
options.D: Be given only to the Igbos and the Nupe

questions.explanation: The document states 'Q70. Benjamin Nnamdi Azikiwe argued that education should A. Be first point of reforms in post-war reconstruction in British West Africa ✓'. Azikiwe, a prominent nationalist and the first President of Nigeria, was a strong advocate for education as a tool for national development and liberation.

questions.stem: In the "constitutional village monarchies" of Onitsha, Oguta, Osonmari and Aboh, the ruler is known as the ______.
questions.explanation: In many Igbo communities, particularly in the areas mentioned like Onitsha, the traditional ruler is known as the Obi.

questions.stem: Besides contributing to education and missionary activities, returnees with links to Sierra Leone were also at the forefront of what struggle in the last quarter of the nineteenth century?

options.A: The abolition of the slave trade
options.B: The establishment of British colonial rule
options.D: The promotion of the Brazilian carnival

questions.explanation: The document states: "In the last quarter of the nineteenth century, as European colonial rule was established, the ex-slaves and others that had moved to other West African territories were at the forefront of the anti-colonial struggle."

questions.stem: What year did Nigeria join OPEC?
questions.explanation: Nigeria joined the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) in 1971, during the period when crude oil became the mainstay of the economy.

questions.stem: Among some groups in Nigeria, a woman who committed adultery without confessing would not _________?
questions.explanation: In some traditional Nigerian beliefs, it was thought that unconfessed adultery could lead to infertility, hence 'Be able to bear children' (or rather, unable to).

questions.stem: According to E.M. Igbo, what is the origin of culture?

options.A: Culture is God-given and divinely inspired
options.B: Culture is biologically inherited through DNA
options.C: Culture is not God-given but man-made, deliberately fashioned by society members
options.D: Culture emerges spontaneously from natural environments

questions.explanation: E.M. Igbo explicitly states that culture is 'not God-given but man-made; deliberately and fashioned out by members of a society to guide their life and living.'

questions.stem: What was the major organ of government among the Igbo, and who presided over it?

options.A: The Oyo Mesi, presided over by the Bashorun
options.B: The Amala council of elders, presided over by the head of the most senior lineage
options.C: The Ekpe society, presided over by the Obong
options.D: The Arochukwu oracle, presided over by priests

questions.explanation: The text states: 'the council of elders called Amala was the major organ of government in this area... presided over by the head of the most senior lineage in the village.'

questions.stem: The Leader of Faith Revival Ministries World Outreach in Lagos is _________
questions.explanation: Rev. (Mrs.) Nkechi Anayo-Iloputaife is the leader of Faith Revival Ministries World Outreach in Lagos.

questions.stem: The introduction of remuneration for labour (wages) in Nigeria came with which significant historical event?

options.B: The development of extensive inter-kingdom trade routes.
options.C: The coming of British colonial policies in the twentieth century.
options.D: The rise of powerful pre-colonial empires like Mali and Songhai.

questions.explanation: The text explicitly states: "The introduction of remuneration for labour came with the coming of the British colonial policies in the twentieth century."

questions.stem: The characteristics of urban culture do not include _________
questions.explanation: Study Session 13 outlines the characteristics of urban culture, which include multiculturalism, competitiveness, individualism, and diversity. 'Mutual annihilation' is not a characteristic of urban culture; rather, cities are characterized by interaction and adaptation.

questions.stem: What was the main political authority in a typical Ijaw village before European arrival?

options.B: The assembly of all adult males presided over by the Amanyanabo

questions.explanation: From Study Session 2, the text states: 'The main political authority in the village was the assembly of all adult males which was presided over by the Amanyanabo.'

questions.stem: The Islamisation of Borno reached its peak during the reign of _______.
questions.explanation: The reign of Mai Idris Alooma (c. 1571-1603) is often cited as a period of significant Islamic reform and expansion in the Kanem-Borno Empire, marking the peak of its Islamization.

questions.stem: Islam in Hausaland was aggressively promoted in the 15th century by _________
questions.explanation: According to Study Session 6, a significant milestone in the Islamization of Hausaland was achieved during the reign of Sarki Rumfa (1463-1499). He requested the famous Algerian scholar, Abdul Karim Al-Maghili, to prepare a treatise for him to facilitate his administration, which shows his aggressive promotion of the religion.

questions.stem: How does marriage among the Urhobo connect with the spirit world immediately after the traditional marriage ceremony?

options.A: The couple offers sacrifices to river spirits for fertility.
options.B: The girl's family takes her to ancestral shrines to lift her spiritually and cut any ancestral links she might have had.
options.C: The groom's family performs a ritual to bind the couple's spirits together.
options.D: A priest blesses the couple by invoking spirits of prosperity and longevity.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'After the traditional marriage has been performed, the girl's family would take her to the ancestral shrines to lift her spiritually, ask for blessings on her behalf and cut off any ancestral link she might have had.'

questions.stem: Traditionally among the Yoruba, on which day is a baby boy named?
questions.explanation: Traditionally, naming takes place on the seventh day for a baby girl and the ninth day for a baby boy among the Yoruba.

questions.stem: Nigeria has reached a situation of what regarding corruption?

options.A: The budding of the culture of corruption
options.D: The prevalence of the culture of corruption

questions.explanation: The question implies a widespread and deeply ingrained issue of corruption. The phrase 'prevalence of the culture of corruption' suggests that corruption is not merely isolated incidents but has become a systemic and accepted norm within various aspects of society.

questions.stem: A direct opposite of the Indirect Rule system of administration was:
questions.explanation: While Indirect Rule sought to govern through existing indigenous structures, the Assimilation system, primarily used by the French, aimed to integrate colonial subjects fully into the culture and administration of the colonizing power, effectively erasing their indigenous systems.

questions.stem: How did pre-colonial indigenous education provide intellectual training for boys?

options.A: They attended formal schools where they learned reading and writing.
options.B: They sat quietly beside their fathers at meetings, learning arbitration, oratory, wise sayings, and proverbs.
options.C: They were taught advanced mathematics and astronomy by village elders.
options.D: They engaged in debates with adults to sharpen their critical thinking skills.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'Intellectual training for them consisted of their sitting quietly beside their fathers at meetings and listening attentively to learn the intricacies of such tasks and skills as arbitration of cases, oratory (public speaking), wise sayings and use of proverbs.'

questions.stem: According to the text, what is the relationship between technological advancement and discrimination among cultures?

options.A: Technological differences have no effect on discrimination
options.B: More technologically advanced cultures are always more respectful of others
options.C: Differences in technological advancement have often been the basis for discrimination between cultures
options.D: Less technologically advanced cultures usually dominate more advanced ones

questions.explanation: The text states that 'the difference in the advancement of the technological component of the different cultures of the world has often been the basis for discrimination between and among cultures.'

questions.stem: Where is the original homeland of the Fulani?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'The original homeland of the Fulani is the River Senegal valley region where they were derived from miscegenation between local inhabitants and Berber immigrants.'

questions.stem: Every production system has a corresponding ______. Select one:
questions.explanation: A production system, which defines how goods and services are created and distributed, is intrinsically linked to a political system that sets the rules, regulations, and overall framework for economic activities. This relationship ensures the stability and function of the economy within a given society.

questions.stem: What key event during 1976/1977 first opened up the sectarian discourse on Sharia in Nigeria?

options.A: The emergence of the Boko Haram sect.
options.B: The deliberations of the Constitution Drafting Committee (CDC).
options.D: The introduction of the Sharia Penal Code in Zamfara State.

questions.explanation: The text explains, 'It was during the deliberations of the Constitution Drafting Committee (CDC) in 1976/1977 that the Sharia issue opened up the sectarian discourse.'

questions.stem: Which famous Algerian scholar was requested by Sarki Rumfa of Kano to prepare a treatise to facilitate his administration?
questions.explanation: The text states that Sarki Rumfa (1463-1499) 'requested the famous Algerian scholar, Abdul Karim Al-Maghilli to prepare a treatise for him to facilitate his administration.'

questions.stem: Post-Civil War National Rehabilitation Commission of Nigeria was headed by ________
questions.explanation: Mr. Ukpabi Asika was the Administrator of East Central State and head of the National Rehabilitation Commission after the Nigerian Civil War, responsible for post-war reconstruction and reconciliation in the affected areas.

questions.stem: When was the Benin Kingdom estimated to have been established, and when was its height of power?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'The [Benin] kingdom is estimated to have been established sometime in the thirteenth century and at the height of its power in the sixteenth century.'

questions.stem: How did the 'Owe' (working bee) group farming method differ from 'Aro'?

options.A: Owe involved monetary payment, while Aro did not.
options.B: Owe was practiced among age-mates, while Aro was among relatives/in-laws.
options.C: Owe involved helping a needy member without rotational reciprocation, unlike Aro.
options.D: Owe required the beneficiary to feed the benefactors, while Aro did not.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'Owe (working bee) is the last of the group farming methods. This is practiced among relatives and in-laws. The object is to come together to help a needy member. There was no rotational labour exchange. It was simply giving a helping hand. The beneficiary is not bound to reciprocate. He demonstrates his appreciation by feeding his benefactors after the day’s work.' In contrast, Aro was rotational and among age-mates.

questions.stem: When crude oil export replaced agriculture in Nigeria, the culture of corruption also _______.
questions.explanation: The sudden influx of wealth from crude oil, replacing a more diverse agricultural economy, often created new avenues and temptations for corruption, leading to its escalation.

questions.stem: In some pre-colonial societies, a chief was usually buried with which of these people?
questions.explanation: In some pre-colonial societies, chiefs were sometimes buried with slaves as part of burial rites.

questions.stem: The focus of the Aburi agreements favoured _____.
questions.explanation: The Aburi Accord, reached in Ghana in 1967, aimed to restructure Nigeria into a looser confederation of regions with greater autonomy for each region, effectively favoring a confederal system rather than a strong federal or unitary one. This was an attempt to avert the Nigerian Civil War.

questions.stem: Due to financial misappropriations, Nigeria has not experienced _______
questions.explanation: Study Session 15 explains that due to corruption and financial misappropriation, Nigeria is unable to fix its broken infrastructure, the educational sector is poorly funded, and maternal health crises persist. A major volcanic eruption is a natural disaster not related to financial misappropriation.

questions.stem: Which of these were the '3Rs Agenda' after post-Nigerian Civil War?
questions.explanation: After the Nigerian Civil War, the federal government under General Yakubu Gowon launched the '3Rs' policy, which stood for Reconciliation, Rehabilitation, and Reconstruction, aimed at national healing and rebuilding.

questions.stem: In the Hausa states during the pre-colonial period, who were most often relegated to the tending and harvesting of agricultural crops?

options.D: Women who were part of polygamous families.

questions.explanation: The text specifically mentions, 'In the Hausa states, the peoples most often relegated to the tending and harvesting of agricultural crops were captives.'

questions.stem: What was a defining characteristic of the 'Creole' culture developed by the returnees and re-captives in Sierra Leone during the nineteenth century?

options.A: Strict adherence to traditional African religions exclusively.
options.B: A complete rejection of Western education and practices.
options.C: A fusion of diverse peoples' cultures, embrace of Christian faith, and Western education.
options.D: Isolation from European trade and commerce.

questions.explanation: The returnees to Sierra Leone and the re-captives who joined them in the course of the nineteenth century developed a new and unique culture called 'Creole' which was a fusion of the cultures of the diverse peoples that came to settle in Sierra Leone. The Creoles embraced the Christian faith and Western education.

questions.stem: Under some cultural traditions, a prospective bride must undergo
questions.explanation: Female genital mutilation (FGM), often referred to as female circumcision, is a traditional practice in some cultures, including some in Africa, which a prospective bride might undergo as a rite of passage.

questions.stem: Who discovered coal in Enugu area?
questions.explanation: Study Session 13 states that Enugu was founded in 1909 when Mr. Kitson, a British mining engineer/geologist, discovered a large coal reserve in the Udi ridge while prospecting for silver.

questions.stem: In Hausaland, ________ was ruled by a Queen in the pre-Bayajidda era?
questions.explanation: According to the Bayajidda legend, Daura was ruled by a Queen before Bayajidda arrived and married her. This is a key part of the Hausa origin story.

questions.stem: Which of these cities was not directly influenced by colonial industrialisation/commercialisation efforts?
questions.explanation: Study Session 13 mentions that Sapele grew due to timber trade, Jos due to tin mining, and Port Harcourt as a port city for coal export. Oka-Akoko (in Ondo State) was not directly influenced by colonial industrialisation or commercialisation efforts to the same extent.

questions.stem: In Ngor Okpala (Igbo), what signified that an abomination had been committed?

options.A: A lion came out at night to roar in the village square
options.B: A bat cried behind a house
options.C: A goat gave birth to twins

questions.explanation: In Ngor Okpala, if a lion came out at night to roar in the village square, it signified an abomination had been committed.

questions.stem: Under some cultural traditions, a prospective bride must undergo ________
questions.explanation: Study Session 5 states that among some Nigerian communities like the Edo, Ibibio, and Efik, prospective brides undergo circumcision as part of the marriage preparation process.

questions.stem: The major religious insurgency that affected Nigeria since 2009 was caused by the activities of the
questions.explanation: The Boko Haram insurgency is a well-documented conflict that escalated in Nigeria around 2009, making it the most significant religious insurgency in the country since that time.

questions.stem: Who described the towns and cities of Nigeria as 'crucial nodes or swellings in the spatial economy'?
questions.explanation: Study Session 13 states that as Akin Mabogunje has noted, the towns and cities of Nigeria are viewed as the crucial nodes or swellings in the spatial economy.

questions.stem: The National Youth Service Corp (NYSC) was established in ________
questions.explanation: The NYSC was established in 1973 by General Yakubu Gowon.

questions.stem: Usman Dan Fodio was ethnically connected to the ________ ?
questions.explanation: Usman dan Fodio was of Fulani ethnic descent.

questions.stem: Among the Ibibio, what traditional practice is performed on the body of a child who dies, to prevent re-incarnation?

options.A: The body is mummified and buried in a special shrine.
options.C: The body is thrown into the 'evil forest'.
options.D: A special ritual is performed by the village elders to appease the spirits.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'If a child dies, the body is mutilated to prevent his re-incarnation.'

questions.stem: The Islamisation of Borno reached its peak during the reign of _______
questions.explanation: Mai Idris Alooma's reign marked the peak of Islamisation in Borno.

questions.stem: What does the text suggest is a major significance of culture in a multi-ethnic country like Nigeria?

options.A: It causes conflict between ethnic groups
options.B: It gives order, meaning and identity to existence
options.C: It eliminates all differences between groups
options.D: It only matters for political purposes

questions.explanation: The text states 'one of the major functions of culture is that it gives order, meaning and identity to our existence. This point is better appreciated in a multi-ethnic country like Nigeria,' where multiple cultural identities coexist.

questions.stem: What example does the text give of how culture differs between societies?

options.A: All societies have identical ways of transmitting beliefs
options.B: Different cultures have different and diverse ways of passing information about their beliefs and values
options.C: All cultures use the same symbols for the same things
options.D: Cultural transmission is identical in all human societies

questions.explanation: The text explicitly states 'different cultures have different and diverse ways of passing information concerning their beliefs and values from one generation to the other,' using the example of symbolic communication about taboo topics.

questions.stem: On 30th May 1967, the independence of ______ was proclaimed.
questions.explanation: On 30th May 1967, Lt-Col Odumegwu Ojukwu declared the independence of the Republic of Biafra from Nigeria. This proclamation was a direct response to rising ethnic tensions and political instability, ultimately leading to the Nigerian Civil War.

questions.stem: Most traditional laws are not ________ to widows.
questions.explanation: In many traditional Nigerian societies, customary laws and practices related to widowhood often place burdens or restrictions on widows, such as property inheritance limitations, forced remarriage, or mourning rituals that are not 'favourable' to their well-being or autonomy.

questions.stem: Muhammed Shitta Bey, a Muslim Creole, made a significant financial contribution in the 1890s towards:

options.A: Building a new school in Lagos.
options.B: Founding a bank for local traders.

questions.explanation: The document states: 'Prominent among these was Muhammed Shitta Bey, a Muslim Creole who gave a whopping 400 pounds for the building of a mosque in Lagos in the 1890s.' (Page 7)

questions.stem: Nigeria began petroleum production with the bold initiative of establishing refineries at:
questions.explanation: The text indicates that 'Nigeria began petroleum production with the bold initiative of establishing refineries at Port Harcourt, Warri and Kaduna to meet domestic needs.'

questions.stem: The detailed description of Yoruba Calabash dressers in the nineteenth century highlights their skill in:
questions.explanation: The text quotes Johnson: '“Calabash dressers are always found in a row in market places, plying their trade; all sorts of geometrical figures are traced or cut in calabashes; some designs are exquisitely beautiful.”'

questions.stem: Among the Fulani, a critical test of a woman's chastity before marriage involved:

options.A: A public confession before the village elders.
options.B: A white sheet spread on the bed on the first night of marriage.
options.C: An interview with the groom's mother about her past relationships.
options.D: A test of physical endurance similar to the sharo for men.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'On the first night of the marriage, a white sheet would be spread on the bed. If it is stained with blood, the bride and her family would be highly respected, for that implies that the lady was not defiled before marriage.'

questions.stem: According to J F Ade Ajayi, the relics of early missionary activities in Nigeria included the ________.

options.C: Huge Cross at the Redemption Camp
options.D: Huge Cross in the centre of Old Warri

questions.explanation: The First Storey Building in Badagry is a significant historical landmark associated with early missionary activities and the spread of Christianity in Nigeria, often cited by historians like J.F. Ade Ajayi.

questions.stem: In the context of political economy, what is primarily determined by 'property relations'?

options.A: The types of crops cultivated in a region.
options.B: The distribution of wealth or surplus generated in the production process.
options.C: The effectiveness of the administrative machinery.

questions.explanation: The text explicitly states that 'Property relations determine the distribution of wealth or surplus generated in the production process.' This is a direct consequence of who owns the means of production.

questions.stem: The pre-colonial Nigerian communal economic system fostered inclusive development because:

options.A: It encouraged individual accumulation of wealth for social status.
options.B: The surplus income of the rich was usually expended in benevolence to the extended family.
options.C: It strictly regulated markets and financial institutions.
options.D: People were motivated by remuneration for their labor.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'This communal system inevitably fostered inclusive development because very rarely did people accumulate wealth inordinately or try to raise their own standard of living at the expense of the larger community. This was perhaps because the surplus income or estate of the rich was usually expended in benevolence to his immediate and extended family members.'

questions.stem: In Urhobo marriage traditions, what spiritual ritual is performed by the girl's family at ancestral shrines after the traditional marriage, before she goes to her husband's house?

options.A: To seek blessings for fertility and prosperity from river spirits.
options.B: To lift her spiritually, ask for blessings, and cut off any ancestral link she might have had.
options.C: To introduce her to the communal gods of the village.
options.D: To perform a rite of passage into motherhood.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'After the traditional marriage has been performed, the girl's family would take her to the ancestral shrines to lift her spiritually, ask for blessings on her behalf and cut off any ancestral link she might have had.'

questions.stem: How did migration encourage cultural evolution in pre-colonial Nigeria?

options.A: By isolating communities from one another
options.B: By encouraging linguistic and economic interactions

questions.explanation: The text states that 'the migration of people from one place to another encouraged linguistic and economic interactions that ultimately contributed to the evolution of culture.'

questions.stem: Marriage rites and processes are ________ from one ethnic group to another.
questions.explanation: Study Session 5 emphasizes that while many Nigerian communities follow similar processes in marriage, there are differences among the various groups in terms of steps, rituals, and requirements, as detailed for the Yoruba, Akoko Edo, Igbo, Fulani, etc.

questions.stem: One of the following is not a problem associated with big cities in Nigeria _______
questions.explanation: Big cities are associated with traffic congestion, housing deficits, and waste crises, not serenity.

questions.stem: Women organizations in Nigeria have contributed to all of the following except _________
questions.explanation: Study Session 14 highlights that women's organizations contributed to the building and running of community schools, maternity homes and hospitals, motherless babies' homes, roads, and markets. Production of aircrafts is an industrial activity not typically associated with these organizations.

questions.stem: What event in 1976/1977 significantly opened up sectarian discourse regarding religion in Nigeria?

options.A: The emergence of the Boko Haram sect
options.C: Deliberations of the Constitution Drafting Committee (CDC) on the Sharia issue
options.D: The Fulani Jihad's impact on Hausa land

questions.explanation: The document specifies: 'It was during the deliberations of the Constitution Drafting Committee (CDC) in 1976/1977 that the Sharia issue opened up the sectarian discourse.'

questions.stem: One of these urban cities was not directly influenced by colonial railway lines _________
questions.explanation: Study Session 13 states that several Nigerian towns owe their existence to railway lines built by the colonial administration which led to the creation of urban nuclei such as Aba, Umuahia, Makurdi, Kaduna, and Jos. Owo in Ondo State was not directly influenced by colonial railway lines.

questions.stem: A key characteristic of a 'dependent economy,' as described in the text, is that it is:

options.A: Highly integrated with global financial markets.
options.B: A disarticulated one, lacking internal inter-sectoral interdependence.
options.D: Primarily focused on developing its domestic market.

questions.explanation: The text defines: 'A dependent economy is a disarticulated one. It lacks internal inter-sectoral interdependence and symbiosis.'

questions.stem: Among the Igbo, what is done with lepers and those who died of smallpox?

options.A: They are given a chief's burial
options.B: They are thrown into the evil forest
options.D: They are buried under their beds

questions.explanation: The text states that lepers and those who died of smallpox were thrown into the evil forest.

questions.stem: ________ is the mainstay of the Nigerian economy since the 1970s?
questions.explanation: Crude oil has been the mainstay of the Nigerian economy since the 1970s.

questions.stem: Corruption does not include ______.
questions.explanation: Corruption involves dishonest or fraudulent conduct by those in power, typically involving bribery, extortion, or abuse of public office. Equity, meaning fairness and impartiality, is the opposite of corrupt practices.

questions.stem: According to the text, when did the Sharia debate at the Constituent Assembly occur, leading to significant controversy?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'You will observe that the Sharia debate at the 1988 Constituent Assembly degenerated to a level where some distinguished members of the Assembly demanded that Sharia must be totally expunged from the Constitution.'

questions.stem: According to the text, what does 'property relations' primarily determine in a society?

options.A: The types of goods and services produced.
options.B: The distribution of wealth or surplus generated in the production process.

questions.explanation: The text defines property relations as: 'The structure of ownership of the means of production is termed property relations. Property relations determine the distribution of wealth or surplus generated in the production process.'

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes why culture is considered 'complex'?

options.A: Because it involves only written laws and regulations
options.B: Because it regulates human behaviour which is highly unpredictable
options.C: Because it is inherited through multiple generations
options.D: Because it exists only in large urban societies

questions.explanation: The text explains culture is complex 'rightly so because culture is what regulates human behaviour which is highly unpredictable.'

questions.stem: What does the text identify as the most complex part of the components of culture?
questions.explanation: The text states the sociological aspect 'is the most complex part of the components of culture' because it outlines the proper modes of action across virtually all areas of social life.

questions.stem: The pre-colonial labour system known as Aro among the Yorubas involved:

options.A: Wealthy farmers hiring laborers for continuous work.
options.B: Relatives and in-laws offering a helping hand to a needy member without reciprocation.
options.C: A form of labour exchange among age-mates on individual farms in rotation.
options.D: Youths working on their fathers' farms seasonally, accompanied by feasting.

questions.explanation: The text defines Aro as: 'It was a form of labour exchange among age-mates. These youngsters tacitly vow to help one another on individual's farm in rotation.'

questions.stem: Among the Akoko Edo, what happens if the girl's father disagrees to a marriage but the mother agrees?

options.B: The girl is sent away to another village
options.C: The mother aids in abducting the girl
options.D: The father is forced to pay a fine

questions.explanation: The text explains that if the father disagrees but the mother agrees, she will assist in abducting the girl on an agreed date.

questions.stem: What name were the Jukun referred to by in the Kano Chronicle?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'The Jukun appear only in such external sources as the Kano Chronicle where they are referred to as the Kwararafa.'

questions.stem: ________ have contributed to the untimely death of so many undergraduate students in Nigerian universities?
questions.explanation: Secret cults are widely known in Nigerian universities for their violent activities, which have led to the deaths of many students. The other options are religious or fellowship groups that do not have this reputation.

questions.stem: Which statement accurately describes the cultural interaction mentioned in the text regarding the early presence of Islam in Borno?

options.A: Interaction primarily between Hausa traders and coastal communities
options.B: Significant interaction between the Kanuri speaking people of Kanem-Borno and the Berber merchants of North Africa
options.C: Limited interaction with external cultures due to geographical isolation
options.D: Direct cultural exchange with European missionaries

questions.explanation: The text says, 'You will observe that from the beginning there has been a considerable amount of interaction between the Kanuri speaking people of Kanem-Borno and the Berber merchants of North Africa. Accordingly, the earliest indication of the presence of Islam in Nigeria was in Borno...'

questions.stem: All except one of the following are the causes of religious crises in Nigeria

options.B: Ignorance or lack of information about the religious groups

questions.explanation: Study Session 6 states that causes of religious violence include incitement, ignorance about other religions, and fanaticism. Good neighbourliness promotes peace and harmony, not religious crises.

questions.stem: Which of the following traditional implements was NOT mentioned as being used in pre-colonial agricultural systems?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'Farming activities was based on traditional homemade implements, namely: hoes, cutlasses and axes.' Ploughs are not mentioned.

questions.stem: The Aba women riot occurred in the ________ century?
questions.explanation: The Aba Women's Riot occurred in the twentieth century (1929).

questions.stem: How did women primarily coordinate family labor in pre-colonial Nigerian societies, especially within polygamous families?

options.A: They directly supervised all male farming activities.
options.B: They ensured their respective children worked passionately on the farm to earn the father's love and respect, maintaining harmony.
options.C: They managed all financial aspects of agricultural production.
options.D: They primarily focused on craft production, leaving farm labor to men.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'it was expedient for wives to mobilize their respective children to the farm to ascertain that they worked passionately for their father and earned his love and respect. In other words, family labour was coordinated mostly by the women in a way that maintained harmony and peace within the family.'

questions.stem: What skills were girls primarily expected to acquire from their mothers in pre-colonial societies?

options.C: Cooking, sweeping, weeding farms, hair weaving, body decoration, and cloth dyeing.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'Girls were often expected to stay at home to acquire the skills of cooking, sweeping, weeding the farms, hair weaving, body decoration and cloth dyeing from their mothers.'

questions.stem: In the pre-colonial times, several Nigerian communities comprised _________
questions.explanation: Study Session 13 states that before the British took over, the entire landscape comprised largely self-sufficient traditional communities engaged mainly in agriculture and commercial activities.

questions.stem: According to the text, what was the geographical location of the original town of Oyo?

options.A: In the eastern part of present-day Oyo State
options.B: In the north-western part of present-day Oyo State

questions.explanation: Though from Study Session 2, the text states that 'the original town of Oyo... was located in the north-western part of the present-day Oyo State.'

questions.stem: What was the council of state in the Oyo Kingdom called, and who headed it?

options.B: Oyo Mesi, headed by the Bashorun
options.C: Amala, headed by the eldest lineage head

questions.explanation: The text states: 'In the Oyo kingdom, the members of the council of state were called Oyo Mesi which was headed by the Bashorun.'

questions.stem: Which states are included in the Banza Bakwai (bastard states)?

options.A: Daura, Katsina, Kano, Rano, Zazzau, Gobir, Biram
options.B: Sokoto, Kebbi, Zamfara, Katsina, Kaduna, Kano, Jigawa
options.C: Zamfara, Kebbi, Gwari, Yauri, Nupe, Jukun, Oyo
options.D: Zamfara, Kebbi, Gwari, Yauri, Nupe, Jukun, Biram

questions.explanation: The text lists the Banza Bakwai as including Zamfara, Kebbi, Gwari, Yauri, Nupe, Jukun, and Oyo.

questions.stem: What is the name of the manhood test that a young Fulani man must pass to be considered old enough to marry?
questions.explanation: The document specifies: 'A young man that has reached a marriageable age must pass the manhood test called sharo.'

questions.stem: The 'old' diaspora, as defined in the context of Africa, refers to people of African descent who were:

options.A: Voluntarily sought greener pastures abroad in the post-independence period
options.B: Involuntarily shipped as slaves to Europe and the Americas
options.C: Migrated within Africa for economic opportunities
options.D: Returned to their motherland after the end of slavery

questions.explanation: Section 10.3 clarifies: '“Old" diaspora refers to people of African descent who were involuntarily shipped as slaves to Europe and the Americas from the fifteenth century to the mid-nineteenth century.'

questions.stem: Before colonisation, how did the different peoples and empires in Nigeria typically address the education of their youths?

options.A: Through formal schools established by religious missionaries.
options.B: Through organised systems of apprenticeship and training in traditional occupations.
options.C: By sending them to universities in neighbouring empires.
options.D: Education was primarily informal and unstructured, learned from daily life.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'The education of their youths was done through organised system of apprenticeship and training in the traditional occupations of farming, fishing, animal husbandry, the crafts, and trade.'

questions.stem: Fourah Bay College, established in 1827, became a hub of intellectual activities in West Africa and was affiliated with which university in 1876?
questions.explanation: The text mentions: 'Fourah Bay College that was established in 1827 and affiliated to Durham University in 1876.' (Page 6)

questions.stem: According to J.F. Ade Ajayi, which of these is considered a relic of early missionary activities in Nigeria?

options.C: Huge Cross at the Redemption Camp
options.D: Huge Cross in the centre of Old Warri

questions.explanation: The First Storey Building in Badagry is widely regarded as a significant relic of early missionary activities in Nigeria. It was built in 1845 by missionaries of the Church Missionary Society (CMS) and served as a mission house, reflecting the early impact of Christianity and Western education in the region.

questions.stem: During the Edo marriage ceremony, what unique ritual involving a goat's blood is performed for the couple's blessing?

options.A: The couple drinks the goat's blood mixed with palm wine.
options.B: The couple dips their big toes into the goat's blood while prayers are said.
options.C: The goat's blood is sprinkled over the couple's heads by the eldest man.
options.D: The couple bathes in water mixed with the goat's blood.

questions.explanation: The text describes: 'The family of the boy would slaughter a goat and the blood collected. The couple would stand and hold hands at the entrance of the house with each foot on the door step. They would dip their big toes into the blood of the goat as prayers are said for their marital journey.'

questions.stem: What is the Ibibio belief regarding the death of a child or young man, and what specific action is taken with the child's body?

options.A: It is seen as a blessing, and the body is cremated.
options.B: It is attributed to enemies or the spirit world, and the body is mutilated to prevent re-incarnation.
options.C: It is considered a natural occurrence, and the body is buried with reverence.
options.D: It signals a need for communal fasting, and the body is donated to rituals.

questions.explanation: The text explains: 'You will observe that the Ibibio believe that no child or young man dies without the involvement of either enemies or the spirit world. If a child dies, the body is mutilated to prevent his re-incarnation.'

questions.stem: In Edo marriage customs, what is the purpose of a special present called Ugbo Ogba or 'the strong foot'?

options.A: To bless the union and ensure fertility.
options.B: To persuade a girl's father or brother to allow her to go through the marriage process.
options.C: To signify the completion of the bride price payment.
options.D: To cleanse the bride of any past relationships before marriage.

questions.explanation: The text explains: 'Should she refuse to go through the marriage process, a special present called Ugbo Ogba or the strong foot would be given to her father or brother to persuade her to go through the marriage process.'

questions.stem: Which of the following ethnic groups established the Kanem-Borno state?
questions.explanation: The Kanuri people established the Kanem-Borno Empire.

questions.stem: The focus of the Aburi agreements favoured ______.
questions.explanation: The Aburi Accord, agreed upon in 1967, proposed a looser union for Nigeria, leaning towards a confederal structure where regions would have greater autonomy. This agreement ultimately failed to prevent the Nigerian Civil War.

questions.stem: The legal system encourages corruption through the following ways except when it is ____

options.D: Capable of pursuing justice and equity

questions.explanation: A legal system capable of pursuing justice and equity would actively discourage corruption, not encourage it. The other options describe scenarios where a legal system might inadvertently or directly foster corruption.

questions.stem: The death of a young person is usually ________
questions.explanation: The death of a young person is usually mourned as it is considered a tragedy.

questions.stem: What did white missionaries' close league with colonial authorities imply for nationalist movements?

options.B: The burgeoning nationalist movement could draw inspiration from the emancipatory moves of Nigerian church leaders
options.C: Nationalists rejected all forms of Christianity

questions.explanation: The text states that 'since white missionaries were in close league with colonial authorities, it then followed that the burgeoning nationalist movement could draw inspiration from the emancipatory moves of Nigerian church leaders.'

questions.stem: The 'African' or 'Native' Churches in Nigeria were led exclusively by _________
questions.explanation: Study Session 4 states that splinter groups from many mission churches established their own 'African' or 'Native' Churches to be led exclusively by Nigerians. This was in response to discriminatory practices of white missionaries.

questions.stem: Ikom is located in which state of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Ikom is a town in Cross River State, Nigeria.

questions.stem: How did individual states collect revenue from commercial activities in pre-colonial Nigeria?

options.A: By establishing state-owned monopolies on all trade.
options.B: Through voluntary donations from traders and merchants.
options.C: By levying taxes, tolls, judicial fees, fines, and death duties.
options.D: Primarily by confiscating goods from traders.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'The individual states had effective revenue collection systems... they levied a tax when goods were brought into or taken out of their territory... Such tolls were an integral part of the economic basis of power. They were a major source of revenue, together with taxation, levies, judicial fees and fines, and death duties.'

questions.stem: What role did environmental conditions play in the mode of dressing for pre-colonial Nigerian peoples?

options.B: The mode of dressing was based on environmental conditions (warm or harsh)
options.C: Dressing was identical across all regions

questions.explanation: The text states that 'the mode of dressing was based on their environmental conditions (warm or harsh)' for savannah inhabitants.

questions.stem: The founder of the royal dynasties of Benin with a link with Ife was ________?
questions.explanation: Oranmiyan, a son of Oduduwa (founder of Ife), was sent to Benin and established the Eweka dynasty.

questions.stem: One of these urban cities was not directly influenced by colonial railway lines:
questions.explanation: Owo is an ancient city in Ondo State, Nigeria. While other cities like Jos, Makurdi, and Aba were significant colonial administrative and economic centers, often developed around railway lines for resource extraction and transportation, Owo's growth and infrastructure were not primarily driven by the colonial railway network.

questions.stem: Apart from economic issues and political instability, what other 'push factor' during the colonial and post-colonial periods influenced emigration from Nigeria?

options.B: Land alienation by the colonial government

questions.explanation: Page 2 lists: "Specifically, developments such as land alienation by the colonial government, deterioration of economic conditions as evident in high rates of unemployment, political instability occasioned by military intervention in politics, the civil war as well as social tension, all constituted the 'push factor'."

questions.stem: On 30th May 1967, the independence of __________ was proclaimed.
questions.explanation: On May 30, 1967, Lieutenant Colonel Odumegwu Ojukwu proclaimed the independence of Biafra, leading to the Nigerian Civil War.

questions.stem: Among the Ibibio, a significant ritual that marks the passage from girlhood to womanhood and qualifies a lady for marriage is called:
questions.explanation: The text states: 'You will note that after the payment of the bride price, fattening begins. This marks the passage from girlhood to womanhood and qualifies the lady to marry.'

questions.stem: What is the final test of a Fulani marriage that determines respect for the bride and her family?

options.A: The ability to cook a large meal
options.B: Chastity before marriage, proved by a blood-stained white sheet on the first night
options.C: The number of cattle the groom pays
options.D: The bride's performance in the sharo test

questions.explanation: On the first night, a white sheet is spread; if stained with blood, it proves the bride was not defiled, bringing respect to her and her family.

questions.stem: In spite of regional differences, traditional education equipped individuals to __________

options.C: Fit usefully into their society workspace
options.D: Defeat the Europeans when they came to Nigeria

questions.explanation: Traditional education equipped individuals to fit usefully into their society's workspace and roles.

questions.stem: The leadership of Kanem-Borno before the Shehu was called the ________.
questions.explanation: Before the advent of the Shehu, the traditional ruler or king of the Kanem-Borno Empire was known as the 'Mai'. This title signifies their political and spiritual leadership within the kingdom.

questions.stem: One of the main features of dependency is that the colony depended on:

options.A: the external or metropolitan economy, i.e., Britain, for the purchase of its raw materials.
options.B: Disregard the rules that govern international trade.
options.C: Decide to produce what it likes.
options.D: Promotes its traditional means of exchange.

questions.explanation: The text explains, 'First, the colony depended on the external or metropolitan economy, i.e., Britain, for the purchase of its raw materials.'

questions.stem: In Yoruba land, how is the death of a non-titled man traditionally handled regarding wrappers?

options.A: He is buried with seven pieces of wrapper, but the clothes are removed at interment
options.B: He is buried with only one wrapper
options.C: He is not buried with any wrapper
options.D: The wrappers are given to the family

questions.explanation: The family presents seven pieces of wrapper for his burial; the corpse is folded with the wrapper, but at the time of interment, the clothings are removed.

questions.stem: On matters of faith, the following Christian group could be considered the most intolerant
questions.explanation: While 'intolerance' can be subjective, within the context of Christian groups listed, the question identifies The Pentecostals as potentially holding the most rigid or exclusive views on matters of faith compared to the others, often leading to a perception of intolerance by other denominations.

questions.stem: Before the 1930s, one of the following was not an urban centre:
questions.explanation: Abuja was developed much later as Nigeria's new federal capital territory, officially designated in 1976 and largely built during the 1980s. Calabar, Lagos, and Enugu were all significant urban centers with established colonial and pre-colonial histories long before the 1930s.

questions.stem: Generally, Hausaland in the pre-jihad period remained divided between _________

options.D: Muslim urban elite and the local traditionalists

questions.explanation: Hausaland was divided between the Muslim urban elite and local traditionalists (syncretic practitioners).

questions.stem: Until 1967, ________ was the mainstay of the Nigerian economy
questions.explanation: Agriculture was the mainstay of the Nigerian economy until the oil boom in the late 1960s.

questions.stem: What was the primary motive behind the British conquest and colonization of indigenous Nigerian peoples?

options.A: To establish a democratic political system.
options.B: To promote industrialization within the colony.
options.D: To improve local education and health services.

questions.explanation: The text explicitly states, 'Then, the imperial power turned its attention to the primary motive of conquest which was economic exploitation.'

questions.stem: Nigerians in Diaspora Organization (NIDO) groups contribute to Nigeria's development in which of the following ways?

options.A: Exclusively through individual remittances to family members.
options.B: By isolating themselves from government affairs.
options.C: By identifying needs in education, health, and infrastructure, providing information and resources to government.
options.D: Mainly through cultural exchanges with host countries.

questions.explanation: The text states: "The different NIDO groups have identified needs in different areas such as education, health and infrastructure development. They have assisted government at different levels with information and, in some instances, resources for some projects..."

questions.stem: One of the following is not a problem associated with big cities in Nigeria:
questions.explanation: Big cities in Nigeria, like many urban centers globally, are typically characterized by a lack of serenity due to noise, crowding, and fast-paced life. Traffic congestion, housing deficits, and waste management crises are common and well-documented problems in Nigerian big cities. Serenity is the opposite of what one would usually find.

questions.stem: Which non-agricultural occupation was described as the most widespread and engaging a large number of people in the pre-colonial period?
questions.explanation: The text states: "The cloth industry according to record appeared to be the most widespread and the one which engaged a large number of people in the production of cotton, yarns, threads and dye."

questions.stem: The 'new' diaspora's impact on homeland development includes their organization into groups known as NIDO. What does NIDO stand for?
questions.explanation: Section 10.2 and 10.3 both refer to 'Nigerians in Diaspora Organization (NIDO)'.

questions.stem: Marriages in most Nigerian communities usually start with which of these ______?
questions.explanation: While 'bride price' is crucial, the formal process of marriage often begins with an 'introduction' or 'family meeting' where the families of the prospective couple formally meet and agree to the union, preceding discussions of bride price.

questions.stem: What economic outcome did geographical variations necessarily encourage among pre-colonial Nigerian ethnic groups?
questions.explanation: The text states that geographical variations 'necessarily encouraged economic specialization and inter-dependence among ethnic groups which ultimately led to trade.'

questions.stem: Which of the following was NOT listed as a consequence of war in pre-colonial Nigeria?

options.B: Creation of new towns and villages
options.D: Enslavement of defeated peoples by their conquerors

questions.explanation: The text lists destruction of towns, forced migration, creation of new towns, enslavement, cultural absorption, and learning new ways. Industrial revolution is not mentioned as a consequence of pre-colonial warfare.

questions.stem: What does 'cultural diffusion' refer to as implied in the text?

options.A: The destruction of culture by outside forces
options.B: The spread of cultural traits from one society to another
options.C: The isolation of a culture from outside influence
options.D: The biological inheritance of cultural traits

questions.explanation: The text mentions cultural diffusion as a process alongside migration that makes static culture impossible. The example of computers 'produced in one culture but diffused into other cultures' illustrates this spread.

questions.stem: The Sokoto Caliphate was conquered by the British in ______.
questions.explanation: The British conquest of the Sokoto Caliphate culminated in 1903 with the capture of Sokoto and the eventual defeat of its forces, marking the end of its independent rule.

questions.stem: What historical significance does Kanem-Borno hold regarding Islam in the Nigeria area?

options.A: It was the last state to accept Islam
options.B: It rejected Islam until the 19th century
options.C: It was the first state to record Islamic presence
options.D: It was never influenced by Islam

questions.explanation: The text states: 'Kanem-Borno was the first state to record Islamic presence in the Nigeria area.'

questions.stem: In olden-day Igbo land, who was usually buried with a chief?
questions.explanation: The text states that in the olden days, a chief was usually buried with his slaves.

questions.stem: What was the official stance of the colonial administration and the British government regarding industrialization in Nigeria?

options.A: Neutrality, neither encouraging nor discouraging it.
options.D: Conditional encouragement for processing raw materials.

questions.explanation: The document clearly states: 'Indeed, the official attitude of the administration and its metropolitan principal, Her Majesty's Government, was outright hostility to industrialisation.'

questions.stem: The political economy of colonialism was:
questions.explanation: The text explicitly states, 'The political economy of colonialism was exploitative, through and through.'

questions.stem: What significant economic contribution have Nigerians in the 'new' diaspora made to the homeland, particularly in the past three decades?

options.A: Establishing large-scale industrial factories in their host countries.
options.B: Remitting billions of Naira home to family members for construction or business.
options.C: Investing primarily in foreign stock markets.
options.D: Developing new agricultural technologies for export.

questions.explanation: The document highlights: 'Monies sent by Nigerians in diaspora sum up to billions of Naira every year and economic analysts state that such financial stimulus has contributed to Nigeria's economic development, especially in the past three decades.' (Page 7)

questions.stem: What is the title of the Igala king?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'There are various versions regarding the origin and identity of the first Atta, the title of the Igala king.'

questions.stem: One of the aims of the Better Life Programme for Rural Women was to ________
questions.explanation: The Better Life Programme aimed to raise awareness for women's issues.

questions.stem: Before the colonization of Nigeria, the different peoples and empires had __________

options.A: Members of the ECOWAS and African Union
options.B: Been waiting for the Europeans to come and teach them how manage their economy
options.C: Already existing as Federal Republic of Nigeria
options.D: Organised the production of their own food, clothing and shelter

questions.explanation: Before colonization, Nigerian peoples organized production to meet their own subsistence needs.

questions.stem: How is the death of a hunter announced among the Yoruba?
questions.explanation: If a hunter dies, there will be gun shots to announce the death, and other hunters organize a general hunting for him.

questions.stem: Before the 19th century, what was the general socio-political status of the Muslim community in Yorubaland?
questions.explanation: The text notes, 'Although there was evidence of some Islamic presence in the area during the pre-jihad era, the socio-political status of the Muslim community was generally low.'

questions.stem: ______ is credited as the ancestor of the Hausa?
questions.explanation: According to Hausa legend, Bayajidda is a mythical figure who founded the Hausa states, making him the legendary ancestor of the Hausa people.
